News.title: We live near UK’s BIGGEST traveller site home to 800 caravans blighted by sewage & fire fears – our message to Rayner
News.content:
FURIOUS locals living in the shadow of the UK’s largest traveller site have begged Angela Rayner to not make it harder to oppose the camps.

The Housing Secretary was accused of loosening restrictions that could make it harder for residents and councils to tackle illegal sites, including traveller camps.



Critics fear the new rules could potentially see mega encampments – like this one in South Ockendon, Essex – spring up over the UK countryside.

But locals living near the sprawling Buckles Lane site say they already have serious concerns about its size, with some claiming the stench of sewage has become unbearable during the summer heat.



Others have raised fears over the risk of a major fire breaking out among the hundreds of caravans.

While some say they feel too intimidated to speak openly about the huge community behind the towering metal gates.



When The Sun visited the site – we were repeatedly beeped at and heckled by vehicles coming to and from the gates.

And when our reporter moved away into the centre of South Ockendon, we appeared to be followed by a BMW from the site which parked on the verge as the occupants glared at us working.



Locals spoke of feeling the atmosphere around the site in hostile and intimidating.

And many were unwilling to be named or pictured alongside their comments.

But not everyone in the area shares those concerns, with one young woman insisting the travellers “keep themselves to themselves”.

The Sun visited the site after a new row emerged when Rayner was accused of weaking regulations on unauthorised sites.

Tories claimed that changes to the planning rules made to speed up housebuilding, would lead to more traveller sites.



Housing chiefs strongly pushed back however – insisting the government will “crack down on illegal traveller sites” and said it is “misleading to suggest otherwise”.

Half a century ago, the council granted permission for just 50 caravans for the Gypsy, Traveller or travelling showmen communities.

Today, the site has grown dramatically and is reportedly home to more than 800 static homes and caravans, making it the largest in the UK.



Council boffins have said they have imposed a “number of injunctions” to stop the camp expanding further.

Residents we spoke to however urged the Government not to do anything that could be used to weaken protections and allow more sites like Buckles Lane.

While some on the site are travellers – others on the site are understood be poorly paid manual workers who commute into London each day after soaring rents in the capital priced them out.

And others are believed to be migrants paying peppercorn rents.

A man who has lived in the village for 57 years told The Sun: “Frankly, what goes on within those walls only they know for sure.



“I certainly don’t think it should be allowed to get bigger because essentially that group there becomes an army, which is a law to itself.

“It would be very shortsighted and naive for the government to change things to give them the edge.”

Another woman, who said she has lived nearby for 40 years, claimed the authorities themselves are scared to enter.



She told The Sun: “If Rayner’s plans go ahead to soften laws that clamp down on encampments, goodness knows what issues we will see spill into the area.”

And she said a conviction of a gun-maker earlier in the year, hammered home the need to regulate sites such as Buckles Lane.

Thomas McKenna, 60, was jailed for 16 years after running a gun-conversion workshop from a caravan there.

He was found to have been turning blank-firing weapons into lethal pistols for criminals while preparing for a so-called “race war”.

But not all locals condemned the site or the prospect of it expanding.



A woman in her 20s outside the shop at the top of Buckles Lane said: “I don’t know what people’s issues are with them [the travellers].



“As far as I am aware they are just honest hard working people who provide for their families, they get a lot of bad press.

“If you’re in the village you know they are there, so what is there you can moan about, move somewhere else if you have a problem, they keep themselves to themselves and that’s that.”

Yet concerns over the site’s size, infrastructure and safety were repeatedly raised during our visit.

One local business owner said: “I do not believe that there is anyway on earth that the site is not a serious fire hazard.”



He added: “If a fire were to start in there I think it would spread like crazy and who would be to blame for that?”

Another man, in his 50s, said: “I just don’t understand what happens with human waste.

“I have genuine health concerns about the site, is their sewage and waste being disposed of properly because the other day during the heatwave there was awful gross sewage like coming from the site.

“It is surely big enough and at capacity, the authorities will be irresponsible to allow it to get bigger as the infrastructure cannot cope.”



The concerns come as the Government moves to change England’s planning rules, with critics warning the reforms could make it easier for unauthorised traveller sites to secure permission retrospectively.

Guidance warned against environmental damage caused by unauthorised traveller sites was removed from the updated national planning policy framework – a move the Tories said would make them harder to oppose.

There has already been a 73 per cent rise in the number of unauthorised traveller caravans across England since January 2020, from 2,860 to 4,950.

Shadow Housing Secretary Sir James Cleverly said: “Communities across the country are being forced to tolerate lawbreaking from a small minority of travellers.



“But instead of siding with those who play by the rules, Labour are making it easier for travellers to set up illegal sites and get them rubber-stamped afterwards – often when they’ve already erected permanent structures.”

Though Angela Rayner hit back at Cleverly.

She said: “James Cleverly is spreading fake news designed to stir up tensions in local communities. He should be ashamed of himself. The Tories left our planning system in a mess.

“This Labour government is cracking down on illegal traveller sites and it is completely misleading to suggest otherwise.”

The Government has insisted that councils will retain the powers they need under the revised rules.



A Thurrock Council spokesperson told The Sun: “Thurrock Council has a number of injunctions in place which prevent any further expansion of areas of the Buckles Lane site. Officers take action to enforce any breaches of these injunctions.

“A review of the site is currently taking place and a council project team is working alongside partners in Essex Police, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service and utility companies to enhance the site and protect the wellbeing of those that live there.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Work to resolve issues at the site is ongoing. This is a highly complex issue and involves a great many vulnerable people who the council are working to protect.

“We are in contact with representatives of the Travelling Showpeople community living in Buckles Lane and will continue working closely with them.”

News.title: Our homes have been infested by MILLIONS of insects – street is a living carpet & neighbours have been forced to move
News.content:
A SLEEPY cul-de-sac has been invaded by millions of tiny “indestructible” insects that have driven residents out of their homes.

Local have been left at war with a seemingly endless army of tiny black beetle-like bugs carpeting their streets.



The first bugs began showing up a week ago – and within hours almost every surface including windows, doors, garden furniture and even the road itself was covered with a thick layer of bugs.

Pest controllers called in by residents said they had never seen anything like this before and were powerless to deal with such vast numbers.



Residents believe the bugs moved en masse from a farmer’s field that runs directly behind the cul-de-sac because the recent heatwave made the ground too hard to burrow into.

Resident Becky Lang, 34, who works from home, said she and wife Charlie have been unable to sleep or eat properly for over a week.



And she’s had to constantly try and remove the bugs while coping with sweltering conditions as they’ve been forced to tape up their windows.

She said: “We have had to tape up our windows and dog flap, we can’t let the dog go into the garden to go to the toilet.

“It is so stifling in the house we haven’t slept or eaten properly in a week.

“They are all in the house and I’ve had to constantly try and get rid of them but more keep coming.



“It all happened so suddenly on Thursday 13th, at around 4pm we started to notice some bugs and by 6pm there was a living carpet across the whole road.

“The council have said as they came down from agricultural land it’s not their problem, nobody has even bothered to come out and see.



“We just want a bit of support but we are getting nothing.”

Nobody is quite sure what the tiny bugs are with various pest control experts suggesting they could be Anthicidae, which are known as flower ant beetles, seed-bugs, or Birch Catkin Bugs, none of which bite but all can pose a nuisance when they swarm in vast numbers.

An 85-year-old resident told The Sun she has been forced to move out after the bugs took over her entire house. She said: “It has been horrendous, they are everywhere, they are in every room, they are even in my bed.

“If you open any windows or door they all flood in, it’s unbearable in the heat. I’ve been staying around at my daughter’s at night.

“You can’t sit outside because in a few seconds they are all over you, it’s uncomfortable and they stink too.



“I called out a pest control company and they have never seen anything like this before

“It’s been horrible and so upsetting, when they first arrived every surface was just moving.“

Nigel Pugh, 59, said: “It’s been absolutely horrible.

“We’ve contacted the local council and our MP but nobody has even bothered to come down here.

“They just say they’re not dangerous so they don’t want to know.



“We were told they just can’t get into the ground and that is why they came over.”

When The Sun visited the street this week – seven days after the first bugs arrived – millions of bugs still remained although locals said the numbers had already dropped sharply following recent rains and colder temperatures.

But every householder we spoke to told how their lives had been disrupted by the resilient bugs – which measure less than 1mm across.

Residents have tried numerous ways to get rid of them, one house has piled mounds of salt, lemons and limes at every door and window to try and deter the bugs, others have used bleach, cleaning sprays or boiling water but whatever they try the vast numbers mean more keep coming back.

David Buckingham, 88, a retired chartered surveyor has lived on the street for 56 years says he has never seen the bugs before.



He said: “We were away last week and when we came back on Monday we couldn’t believe what we saw.

“If the window is open they crawl into the house – the only thing we have found to kill them is spraying Dettol directly on them, if it’s just on a surface it doesn’t bother them.

“There are far less than there were initially but nobody has seen anything like this anywhere before. In 1976 we had a swarm of ladybirds but this is worse.

“They seem to be attracted to light colours so they are around our windows so we are washing them more or less every day.”

Aislinn Read, 32, said: “It’s just because it’s been so hot but they are everywhere.



“We can’t open our windows or doors even for a few seconds without them getting in, they are really annoying.

“Some people have had eight inch-thick clumps of them where you can’t see anything else.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We can’t put the washing out but they do seem to be eating some of the weeds which is helpful.”

Plymouth City Council has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Putin planning to mobilise 300,000 troops in weeks, Zelensky warns as Moscow pulls ambassador out of Britain
News.content:
VLADIMIR Putin is set to mobilise 300,000 troops in weeks, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has warned.

It comes as Russia pulled its ambassador out of Britain and rewarded the Kremlin crony with a prestigious post in Moscow.



Ukraine believes Mad Vlad is planning to mobilise an extra 300,000 troops for his invasion of Ukraine after Russian parliamentary elections in September.

Zelensky warned that Russia could draft hundreds of thousands more next year as its deranged dictator attempts to capture the rest of Ukraine’s Donetsk region.





The ageing tyrant is aiming to bolster his flailing forces by half a million extra recruits in total in 2027, he said.

The Ukrainian president said the recruitment drive was likely to target Russia’s far-flung regions.

Zelensky said Russia is losing losing a “maximum” amount of troops, adding that mobilisation “will not take place in the central cities”.

He added: “But I don’t think they will be able to hide it very well.”



Russian ambassador to the UK Andrei Kelin, 69, was in the job for seven years since his appointment in 2019.

He quietly left the role on July 21 and the Kremlin has not replaced him, signalling a serious breakdown in diplomatic relations between Moscow and London.



On Monday, Russia warned of “consequences” after Britain backed Ukraine’s drone attacks last week.

The UK has supplied drones used by Zelensky’s forces for devastating attacks on Russia.

No candidates have been put forward to replace Kelin as Russia tries to force the UK to reconsider its support for Ukraine.

Embassy staff have no idea if or when a successor could be put in place, according to The Times.



A Russian embassy spokesman claimed Kelin had made “considerable efforts to preserve contacts and channels of communication” with Britain.

He accused the government of opting for “path of confrontation” with the Kremlin.

The spokesman added: “He left Britain in the hope that a more constructive and respectful dialogue could eventually be restored, should the UK reconsider its policies towards our country.

“In the meantime, the embassy is headed by the chargé d’affaires.”

Kelin is now tipped for a job overseeing Russia’s Mordovia region, notorious for its gulags.



The ambassador promoted pro-Kremlin propaganda during his time in London, including recently denying reports that dart frog poison had been used to take out Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Last year he denied official conclusions that Putin “must have” authorised the use of a nerve agent Novichok in the 2018 Salisbury poisonings that killed Dawn Sturgess and almost killed former Russian spy Sergei Skripal and his daughter.

News.title: Inside Ukraine’s eerie ‘drone tunnel’ where ‘human safari’ slaughter is so intense that kids learn how to save parents
News.content:
A HAUNTING “drone tunnel” littered with burned-out cars is a grim daily reminder of the brutality of war for Ukrainians.

Vladimir Putin‘s killer drones have been known to target civilians rushing across a long stretch of road where speed limits no longer matter due to the fear of a deadly attack.



The so-called tunnel over the M14 highway between Kherson and Mykolaiv is easily recognisable by the stench of burning rubber and the sight of mangled metal.

Dozens of anti-drone nets also sit above the road in an attempt to fend off the daily strikes by Kremlin forces.



Still, Putin’s men are regularly able to smash through the mesh in pursuit of civilian victims in Kherson.

Andreas Tölke, head of German humanitarian organisation Be an Angel, called the drone tunnel “a journey between life and death”.



He said: “Along the roadside, you see burnt-out cars and private vehicles.

“Everyone here is a target. The same picture can be seen throughout the city. If you do not get to safety quickly enough, you die.”

The drive into Kherson begins long before the city comes into view.

The last military checkpoint has been pushed away from the city as Russian drones extend their reach.



Once through the checkpoint, drivers accelerate into what locals have now dubbed the “drone tunnel”.

They then have seconds to speed through and escape the waiting drones who can quickly latch onto their positions and hunt down cars with terrifying ease.

Burned-out cars and vehicles riddled with shrapnel can be seen left on the roadside, silent evidence of attacks that have become part of everyday life.

It comes amid reports of Russian FPV drones regularly attacking civilians across the city in what residents refer to as “human safari” attacks.



Are Russian civilians paying drone pilots to carry out sick ‘human safari’ attacks? TWISTED Russian civilians have been accused of paying for sick “human safari” hunting missions targeting defenceless Ukrainians on the streets. Drone pilots working within the Russian army are “wilfully targeting civilians for monetary gain” under Vladimir Putin‘s evil rule, a former Nato analyst told The Sun. Dr Patrick Bury, a warfare and counter-terrorism expert and former Nato analyst, says the brutality highlights how Putin has created a regime which is “completely rotten to the core”. He told The Sun: “[Russia is] going in and they’re basically intentionally targeting civilians. “It’s become known as the Kherson safari, essentially civilian hunting missions. Read more here.

Drone operators are accused of deliberately targeting people, cars, and public transport.

Some sick Russian civilians are even facing shocking claims they pay soldiers to carry out the drone attacks and catch it all on camera.

According to locals, FPV drone pilots even attack people in their homes, by flying in through the windows.

Sunny Kherson, home to the sweetest watermelons, was once known for its loving community, flooded with smiling people on the streets.



Now it has turned into a real-life dystopian, apocalyptic town.

Andreas Tölke added: “Each visit over the past three years has revealed another deterioration in the city’s well-being.

“Every time I return, the situation gets worse.



“The attacks have become so widespread that Ukrainians refer to them as ‘Human Safari.’

“Videos of these strikes are regularly published on Russian Telegram channels, turning the killing of civilians into propaganda and entertainment.

“Every day, people are injured or killed.”

The situation had become so bad that now children in Kherson are being taught how to stop severe bleeding, apply tourniquets, and keep an injured person alive until medics can arrive on the scene.

In a dangerous city where ambulances can’t always reach victims immediately, volunteers say a child may need to become the first responder if a parent is badly wounded.



Schools in Kherson remain shut due to the dangers of war.

Kids instead gather in underground bomb shelters that serve as a community centre, classroom, and meeting place for locals.

Many children spend much of their day inside these protective bubbles as their loved ones continue to work or fight on the frontlines.



Mark Friedrich, a critical care paramedic and founder of the Ambulance for Kids NGO who helps in these shelters, is now teaching life-saving medical lessons to these children.

He said: “My intention is to protect the children. We used artificial blood to simulate realistic injuries and allow children to practice under conditions that resembled real emergencies.

“We taught the kids how to apply a tourniquet, treat deep wounds, use chest seals, and control life-threatening bleeding.

“One of the learning scenarios was: ‘What should you do if your mother is injured during a drone attack?’

“Stop the bleeding, apply a tourniquet if necessary, and keep her alive until professional medical help arrives.”



Volunteer Roman Poliychuk coordinated the training together with Friedrich.

He continued: “The children ranged from seven-year-olds to older teenagers.

“One seven-year-old boy, whose father serves in the Ukrainian military, already understood many of the safety procedures because his mother regularly discussed emergency situations with him.”



The two vital workers say that they often overhear the children speaking out the terrifying reality of living in a war zone.

Friedrich and Poliychuk have evacuated more than 100 families from frontline regions since the war erupted in 2022.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They help transport families and critically ill children in specialised ambulances to hospitals in Ukraine or take them safely across into Europe.

Tölke’s Be an Angel group have also helped evacuate around 24,000 people from frontline regions since the start of the full-scale invasion.

News.title: Two siblings are found brutally ‘murdered’ in lonely farmhouse… are they the REAL first victims of Bullseye Killer?
News.content:
WHEN rookie postman Nigel Rossiter peered through the window of the lonely farmhouse, he was horrified to be confronted by the charred remains of an elderly man lying in the kitchen.

The 19-year-old had stumbled upon the body of Griff Thomas, with his younger sister Martha later discovered dead at the scene by police. The case has remained unsolved for 50 years – but The Sun can now reveal why relatives believe they have proof they were the first victims of the notorious “Bullseye Killer”, John Cooper.





It’s been a long battle for justice. When Martha, 70, and Griff Thomas, 73, were found dead at their farm in Llangolman, Pembrokeshire, west Wales, in December 1976, it was initially treated as a double murder.

However, police decided weeks later that Griff killed his younger sister, Martha by hitting her over the head with a chair before making a fire and throwing himself on top of it.

That conclusion was not accepted by their grieving family and locals who were certain the quiet, elderly, chapel-going siblings were both murdered.

Now, the siblings’ second cousin, Huw Gibby, has exclusively spoken to The Sun about how they believe the convicted killer was to blame – and he demands cops finally listen.

He has revealed the family believe Cooper was working for the elderly pair on their farm at the time.

Cooper – dubbed “The Bullseye Killer” due to an appearance on the darts-based TV gameshow – was jailed in 2011 for four murders, two sex attacks and 30 burglaries.

The family are begging Dyfed Powys Police to formally investigate Cooper over their deaths 50 years ago.

Cooper, then aged 31 and living in nearby Milford Haven, is understood to have worked repairing farm fences for the siblings.





And he would have known they never locked their front door and kept cash in their home to pay farmworkers.

An inquest into their deaths the following year found Martha was unlawfully killed, and an open verdict was returned in the case of Griff.

Until now, it has been thought Cooper’s first murder victims were Richard and Helen Thomas, who he blasted to death with a shotgun at their farmhouse home in Scoveston Park.

It was just a couple of miles from where he lived in on the Pembrokeshire coast, a few days before Christmas in December 1985.

After killing the couple, he set their home on fire – just as Griff’s remains were also torched.

Then, in June 1989, he murdered Peter and Gwenda Dixon, from Oxfordshire, again with a shotgun at close range, as they walked the coastal path near Little Haven in Pembrokeshire.

They had been camping nearby at Howelston Caravan Park, and were preparing to return home when they were killed.

All were killed with a double-barrelled shotgun.



And in March 1996, Cooper, wearing a balaclava and again wielding a shotgun, terrorised five teenagers at the Mount Estate in Milford Haven, raping one, a 16-year-old girl, at knifepoint and indecently assaulting a 15-year-old girl.

Cooper was eventually found guilty of the offences following a cold case review set up by Dyfed Powys Police in 2006 called Operation Ottawa.

Cooper’s infamous appearance on the television gameshow Bullseye a month before he killed the Dixons was used as crucial evidence to match him to witness descriptions.

Mr Gibby claims he aired his suspicions that Cooper was the killer during a recent meeting with Dyfed-Powys cops amid a fresh review of the investigation into the deaths.

But he claims a detective working on the four-year probe slapped him down, saying: “Don’t you dare mention his name.”

Mr Gibby told The Sun: “He was furious with me for suggesting what seems to me to be a very logical and reasonable line of inquiry for this review.

“He told me that any suggestion that Cooper was involved could jeopardise their new investigation.

“But we were in a private meeting and I found his tone and the words he used extremely insensitive and patronising.



“I also gave him 12 reasons why I was certain that my relatives had been murdered and had not died in the way the original investigation concluded.

“My only motive is to clear Griff‘s name. There is no way on earth that Griff would have killed Patti (the family’s name for Martha).”

Those 12 reasons include the fact that Griff, a man who suffered from frailty beyond his years and was crippled by a disease that left him unable to grip objects with his hands, had supposedly lifted a heavy wooden chair and used it to beat his sister to death.

Mr Gibby says that locals he has spoken to had never known the siblings to fall out, let alone harm one another physically.

Who is 'Bullseye Killer' John Cooper? WELSH serial killer John William Cooper was given four life sentences for a series of grisly murders in Pembrokeshire in the 1980s. Cooper, a diagnosed psychopath, was eventually convicted in 2011 for the double murders of Richard and Helen Thomas, and Peter and Gwenda Dixon, following a cold-case review that started in 2005. Who is John Cooper and where is he now? John Cooper, 76, is a serial killer with a long history of crimes which include 30 robberies and violent assault. He was sentenced to 14 years in 1998 for burglary and robbery but was released in 2009. Through a cold case review, he was arrested and convicted of two double murders dating back to the 1980s. Cooper, who unsuccessfully tried to appeal his convictions in September 2011, is still behind bars in an undisclosed prison. When did Cooper murder four people in Pembrokeshire? Cooper was referred to as the Bullseye Killer because he appeared on the popular game show four years after killing two siblings in Scoveston Park. He murdered brother and sister Richard and Helen Thomas then burned down their house on December 22, 1985. On 28 May 1989, Cooper participated in a recording of the ITV game show Bullseye. Just one month later, he robbed Peter Dixon of £300 and shot him and his wife Gwenda in the face at point blank range. The murders became known as the Pembrokeshire murders. How long was the investigation into the deaths? Cooper infamously evaded justice for around two decades but was finally convicted using the most advanced forensic techniques of the time. On May 26, 2011, Cooper was given a whole life order for the 1985 double murder of siblings Richard and Helen Thomas, and the 1989 double murder of Peter and Gwenda Dixon, following an eight-week trial. His first prison sentence allowed cops to collect further evidence against him to convict.

He said: “It is preposterous to think that Griff would hurt anybody, let alone his beloved sister, who he doted on.

“He would not have had the strength to have lifted that chair in any case. It was a very heavy, solid oak kitchen chair.

“And why on earth would someone kill themselves in the way they said he did?

“They said he lit a bed of fire using newspapers and clothing, then threw himself upon it. Who would choose to die like that? It is plain ridiculous.



“I have a copy of a photograph of the murder scene and there is a pool of his own blood by his head. Why would that be there if he had set himself alight?

“I believe the pair of them were killed by a third party, most likely John Cooper.

“I believe that third party first killed Patti while Griff was buying groceries at a shop down the road, then when Griff returned he too was murdered.

“They never locked their front door and everyone in the area knew they kept large sums of cash in the house to pay people who worked at the farm for them.

“Cooper is known to have worked on farms in the area, repairing fences, including my family’s farm.”

Mr Gibby, 79, a retired government charted surveyor who later worked with Dyfed-Powys Police handling 999 calls at the force’s headquarters in Carmarthen, has engaged the services of a barrister to push for a thorough reinvestigation of the deaths and a new inquest.

“I will never give up fighting for justice for Patti and Griff,” he said.

He added: “I have lost patience and faith in this review, so I have engaged the services of my own forensics expert and a fire specialist to conduct an investigation independently.



“And meanwhile we are going through the Attorney General to push for a fresh inquest into their deaths.”

Cooper had been convicted in 1998 of 31 offences of burglary and robbery and sentenced to 16 years as a result of a police investigation known as Operation Huntsman.

During the course of that probe, police began to suspect he may be linked to the two then-unsolved double murders in Pembrokeshire and there were evidential links between exhibits gathered during the Huntsman investigation and the two double murders.

New forensic tests on exhibits gathered during the Huntsman investigation pointed to Cooper as the double shotgun killer and sex attacker.



Traces of blood shown to be Peter Dixon’s were found on a shotgun owned by Cooper, thrown into a hedge after a failed armed robbery in November 1996.

Traces of Mr Dixon’s blood were also discovered on a pair of shorts worn by Cooper, found in his house.

During the trial, he was depicted as an outdoorsman who used hedgerows as “safes” to hide the valuables he stole and to discard items.

He also cut escape routes through fences and fields to evade police.

Significant fibre evidence also linked Cooper to the two double murders and other offences.

There were also strong textile-fibre links with the two girls who had been sexually assaulted in Milford Haven.

These included fibres found on the inside of the girls’ clothing that could have come from a pair of gloves discovered in a hedgerow discarded during a robbery and other fibres transferred in the reverse direction, from the clothing to the gloves.

Cooper’s home had been thoroughly searched as part of the investigations into the burglaries and the robbery, and a number of items were removed from both inside and outside his home.

Other items, including jewellery and gloves, had been recovered from hedgerows in the local area.

In December 1976, following the discovery of the Thomas siblings’ bodies, Dyfed-Powys Police launched the double murder investigation and set up an incident room in the heart of the village.



The case was led by a celebrated detective who had solved the Cannock Chase murders in Staffordshire, one of the biggest manhunts in British criminal history, Det Ch Supt Pat Molloy.

More than 1,200 people were spoken to, with police officers knocking on doors over a five-mile radius.

Over the coming weeks, 572 men provided alibis to police that ruled them out of the investigation, but no leads emerged.

By late January 1977, the detective concluded that Griff had “probably” killed his sister.

Dyfed-Powys Police told The Sun: “We can confirm that a significant amount of complex work has been undertaken as part of the forensic review process, and the family of Griff and Martha Thomas have been updated of the progress made so far.”

They continued: “To ensure all available material was obtained, several detailed searches have been conducted by the force in line with an overarching forensic strategy.

“Search locations included police stations in Pembrokeshire, our scientific support unit archive at Police Headquarters in Carmarthen, The National Archive of Wales, Aberystwyth, and the Forensic Science Service Archive, in Birmingham.”

The searches have retrieved Martha’s handwritten diaries, original investigation documents, fingerprint lifts from photographs, postmortem moulds of the siblings’ hands, and a tapestry.

They added: “The family has been updated on the findings from these enquiries, and the limitations faced in reviewing an incident that took place 50 years ago.

“We are now at a stage where communication has begun with HM Coroner to keep them informed of the latest position, and to seek advice and guidance on how we proceed.



“We will continue to keep the family of Griff and Martha updated on the review, along with any recommendations from HM Coroner.”

News.title: Brits’ biggest dating icks revealed as singletons admit avoiding people with dandruff and food in teeth
News.content:
FLAKING OUT Brits’ biggest dating icks revealed as singletons admit avoiding people with dandruff and food in teeth

A POLL of 2,000 adults revealed the most annoying beauty issues, with plucking nose or ear hairs and overgrown leg hair among the top concerns.

It emerged 36 per cent of all adults were guilty of carrying out beauty habits that they consider to be an ick, with Gen Z the biggest culprits.



But while those polled claim to feel most ‘put together’ with freshly washed hair, perfume and a moisturised body, one in 10 don’t like the feeling of their body immediately after applying the lotion.

A spokesperson for Nivea which commissioned the research to mark the launch of its new body serum range, said: “The research shows there’s no shortage of complaints when it comes to self-care.



“We all want to look and feel our best, but there are some beauty habits which can be seen as more annoying or undesirable than others.

“There is nothing more annoying than showering and moisturising in the morning, only for it to still be greasy or sticky when you then want to get dressed.

TOP 20 BEAUTY ICKS Deodorant leaving white marks on clothes Picking food out of teeth Dry/flaky scalp Overgrown leg hair Plucking nose/ear hairs Touching sticky nail varnish too early Make up sweating off Chipping nail varnish Moisturiser which takes ages to soak in or dry Unblended foundation Sweaty upper lip Mascara on eyelids Running out of product unexpectedly Poking yourself in the eye with mascara Dry shampoo visible in your hair Patchy fake tan Lipstick smudging Plucking eyebrows Uneven/patchy beard hair Filing feet with a pumice

“It can be especially challenging in the summer months with the heat to contend with, and there’s nothing worse than feeling sticky or uncomfortable, which is why the right products are so valuable to make your routine as easy as possible.”

The study also found 41 per cent of those who have committed one of their own beauty icks did so as they think it will benefit their skin long term, while 38 per cent admitted it was simply a habit.

With the hot weather revealed as the most common trigger for a frustrating beauty moment among a third of those polled via OnePoll.



It also emerged that when it comes to beauty body care routines, 48 per cent take more time over them before a special occasion, while 27 per cent said the same of the summer months.

But the morning non-negotiable beauty routine includes tooth brushing (61 per cent), showering (40 per cent) and applying lotion to their faces (34 per cent).

On the flipside, 15 per cent claim they’ve gone back to their house after leaving once realising they forgot to spray perfume, while 11 per cent have returned after forgetting to moisturise themselves.

But moisturising was also the most likely activity to be skipped due to lack of time to get ready. But in contrast, 25 per cent said they feel more ‘put together’ when they apply lotion to their body.

With 37 per cent seeking a hydrating, quick absorbing (36 per cent) and smooth (32 per cent) feeling on their skin.



Overall, 35 per cent feel more confident when they’ve carried out their full body care routine.

A spokesperson for Nivea added: “The survey findings show the impact when it comes to self-care and finding the right moisturiser.

“Being equipped with the right tools can build on someone’s confidence, when products are tailored to our different skin types and solve any ongoing irritations, they can be the difference between a good day and a bad day.

“Having a routine can be a mindful practice but it can also be empowering and help build a sense of reassurance as you’re about to head out the door.”

News.title: Moment fox sneaks into home and bites sleeping 3-month-old baby – leaving tot with ‘four bloody puncture wounds’ to head
News.content:
THIS is the moment a fox is seen prowling around a garden before sneaking into a three-month-old baby’s room and biting her.

Footage shows the critter curiously sniffing around inside the house before coming across little Josephine.



Carly Clarkson had dozed off while feeding Josephine only to be woken with a start by the animal sniffing her face – before noticing blood around her baby lying beside her.

Mum-of-two Carly, 37, screamed and then realised the four bloody puncture wounds on her baby’s head.



She snatched up Josephine and chased the fox to the top of the stairs, before darting to her one-year-old daughter’s room to check she was alright.

Carly, who had left the back door to their home in Watford open, said: “Imagine waking up and your child’s blood is next to you. It was absolutely horrifying.”



She said the four puncture wounds on Josephine’s head “looked like a dog had bitten a football“.

She rushed to Watford General Hospital at around 9.45pm on Thursday where it was confirmed there were no fractures to Josephine’s skull or concerns around the baby’s brain.



Carly says it may only have been due to the position they had fallen asleep in that the wounds were not to the face or an artery in the leg.

She suggested the fox may have been trying to pull her daughter away with it.

Now, Carly has been left scared to use her garden or leave doors open with her daughters around.



She added: “I feel absolutely violated, I don’t feel safe in my home with two young children.

“Clearly there is an issue of either the same fox or multiple foxes being fed or just really acclimatising and becoming comfortable with people.”

Even as they left to take their daughter to hospital, Carly and her husband saw a fox – which may have been the same animal – coming right up to them at the front door and seemingly trying to get in.

CCTV from the garden shows what they believe to be the animal wandering around moments before its entrance.

They reported what happened to Watford Borough Council and investigated what they could arrange privately, but all that could be offered were £300 pellets which may deter foxes.



Carly claims the brazen foxes in the area are becoming “out of control”, and has been in touch with The Fox Project for help.

She said: “I was very lucky that we came away with just needing some tetanus shots and some antibiotics.

“I would hate to find out that in a week or in a few weeks time someone else isn’t so lucky.”

Trevor Williams, founder of The Fox Project, says that incidents like this are extremely rare and there hasn’t been one in over a decade.

He said: “It’s pretty clear to me that this incident involves a young cub.



“Experienced adult foxes would never behave in this way and will always avoid putting themselves in such a vulnerable position.

“We’re at the point of the year when annual dispersal is taking place and this year’s fox families are breaking up – cubs being around four and a half months.

“For most, their natural instincts kick in quickly, and they will avoid immediate human proximity.

“But there will always be a few who find themselves wandering through open doors into homes or businesses as they investigate unfamiliar territory.

“If undisturbed, as this particular cub appears to have been, their natural curiosity will oblige them to check out everything at leisure and, in this case, it looks as if it’s tested out its sharp young canines on the tender skin of a baby.



“As alarming as this must have been for the baby’s mother and, thankfully, resulting in only superficial injury, incidents involving foxes are so rare that the last time we heard of anything similar was somewhere around 2010 / 2012.”

The charity founder has said to protect yourself it is advised to keep doors closed and use non-toxic repellents.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “Obviously, taking care to keep doors closed, despite the extreme weather, is a basic precaution.

“But anyone concerned about foxes regularly sharing their environment can reduce activity and discourage them very easily by use of safe, non-toxic mammal repellents easily acquired from garden centres and hardware stores.”

News.title: State of emergency declared as huge 10,500-acre wildfire explodes in Nevada sparking urgent evacuation warnings
News.content:
A STATE of emergency has been declared as a huge 10,500-acre blaze is tearing through Nevada’s desert.

The enormous wildfire exploded near Reno, on the state‘s border with California, sparking urgent evacuation warnings.



Whipped up by powerful winds, the fire has quadrupled in size in mere hours and is spreading rapidly.

The fast-moving fire erupted on a hillside in Northern Nevada outside Reno on Saturday, around 30 to 40 miles north of the Lake Tahoe area.



It is now threatening to engulf around a thousand homes, Washoe County Sheriff’s Office said.

Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo wrote in a statement that the blaze was “spreading quickly and threatening homes and structures”.

He declared a state of emergency for Washoe County.

Firefighters and emergency crews are battling the blaze.



Truckee Meadows Fire Chief Richard Edwards called the huge wildfire “a very dynamic incident” and urged residents to follow evacuation orders.

He said in a video: “The wind-driven fires move very rapidly into our residential areas, creating a lot of challenges for our firefighters to save homes and protect lives.”



Sierra County Sheriff’s Office told residents in the Verdi and Long Valley areas along the California-Nevada border to be prepared to evacuate as the fire ravages the arid landscape.

In Nevada, “Go now” evacuations have already been ordered near Verdi and Somersett.

The fire is heading northeast, tearing towards the county’s detention centre.

Powerful winds and low humidity also fuelled the flames to rip south and east, expanding the danger zone and completely consuming the entire area around Peavine Peak and the back of the mountain.



Mandatory evacuations have been ordered from Raleigh Heights north to Red Rock on the west side of US 395.

“Get Set” warnings – telling people to prepare to evacuate – have been given for more than 1,000 threatened homes in North Virginia Street, Hoge Road, Golden Valley, Lemmon Valley and Stead.

Thousands of homes were left without power and a highway was partially shut, as a hospital emergency room north of Reno was shut due to evacuations.

Reno Mayor Hillary Shieve said: “My heart goes out to anyone in our community who has been impacted by the dangerous and fast-moving Hawk Fire.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our firefighters and first responders are heroically fighting the fire and the high winds to save lives, homes, businesses, livestock and pets.”



Authorities instructed residents to refer to the perimeter map for up-to-date evacuation information.

News.title: UK weather maps show 20 counties face heavy rain during 'Spanish plume' – list
News.content:
UK weather maps show 20 counties face heavy rain during 'Spanish plume' – list

Weather forecasters say a 'Spanish plume' could develop next week and bring thunderstorms to the UK, with data suggesting some 20 counties face heavy rain

View 2 Images England and Wales will see the most rain this week (map shows total rainfall up until 6pm on Friday) (Image: WXCHARTS)

Heavy rain and widespread thunderstorms are on the cards this coming week.

‌



The UKMO weather model suggests some parts of the country could see around 90mm of rain in total from now until Friday, a welcome relief following record dry spells and the declaration of drought status across parts of England and Wales.

‌



Areas in the east of England should see the most rain through the week, although the data suggests there will also be significant downpours in North Wales, the north-west, the Midlands and parts of the south-east.

‌



In total, the data suggests some 20 counties might see 40mm of rain up until Friday. They are all in England and Wales.

View 2 Images Total rainfall up until 6pm on Friday (Image: WXCHARTS)

Met Office forecasts thunderstorms on Tuesday as BBC names areas facing heavy rain READ MORE :

UK counties facing heavy rain next week

Yorkshire

Lincolnshire

Nottinghamshire

Derbyshire

Leicestershire

Cheshire

Shropshire

Staffordshire

Warwickshire

Northamptonshire

Cambridgeshire

Norfolk

Suffolk

Essex

Sussex

Oxfordshire

Bedfordshire

Flintshire

Denbighshire

Caernarfonshire

‌



‘Spanish plume’ heading to UK

BBC Weather forecasters have said a “Spanish plume type of system” could bring “thundery outbreaks” across the UK next week.

A Spanish plume is a meteorological term which refers to when warm air moving northward from Spain rises and cools, leading to the formation of thunder clouds.

The Met Office explains: “As cooler air spreads from the west, instability increases and the very warm air rises through the cooler air, enhancing the formation of thunderstorms.

Article continues below

“The very warm air from Spain forms a layer at height and acts as a lid, initially preventing warm air rising from the surface. However, as the air at the surface increases in temperature eventually it warms enough to break through this barrier and air can then rise from the surface up to the higher parts of the troposphere.

“This air is very unstable and the dramatic release of energy that occurs results in the formation of cumulonimbus clouds, lightning, thunder, hail, downpours of rain and sometimes gusty winds.”

The mercury is expected to reach 25C in southern areas on Monday and 22C in northern areas, before climbing to 26C in the south on Tuesday, followed by 28C on Wednesday. Conditions will then cool off as we head towards the weekend, forecasters say.

News.title: Parents are fretting about the end of the summer holidays as back to school season looms
News.content:
Parents are fretting about the end of the summer holidays as back to school season looms

Most parents are just as anxious as their children about going back to school after the end of the summer holidays - and are concerned their kids may not be suited to the current school system

View 2 Images Parents are worried about the return to school, a survey shows (Image: Getty Images)

Almost two thirds of parents feel anxious about their child going back to school after the summer holidays, researchers found.

‌



Some 59 per cent of surveyed mums and dads reported fears, and almost half - 49 per cent - say the summer holidays make them think about whether their kid is suited for the current school system.

‌



According to the research, one in three are concerned about the amount of academic pressure, while further one in four say school makes their child unhappy.

‌



And 31% say their child’s education is like forcing a square peg into a round hole. In fact, as many as a quarter (26%) say they have thought about, or let, their child take a sick day on the first day of term because they were anxious about going in.

The study of 2,000 parents of school aged children found that 71% now see the traditional 9–3, five-day school model, which was formed over 200 years ago during the Victorian era, as outdated

View 2 Images Many parents are unsure whether or not the school system is right for their children (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Over half have considered homeschooling, rising to 73% among families with children with SEN, driven by a desire for their children to receive more personalised learning and support better suited to their individual needs.

The research was commissioned by online homeschooling provider, Wolsey Hall Oxford, which is urging the Department of Education to reform the current education system, calling for more flexible learning options tailored to each child rather than forcing children to adapt to unsuitable models.

Concerns are even greater among parents of children with Special Educational Needs (SEN). The school found 81% of parents of children with dyslexia, dyspraxia, autism or ADHD, say the current model is outdated, while almost three quarters of all parents surveyed believe a “one size fits all” approach is no longer effective.

‌



The school says this view has strengthened since the pandemic. When schools couldn’t meet families’ needs, parents sought alternatives and discovered a range of options beyond the traditional system, many of which remain underpromoted in favour of a rigid, top-down model of education.

Flexibility is seen as a key priority in 2026. Nearly half of parents believe a more flexible education system would better support their child’s wellbeing and academic success. Similarly, 44% say greater flexibility in how and when children learn would be beneficial.

Parents are also calling for different approaches to learning, with 62% favouring small group teaching amid concerns of growing class sizes, 40% backing project-based learning and 26% supporting a blended model of classroom and online education, reflecting the hybrid working patterns many parents now follow post-pandemic.

‌



Parents report that children are easily distracted (40%), become bored quickly (27%), dislike speaking in front of their peers (22%) and feel their learning is not tailored to their individual needs (17%).

Reflecting this, 78% of parents, rising to 80% among SEN parents, believe their child would benefit more from hands-on, experiential learning rather than spending the day at a desk. Over half (54%) say they would prefer a more practical approach to education.

‌



Almost all (99%) of parents would like their child to have more opportunities to explore the world beyond the classroom, while 48% feel their child’s skills are not being applied in real-life situations. Meanwhile, one in three (32%) believe the curriculum is outdated or irrelevant, and 30% say it is too repetitive.

Gavin McLean, Principal at Wolsey Hall Oxford, said: “Today’s education system still reflects a model first set up over 200 years ago, designed to fit the needs of parents who were factory workers, but children are not products on an assembly line.

“An education system should adapt to the child, nurturing their individuality, curiosity, and pace of learning, not force the child to conform to a rigid system that was never built for them. The fact many are forced through this outdated system throughout their younger years is a national crisis and one we are urging the Department of Education to address for all students and teaching practitioners.

Article continues below

“Homeschooling is increasingly seen as a popular alternative, giving parents the freedom to create a more personalised, flexible environment where children can truly engage through hands-on learning, real-world experiences, and the time and space to build confidence without pressure.

“As our research shows, many parents are already questioning whether the mainstream education system is the right fit. Exploring alternatives like homeschooling or a hybrid model of studying at home and in a physical school environment can open up new opportunities for children to thrive, develop independence and foster a genuine love of learning that stays with them for life.”

Parents are calling for a broader, more practical curriculum. Top priorities include first aid and CPR (64%), financial literacy (63%) and mental health and stress management (62%). Other areas highlighted include cooking and meal planning (57%), basic household maintenance (52%), interview skills (46%), identifying misinformation (33%), understanding tax (32%) and gardening (31%).

News.title: Teen dead in A66 crash which also killed cops 'seen in police chase on TikTok'
News.content:
Teen dead in A66 crash which also killed cops 'seen in police chase on TikTok'

A Volkswagen Passat occupied by five people was driven on the wrong side of the A66 near Middlesbrough and crashed into a police car yesterday, killing two officers as well as the five occupants

View 4 Images A teen believed to have died in yesterday's crash near Middlesbrough shared this footage on TikTok, it is reported

A teenager believed to have died in the A66 crash which killed two police officers had previously posted videos taking part in high-speed police chases on social media, reports suggest.

The teen is said to have published a string of clips on TikTok which show a car driving erratically through residential streets in recent months. In a clip filmed by a passenger in May with rap music playing in the background, an individual is driving an Audi at speed through a housing estate as a police car's blue lights can be seen behind.

The car then veers across a grassy playing field as the teenager tries to evade police officers. The TikTok account has since been removed.

View 4 Images The shocking footage was posted on TikTok (Image: Tiktok/unknownm829)

A66 Middlesbrough crash: Andy Burnham leads tributes to police officers killed on active duty READ MORE :

The footage has come to light as the individual is understood to have died - along with four other people - when a Volkswagen Passat was driven on the wrong side of the A66 near Middlesbrough and into an armed police car travelling in the right direction.

The two Cleveland Police officers in the marked police vehicle, who have since been named as PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died at the scene of the crash in the early hours of yesterday. Ring doorbell footage captured by houses in the area just minutes before the crash shows the Passat being driven at speed.

View 4 Images Security camera footage appears to show police chasing a car just moments before yesterday’s fatal collision

A pursuit of the "suspicious vehicle" came to a halt as the Passat turned on to the A66 three minutes before the crash. PC Blades and PC Clough were not part of the chase. Chief Constable Victoria Fuller paid tribute to her colleagues, saying: "These were brave officers, protecting our communities and serving our residents, who didn’t return home to their families at the end of their shift.

"This is an incredibly sad day for Cleveland. The loss has been felt across our communities, by our police family, and by our partner agencies. My thoughts, and the thoughts of everybody here at Cleveland Police, are with their families, friends, colleagues, and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time."

View 4 Images Tributes have been left at the scene for the two officers (Image: Richard McCarthy/PA Wire)

Lauren Somerville, chairman of the Cleveland Police Federation, added: "Words cannot describe the pain the Cleveland Police family is feeling today. Our colleagues who should have been going home to their loved ones at the end of their shifts are not. That is just unfathomable."

The Independent Office for Police Conduct have since opened an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the fatal crash. Chief Constable Fuller added: "While this investigation is ongoing, and out of respect for all those who have lost loved ones, I would strongly urge people to avoid speculation and respect the privacy of the families."

Article continues below

Just last week on Sunday, five teenagers died in a head-on collision on the M9 motorway in County Kildare, Ireland. The masked youngsters drove their vehicle on the wrong side of the road and into a family's car, leaving three adult sisters and a boy fighting for their lives.

News.title: Hero veterans left to struggle with mental health after leaving the armed forces
News.content:
Hero veterans left to struggle with mental health after leaving the armed forces

Nearly 20,000 military veterans sought help for their mental health, new figures show, as experts say navigating Civvy Street can be daunting for those leaving the forces

View 6 Images Thousands of soldiers are seeking help with their mental health (Image: Getty Images)

Almost 20,000 military veterans are being treated for mental health issues by the NHS after leaving the forces, latest figures show.

‌



They are being treated for issues including depression, PTSD, anxiety, self harm, psychosis, drug and alcohol difficulties, and gambling addiction.

‌



Between April 2025 and this March, 19,432 ex service members sought help. The total is more a tenth of the 148,000 in the armed forces.

‌



Organisations that support former military personnel say navigating life on Civvy Street can be daunting as many struggle after being institutionalised by years in the forces.

Colin Eastaway at The Block, in Liverpool, which offers support to veterans, said many former servicemen and women suffer in silence though.

View 6 Images Colin Eastaway offers support to veterans

‌



The former paratrooper, who set up the organisation in 2020 after struggling himself, said: “Things fell hard for me in Covid, I lost my employment and was struggling to pay the bills.

“I tried to get help, but felt doors were closed in my face. I had the idea to create this drop-in space to offer support for other veterans.”

So far this year 160 former servicemen have visited his offices seeking help. Colin said: “Demand is high, we’re always busy. We help people navigate available support, provide mental health support with specialists.

‌



“Everything is intertwined – mental health problems, homelessness, financial issues. But a problem shared is a problem halved. We help people bridge the gaps, pick up the slack.

“We have eight self-contained flats. Here you can speak to specialists, or other veterans. Our door’s always open.”

As the numbers visiting increase, the main problem is money. Colin said: “I can’t tell you why the numbers are so high, maybe word is getting around that we are helping. But the issue is always about funding. We can only plan for the next six months ahead.”

‌



View 6 Images Kieran Smith said he was not prepared for life after serving his country

Kieran Smith, 30, spent nine years in the RAF before leaving in 2024. He said: “There was a massive drop-off from that organised life to Civvy Street. I wasn’t prepared for it. It was a struggle from the start.

“I left the military with an alcohol addiction and mental health issues so I was already on the back foot. The military can only do so much. I was in and out of hospital. I was homeless on a number of occasions, sleeping in my car.

‌



“A big component of alcoholism is denial. When you’re in hospital, the whole aim is to detox you. But the internal problems were much larger.”

Kieran, who was put in touch with Colin, said: “I wouldn’t be here if it wasn’t for them. They gave me a base, they gave me support around the clock.

“I did create a lot of work for them. Things were really deep. There were so many things I didn’t understand. In the military everything is done for you. I was in mental torment. They put me in touch with an addiction specialist. It’s not been an easy road but they put me in the right place.”

‌



View 6 Images Blair Murray served in the Royal Logistics Corps

Blair Murray, 44, who served for more than a decade in the Royal Logistics Corps, was made homeless by a landlord last year. After sofa-surfing with friends, he spent 17 weeks living in a tent in woodland in County Durham.

The local authority has now placed him in a hotel while he seeks permanent housing. He said: “I’ve been out for 16 years and a lot of the problems are due to my mental health.

‌



“I’ve struggled to get help. The system is so complicated. I didn’t help myself at first, I was taking drugs, life was a constant battle. I’d get high as it made me forget my problems.

“It affects people around you. I’ve been declined social housing. I’ve been offered hostels, but there’s drink and drugs I don’t want to be around.”

Blair, who served in Iraq, Kosovo, Bosnia and the Falklands, added: “When I left they didn’t prepare you for Civvy Street. Now they get people in six months before you leave to help prepare you.

‌



"That wasn’t there for me. All the doctor wanted to do was stuff me full of antidepressants. It costs £600 a week to put me in this hotel – a lot more than housing benefits cost. The whole system isn’t working.”

View 6 Images Research has shown that rates of PTSD have increased among UK armed forces personnel (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Dave Tindale, from Changing Step North East, which provides help, support and advice for veterans, said: “Every client we assist has different issues. Dealing with the different authorities can be daunting.

‌



“Mental health services are not diagnostic, so they treat without properly diagnosing the problems. They have not got the time or resources to properly assess people. Often, the only way to properly diagnose problems is by going down the private route, but that costs a lot.”

Research by the King’s Centre for Military Health Research in 2024 found rates of probable PTSD and mental disorders had increased among UK Armed Forces personnel, as well as former personnel. The report investigated the impact of deployment to Iraq and Afghanistan on health and wellbeing.

Its recommendations included continued investment into Armed Forces and veteran mental health services, as well as a review of provision of treatment and care of complex PTSD and alcohol misuse.

‌



View 6 Images A survey of veterans found 55% had experienced a mental or physical health issue (Image: Getty Images/Stocktrek Images)

A 2022 survey of 4,910 veterans, found 55% have experienced a mental or physical health issue potentially related to service since leaving. More than 80% said their condition got worse as civilians.

The MoD said: “We have made significant improvements to mental health support for personnel and veterans.

Article continues below

“All personnel receive a structured mental health assessment when they leave service. We back NHS England with £25million a year for healthcare services for veterans, service leavers, reservists and their families.”

It added: “A new £50m Valour programme will make support services from health to housing, employment and finance, more joined up at every level, making it easier for veterans to access support.”

News.title: TV Licence Amazon Prime rules as UK households may be fined £1,000
News.content:
TV Licence Amazon Prime rules as UK households may be fined £1,000

Many people assume paying for Amazon Prime means they’re covered to watch whatever they like - but this isn't always the case

View 3 Images People may need a TV Licence and not know it (Image: Getty)

You might settle down to watch your favourite series on Amazon Prime without giving it a second thought - perhaps Elle or Clarkson's Farm. But some UK households may need to be more careful, as viewers could face a fine of up to £1,000.

‌



TV Licensing guidance says a Licence may still be required for some programmes watched via streaming services - and that includes Prime. TV Licensing officials state: "If you’re watching TV showing live on Amazon Prime, you need to be covered by a TV Licence."

‌



It further confirms: "You don’t need a TV Licence if you’re only watching on-demand programmes on Amazon Prime."

‌



View 3 Images Households caught watching live TV without a licence could face a fine of up to £1,000 (Image: Getty)

People may assume a TV Licence isn’t needed if they pay for Prime, but Amazon's subscription fee only covers access to Prime perks - such as free one-day delivery, on-demand streaming through Prime Video and Prime Music and additional discounts.

Paying for Amazon and a TV Licence "means you can legally watch live programmes on Amazon Prime, so you can make the most of everything included with your subscription", TV Licensing confirms.

‌



A licence is needed to watch any live TV programme as well as BBC iPlayer.

How much is a TV Licence in 2026?

The TV Licence fee changed on April 1, 2026. A colour licence now costs £180, while a black-and-white licence costs £60.50.

If you’re blind (severely sight impaired), you can still apply for a 50% concession, reducing the cost of a colour licence to £90.

Article continues below

What happens if I don't pay my TV Licence?

View 3 Images Amazon Prime viewers could still need a TV Licence, depending on what they watch (Image: Wang Yukun via Getty Images)

TV Licensing says it may visit your address to check whether you need a TV Licence. If it’s found that you’ve been watching, recording or streaming programmes without the correct licence, you could face prosecution.

You could also face a fine of up to £1,000, plus any legal costs and/or compensation the court orders. In Guernsey, the maximum fine is £2,000, with legal costs and/or compensation potentially added on top.

News.title: Nurse's two-second pen method could save lives and it's helpful for parents
News.content:
Nurse's two-second pen method could save lives and it's helpful for parents

A paediatric nurse has shared an incredibly simple pen trick that takes just two seconds and could help parents spot warning signs of a child rash before it becomes a medical emergency.

View 2 Images This health tip is very useful for parents who are checking their kids' skin (Image: Petri Oeschger via Getty Images)

Everyone should know this incredibly simple pen trick, particularly parents, as it could genuinely save a life.

‌



If you notice a rash or red mark on yourself or your child, it's easy to dismiss it. Such marks can be triggered by any number of causes, including stress, fatigue, allergies or medication. However, they can also signal something far more serious - such as scarlet fever or measles.

‌



Paediatric nurse Sarah Hunstead, creator of child and first aid education group CPR Kids, has highlighted the importance of keeping a close eye on suspicious marks. If one changes, you should get it examined by a GP.

‌



An easy way to tell if a mark or rash is changing is to grab a pen. According to Nurse Hunstead, you should draw a border around the suspected rash, mark or spot using a skin-safe pen. This makes it easy to spot any changes, such as the mark growing larger.

The expert used a handy slogan to prompt parents, stating: "Remember: Outline with pen, then check it again!"

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



In a recent Instagram post, she added: "Grab a pen, circle around the outside, and check it again later. This is an easy way of being able to tell whether something is spreading or not."

If you don't have a skin-safe pen, don't fret. Another way to track how your skin is changing is to take photos of the impacted area.

You can look back at the pictures and see how the skin is developing – and even share them with your doctor if you have any concerns.

‌



NHS advice about rashes on babies and children

The NHS website states: "Many things can cause a rash in babies and children, and they're often nothing to worry about." However, you should call 999 or go to A&E immediately if your child is unwell with the following symptoms:

a stiff neck

bothered by light

they seem confused, agitated or they're not responding like they usually do

difficulty breathing (you may notice grunting noises or their tummy sucking under their ribs), breathlessness, or they're breathing very fast

their skin, lips or tongue look pale, blue, grey or blotchy

sudden swelling of their lips, mouth, throat or tongue

their throat feels tight or they're struggling to swallow

the rash looks like small bruises or bleeding under the skin and does not fade when you press a glass against it

View 2 Images It's important to keep an eye on rashes to see if they change or develop rapidly (Image: Marina Demidiuk via Getty Images)

‌



The NHS adds: "On brown and black skin, it may be easier to see the rash or colour changes on the soles of the feet, palms, lips, tongue and inside the eyelids."

Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if your child:

has a rash you're worried about and you're not sure what to do

feels hotter than usual when you touch their back or chest, feels sweaty or they’re shivering

is under 3 months old and has a temperature of 38C

is aged 3 months or older and has a temperature of 39C or higher

is aged 5 years or older and has a temperature below 36C

Article continues below

You can get more information about rashes on babies and children by heading to the NHS website. You should also consult a medical professional if you have any worries about yourself or a loved one.

News.title: Amanda Abbington hits back over Giovanni Pernice’s Strictly Come Dancing claims
News.content:
Amanda Abbington hits back over Giovanni Pernice’s Strictly Come Dancing claims

Amanda Abbington spoke out after former Strictly Come Dancing partner Giovanni Pernice said that he had suicidal thoughts over her bullying allegations.

View 3 Images Amanda Abbington spoke out over Giovanni Pernice's new book (Image: PA)

Amanda Abbington has hit back after former Strictly Come Dancing partner Giovanni Pernice said that he had suicidal thoughts over her bullying allegations.

‌



The Sherlock actress, 54, took part in the competition in 2023, where she was partnered with the champion, 35. Viewers were stunned when she quit just weeks into the competition, and she later alleged that she was suffering from PTSD, accusing the pro of bullying and harassment.

‌



He fiercely denied all claims, with BBC bosses investigating 16 allegations - he was cleared on 10 counts while six were upheld. The broadcaster also issued an apology to the star.

‌



Pernice spoke about his experience in his new memoir, Taking The Lead, where he claimed that he was left a ‘burnt-out shell’ after their fall-out, and battling a deep depression.

View 3 Images The pair took part on Strictly in 2023 (Image: BBC)

In response, Abbington told the Sun: “It’s sad, though not surprising, that Giovanni is continuing down this route.

‌



“He took part in the BBC investigation that made findings against him, following which the channel paid me compensation.

“He is grossly mischaracterising what happened to suit his own narrative, but I have no interest in engaging with that. My focus is on moving forward.”

A friend of the Mr Selfridge star added: “Amanda will forever regard Giovanni as a monster. She stands by her allegations - she’s not the only one who was a victim of his behaviour.”

‌



In a serialisation of his book, published on Saturday by the Daily Mail, Pernice said that he was instantly impressed with his former partner’s efforts in rehearsals, claiming that she sent him a thank you message following their first session.

He described ‘moments of tension’ but reportedly said that there were ‘never any arguments’ between them, describing his behaviour as supportive and encouraging.

As the competition continued and rehearsals became more intense, he alleged that their bond quickly fractured. Abbington then quit the series midway through, and later accused her professional partner of "unnecessary, cruel and abusive behaviour”.

‌



Following a public fall-out, Pernice claimed that it had become “increasingly difficult” to read “all the bile that was flowing in my direction”, before thanking then-girlfriend Molly Brown for remaining by his side.

“She could see that I was spiralling and she was there to talk to me when I was down,” he added. “There were certainly times I would have killed myself if Molly hadn’t been there.”

View 3 Images Giovanni was cleared on 10 allegations while 6 were upheld (Image: PA)

‌



The accusations sparked an internal investigation. Former Met officers were brought on by BBC bosses to oversee the "evidence gathering", and review footage of Pernice’s rehearsals with Abbington, as well as their texts.

Pernice has always denied all allegations. The probe found that he was not physically abusive, but complaints about verbal bullying and harassment were upheld - though the exact details of the complaints have not been made public.

In a statement, the broadcaster said: “The BBC has now concluded its review into the complaints made by Amanda Abbington against Giovanni Pernice. We take any allegations of bullying and harassment very seriously, and this review has taken time due to its complex nature and our desire to ensure a rigorous and robust process was undertaken.

‌



"Strictly Come Dancing is a family show and we rightly expect very high standards. While competition can be tough, rigorous and demanding, we want the show to ultimately be a joyous and transformative experience. It is a great shame if this hasn’t been the case for everyone who has appeared on the show.

“We have assessed the complaints, and we have upheld some, but not all, of the complaints made. We want to apologise to Amanda Abbington and to thank her for coming forward and taking part. We know this would not have been an easy thing to do.”

The Mirror has contacted Giovanni’s reps for a comment.
