One source said the official Fifa party had attempted to portray their governance crisis as a private dispute between Infantino and Montagliani. The Canadian businessman has not commented since news of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise emerged, but has been widely touted in Europe as a possible contender to replace Infantino.

The pair met briefly and shook hands before the CFU meeting in an exchange captured by Infantino’s personal camera crew.

While Mexico, Grenada and St Kitts and Nevis have all broken with Concacaf and declared their support for Infantino, the majority of their 41 members are understood to back the alliance with Uefa advocated by Montagliani.

The Uefa/Concacaf pact extends beyond attempts to unseat Infantino, with the two confederations in talks about setting up a joint Nations League in 2028 that could develop further into a new global competition.

Sports.title: Meet the new Spurs, same as the old Spurs despite big summer spending | Billy Munday
Sports.content:
This was supposed to be New Spurs. Daniel Levy, such a magnet for fan apathy, has been sidelined. Roberto De Zerbi’s recruitment drive has won the transfer market. The stadium is still nice. But Spurs and ambition were always an awkward combination and all those cash-fuelled dreams were shattered within an hour of the new season. A few headed for the exits after Brentford’s third goal on 49 minutes. There were not many left by the time those in freakish purple made their way over to that corner of the Gtech at full time.

There was no escaping the irony that the best player on the splendid opening-day pitch was the only new face in Brentford’s starting XI. Mamadou Sangaré, signed for a club-record fee from Lens, made sure his Premier League debut was played at his pace – faster and more dynamic than any of Sandro Tonali, Lucas Bergvall or Conor Gallagher could deal with in midfield. The Mali international ran off Bergvall to set up Keane Lewis-Potter’s first and struck the shot that led to Michael Kayode’s third.

Sangaré is an example of what happens when a club gets its recruitment right. The 24-year-old is clearly a player on the up – and has the temperament to match his talent. His career has not been easy, moving to Europe and Red Bull Salzburg at 18 but spending his years in Austria on loans in the second tier and in Belgium. After a year at Lens that included Coupe de France glory and individual Ligue 1 accolades, Brentford paid what already looks like a bargain £41m. The standing ovation at his second-half withdrawal was the least he deserved.

On the other side, Tonali was the face of Tottenham’s troubles, the £100m marquee signing playing a game where the ball seemed to elude him, tease him from afar. De Zerbi has spoken this summer of how impressed he had been watching the midfielder play as a teenager for the Italian club he supports, Brescia. He looked considerably less impressed with the 26-year-old version after he skied a volley high over the crossbar on 40 minutes, completing a first half of misplaced passes and frustrated fouls, always one step behind the imperious Sangaré.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré emphatically won the battle of the midfield summer signings against Sandro Tonali. Photograph: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images

De Zerbi is known for his boldness – and there was certainly something to be said for making Archie Gray the youngest captain in Tottenham’s history in the absence of the injured new club skipper, Micky van de Ven. You could forgive his predecessor, Cristian Romero, for feeling a touch smug in his new Madrid apartment. The edgy Marcos Senesi, such an unflappable figure amid the turnover in the Bournemouth defence last season, clearly spent too much time with his Argentina teammate Romero at the World Cup. His defensive partner, Jan Paul van Hecke, has not settled in either. Scotland’s captain, Andy Robertson, led out by the 20-year-old Gray here, must be asking what he has let himself in for.

So must Savinho and Omar Marmoush, pending arrivals that will take Spurs’ summer spending towards the dizzying heights of £400m – only Liverpool in 2025 have spent more in a single window out of any club, anywhere. Spurs had brought in six new players before a ball was kicked but still started the season with Richarlison leading the line. The contrast between his meek performance and that of his compatriot and opposite number Igor Thiago, combining power and poise, felt significant. The ease with which Brentford’s No 9 had it all afternoon was evident in his over-relaxed penalty that pinged back off the foot of a post at 3-0.

After establishing a two-goal lead through Lewis-Potter and Vitaly Janelt, Brentford were unfazed by Spurs’ introduction of their £85m signing Mateus Fernandes at the break and carried on where they left off. How high can they fly this season? Unlike many of their rivals, Keith Andrews’ side are without the burden of European football after missing out on the final day of last season. Second-half substitutes such as Jaidon Anthony and Callum Wilson are handy additions of firepower at a fraction of the cost in a market that is ballooning off the back of Spurs’ wild spending.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Tottenham started last season with a 3-0 win over Burnley and a 2-0 victory at Manchester City – points that promised a new beginning under Thomas Frank, who haunted them from his old manor here, but ultimately proved vital in their fight for survival under De Zerbi in May. Where does this result and performance leave the head coach? This will probably work out eventually – his vastly changed squad must be given time to gel. But what if this is New Spurs? A constant cycle of new lows and new ways of embarrassing themselves. After two 17th-place finishes in succession, would anyone blame them for taking that now?

Sports.title: Mateta’s Palace dispute deepens after losing appeals to end contract early
Sports.content:
Jean-Philippe Mateta is in dispute with Crystal Palace over the final year of his contract but failed in an attempt to have it ruled invalid by an independent Premier League tribunal and Fifa. The France striker signed a four-and-a-half-year contract when he joined permanently from Mainz in January 2022 after an initial loan, in a deal that also included the option of a 12-month extension. That was activated by Palace in 2024, with Mateta’s contract now due to expire at the end of this season.

But it is understood the 29-year-old and his representatives have disputed whether that extension was valid and took the case to an independent tribunal under Premier League regulations last season. Official confirmation of the outcome has not been disclosed, although Palace insist Mateta’s contract remains binding and he played in their defeat at Everton on Saturday. Fifa also rejected his claim after ruling it did not have jurisdiction over the dispute. Mateta’s representative has been approached for comment.

Quick Guide How do I 

Mateta has been trying to force through a move from Selhurst Park for some time and it is understood he has interest from Aston Villa, who are considering whether to sell Ollie Watkins to the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. Mateta failed a medical with Milan in January because of a knee problem after the Italian side had agreed a fee of around £30m and spent two months on the sidelines before returning to help Palace win the Conference League. Mateta was booed by some sections of supporters at first and is likely to get another frosty reception when Manchester City visit south London on Friday night in their first home match of the new campaign.

View image in fullscreen Jean-Philippe Mateta had a shot hit a post during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Everton. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock

Meanwhile, Pierre Sage has insisted that Ismaïla Sarr will remain at the club despite strong interest from Galatasaray. The Senegal forward missed the 2-0 defeat at Everton due to what Sage described as a “pain in his groin” and Palace’s new manager dismissed reports that the 28-year-old had refused to travel to Merseyside because he wants to leave.

“We took the decision before the session with the doctor, the player, and me, to let him get treatment and do an individual session, and he will be back on Monday with us,” he said. “For the moment, we don’t want him to leave. He is under contract with us with three years to go and he will be with us on Monday.”

Palace are also braced for more interest this week in Adam Wharton and Daniel Muñoz, who has entered the final two years of his contract and has been linked with Everton, Nottingham Forest and Tottenham. They have already agreed a loan move for Chelsea’s Axel Disasi but may be forced into signing another centre back before the deadline if fears over Chadi Riad’s knee injury are proved correct.

The Moroccan, who was out for more than a year after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury on his second appearance for the club after joining in 2024, was carried off on a stretcher after attempting to block a cross in the second half against Everton. “I hope it will be better than we think,” said Sage. “We await the medical tests.”

Sports.title: Lincoln spirits soar despite defeat on second-tier return 65 years in the making
Sports.content:
There is optimism to be found in almost every corner of the footballing landscape at this time of the year, but you would do well to find anyone without a smile on their face on this sunny Saturday lunchtime in one of Britain’s most picturesque cities.

Football may not necessarily be the first thing that springs to mind when you think of Lincoln. After all, Sincil Bank sits in the shadow of the imposing cathedral, high on the hill and a building that symbolically represents the importance of this area stretching back hundreds of years.

But the city’s sporting pride is writing its own slice of history. Yuri Gagarin had only just returned from space when Lincoln last hosted second-tier football, a 2-0 win over Leyton Orient in 1961. But after more than 65 years, the Imps are a Championship side again, having won League One last season with more than 100 points.

View image in fullscreen Lincoln won League One last season in style, finishing top by 12 points. Photograph: Harriet Massey/Getty Images

Sincil Bank housed the biggest attendance here, 10,545, for more than 40 years for their return to the second tier. While the majority left disappointed as Portsmouth inflicted the hosts’ second consecutive defeat to start the season, the mood did not feel too dampened given the extraordinary journey this club have enjoyed of late.

Most of Lincoln’s recent history has been in the footballing wilderness, but there is rapid change, on and off the pitch. The Imps have spent £10m over the summer modernising the ground with a new fan village, a big screen and upgrades to the stands that were all but sold out.

There is change in the dugout, too, with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw jointly taking over from Michael Skubala, but some things remain the same. The air raid siren – a nod to the city’s military history – still sounds every time a Lincoln corner booms its way into the opposition area and the dedication to a traditional 4-4-2, which has seen them rise through the leagues, endures.

Whether it will need adapting over the course of this season remains to be seen, but for now, Lincoln are backing what has got them this far. The most important constant is the deep-rooted connection between supporters and team, which has helped fuel their progression. Togetherness is at the heart of everything.

Barely a soul left before the final whistle, even when Ebou Adams’s strike secured a first win of the season for Portsmouth in the 69th minute. Many supporters stayed behind in the new fan village to debrief the loss and they remain generally upbeat. Given how far they have come, it will take more than two defeats to steer this club off course.

Had Ben House scored when through on goal early on, this historic afternoon may have been one of celebration. But Portsmouth underlined the step up in quality shortly after, going 2-0 ahead with wonderful strikes from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen and Adrian Segecic.

View image in fullscreen Defeat by Portsmouth did not detract from a celebratory day for those associated with Lincoln. Photograph: Mark Kerton/Shutterstock

Reeco Hackett’s penalty before the break gave the Imps hope but Adams sealed the deal for Pompey.

“It’s been an amazing day for the club,” Shaw said. “The atmosphere was fantastic at the start of the game and it all aligned lovely until the goal.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“People have waited a long time to have a Championship football match here and I desperately hope we can have some good results here. But the ball moves around a bit quicker at this level, the quality increases so we’ve got to be a bit more alive to certain situations.”

To take this afternoon on face value would perhaps be overlooking the more important story. Lincoln represent a beacon of hope not just for themselves, but for much of the EFL, by showing that aggressively spending beyond your means is not the only way to achieve success. If they can go from non-league to the Championship in 10 years, why can’t anyone?

View image in fullscreen Reeco Hackett became the first Lincoln player to score a second-tier goal at Sincil Bank since Joe Buick in April 1961. Photograph: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images

Perhaps money is not everything. Instead, success can be built on spirit, being greater than the sum of your parts and a bond between all involved. This club is still firmly in touch with what matters; the revamped Stacey West Stand bears the name of the two fans who died in the Bradford fire disaster of 1985, while the family zones were packed with the next generation of Lincoln fans keen for their first real glimpse of their new heroes.

This is not their first rodeo as underdogs, either. Lincoln weren’t supposed to win League Two in 2019. They certainly weren’t supposed to win League One with a mid-table budget last year, a division that included Cardiff, Luton and Bolton.

This time around, they are not expected to survive the Championship; they may not beat the odds again but, with that spirit of togetherness behind them, they will give it a thoroughly good go.

Sports.title: José Mourinho marks Real Madrid return with late drama and touch of humility
Sports.content:
José Mourinho says he is calmer now so when the rest of the bench emptied, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate the 90th-minute goal that finally delivered victory on his first game in charge of Real Madrid in 4,380 days, he did not set off with them. Instead, he clenched his fists, got to his feet and walked down the touchline behind the subs, watching them head, shouting, towards Carlos Espí. As they piled on down in the corner, he pulled over his captain Fede Valverde for a word. Which might just have been: phew.

For all those stars; for all that Mourinho’s main task might just have been to find a way to fit Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Jude Bellingham together; for all that he had introduced Yan Diomande, the most expensive player in the club’s history, it was a 21-year-old, unknown six months ago and unexpectedly signed from Levante, who got the goal that secured victory upon the coach’s second coming.

Espí, whose goals had rescued Levante from relegation last season and who is still living at Madrid’s Valdebebas training ground like his coach, the two of them sharing breakfast every morning, was signed for pretty much this: to be a different type of striker, an old-school No 9, with a presence in the area. And when a scrappy, broken-up move ended with Mbappé seeing the ball run away from him in the area, there he was to force it over the line. Perhaps even to pose a question: is his a profile they could do with and not just in reserve? This time, at least, it had worked.

View image in fullscreen Carlos Espí celebrates the late winner for Real Madrid. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Mourinho’s first game since a 4-2 win over Osasuna in May 2013 began with the photographers abandoning their places behind the goal to surround him on the bench, no doubt what the attraction was; it ended with him hugging the Espanyol coach Manolo González, high-fiving the referee and ducking down the tunnel. In between time, reality was revealed, which he surely always imagined it would be: it is early, solutions are never immediate, and he had said that Espanyol were a good side. At times, they showed it too. Madrid had more chances, but Manolo’s team had largely succeeded in limiting the visitors.

On a night where Madrid exhibited some of the old flaws, there were doubts still – it is the first day after all – but they were at least allayed for a little while. There will be other days, sterner tests of this team; there will also be sterner tests of Mourinho’s temperament, of course.

When Madrid faced Benfica in the spring, Mourinho had described his time there as “three hard, intense, sometimes violent years”. But the thing about nostalgia is that as the bad slips into the distance, only the good remains. Mourinho said that he is “not the kind of man who misses anything”, someone who has “regrets”; plenty though had missed him, the president Florentino Pérez first among them. In his worldview, managers are mostly a necessary evil; the Portuguese is virtually the only coach he had ever truly liked.

There are those who had longed for exactly that intensity, violence even: for a hard man to lead them, some kind of iron surgeon to fix them and go to war with their rivals, someone with the personality to impose. For all that by the end they really could not go on, at some level Pérez had always been drawn to Mourinho’s return. He clung to the idea that their success after his departure – six Champions League wins in 11 years – was down to him, that he had made it possible. He had shown the way.

Mourinho told a story on the eve of this game revealing that after every trophy Madrid won he would have got a call from Pérez. “I always said no, no, no, it was nothing to do with me,” he said, which was a neat way of saying it kind of was. This was not a confidence betrayed: Pérez had said much the same. It took the president 13 years to attend to his urge, but now Mourinho was back.

And, perhaps, why not? The last returnees had done rather well, while all the others had failed. There was a moment at the end of that story when Mourinho said the trophies belonged to Zinedine Zidane and Carlo Ancelotti, not him, and innocently checked that they were the only men to have won anything. The diagnosis of their ills, the challenge before them, required his surgery too. Like in 2010, Madrid had fallen behind Barcelona. They have not won a major title in two years, and that was about culture as well as football.

View image in fullscreen A first look of Yan Diomande in action for Real Madrid against Espanyol. Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images

It may not be as simple as effort but that is a start. “We have to try not to negotiate things that are non-negotiable,” Mourinho said. “Commitment can’t be missing.” Mourinho has the authority to change that, or so it goes. He would be afforded it, anyway. That at least is the theory. Habits had been changed, demands made. Sessions had improved, or the attitude towards them. Diomande had said he was ready to “die” for his coach, who insisted that was just a phrase, but he could not help but be pleased with that.

There were other reasons to be optimistic. Vinícius’s future had been resolved at last, no lingering doubts over status or resentment. The World Cup is out the way, no other priority on the horizon. Mourinho noted that Brazil, France and England had found a way to get the best out of Vinícius, Mbappe and Bellingham, but that getting the best of all three is different. “I don’t think they’re incompatible,” he said; last year it often looked like they were, Bellingham, admitting that they find themselves occupying the same spaces at times.

Here, they all started. Bellingham was at No 10, Vinícius tight to the touchline. “For me this is his [Jude’s] position: the connection with the forwards, he can score goals. He has to play close to the goal. Playing at 6 or 8 we’re losing his closeness to the goal,” said Mourinho.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bellingham had an immediate impact, the first goal of this new era coming from a dead ball and after nine minutes. Vinícius was fouled, which was already looking like becoming a pattern – Álex Calatrava had already given him a kick in the back, prompting Mourinho to raise his arms – and from the left, Arda Guler delivered a superb cross. Bellingham leapt highest to head past Marko Dimitrovic.

View image in fullscreen Jude Bellingham celebrates after giving Real the lead. Photograph: David Ramos/Getty Images

This time, sitting on the left end of the bench, Mourinho barely flinched. He got up, put his hands in his pockets and walked along the touchline to the other end where the rest of his sizeable staff sat in the overspill in the stand beyond the other end. There, he shook hands with Sami Khedira, the in-house assistant Madrid have provided him, and Roberto Merella, the analyst.

And that, it was tempting to assume, was that. The gap between the teams looked insurmountable. Madrid were pressing high, Espanyol barely able to find a way out. Here was a glimpse, they might have hoped, of the future. Instead, the intensity dropped again and that was an invitation for Espanyol.

When Dean Huijsen needed attention for a cut, Madrid’s players came to Mourinho for instructions but the game started to slip from them a little. Espanyol took a step forward and soon had an equaliser. Thibaut Courtois saved from Riedel, Roberto Fernández unable to keep down the follow-up. Then a lovely move concluded with Tyrhys Dolan and Javi Hernández setting up Calatrava to score. Mourinho sat almost motionless.

Twice Mbappé escaped to force saves from Dimitrovic, one on each side of the area, but it was Espanyol who should have led at the break. Again, the ball was worked into position. From the right, Omar El Hilali provided a superb cross. Dolan could not quite get to it, inside the six-yard box, and Fernández headed it straight at his own feet. Mbappé may wonder how he did not put Madrid into the lead just after the break. From Guler’s corner, Bellingham headed against the bar, via Dimitrovic’s hand, and the ball dropped to the Frenchman right by the post. Somehow, it went wide.

Valverde hit the post, Mbappé shot wide, but there was no way through. Mourinho turned to the men behind him – Cucurella, Diomande, Camavinga, Alexander-Arnold, Espí – until, at last, he saw them dash past him, given a reprieve on his return.

“I think we deserved to win, but Espanyol didn’t deserve to lose,” Mourinho said as he ended the night with a touch of humility.

Sports.title: Anton Stach snatches late Leeds winner to sour Glasner’s new dawn at Forest
Sports.content:
For Anton Stach, another sweet direct free-kick to add to the back catalogue, this one souring Oliver Glasner’s first match in charge of Nottingham Forest. Only Dominik Szoboszlai eclipsed Stach’s record of three direct free-kick goals in the Premier League last season, one of those coming against Glasner’s Crystal Palace.

Stach’s latest right-foot strike earned Leeds, fresh from a near-flawless pre-season and an expensive and exciting summer in the market, a divine opening-day victory with a couple of minutes of normal time remaining.

It has been a busy few weeks for the Germany midfielder. “He even released a burger a few days ago and I never expected him to do this,” said the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, alluding to Stach launching a burger at a city-centre eatery to raise money for charity. “He’s a bit of a weird and crazy guy.

“I expected when he was over the free-kick that he could do something special. He has done it time and time again. He surprised me [with his free-kicks] last season [but now] I trust him with everything. Last season, I would have never thought about it.”

For Forest, a few minutes before kick-off, the curtain going up on another season, a new protagonist emerged from the tunnel. Glasner, Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months, surveyed the scene from his technical area. But the start of this new dawn did not go to plan, an underwhelming performance culminating with Stach sneaking in his whipped free-kick at Matz Sels’s near post. At least Forest can put things right quickly, Leeds visiting in a Carabao Cup rematch on Tuesday.

Leeds were imposing and always looked more threatening, rationing Forest to moments. In the first half, Harry Wilson had a debut goal disallowed when the assistant referee raised his flag for offside after the Welshman, whose arrival is evidence of Leeds’ ambition, latched on to Jayden Bogle’s pushed pass. In the second, Sels’ strong left hand prevented a header by the £34m signing Tarik Muharemovic, another debutant, flying into the top corner.

Glasner, who left marquee signing Ousmane Diomande on the bench and introduced Xaver Schlager late on, puffed his cheeks as every outfield Leeds player joined the celebrations. The away end, bathed in the evening sun, was jubilant. The Forest areas began to empty.

“It was pretty clear that I can’t come with my staff, lay our hands on the shoulders [of the players], and all of a sudden we play like Real Madrid in the 70s or whatever,” Glasner said. “It was an OK performance from both teams – a typical first Premier League game after a long break and this is also now not the time to bury our heads into the sand.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Anton Stach jumps for joy after his late winner for Leeds. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA

These remain early days – Nuno Espírito Santo was in charge when Forest beat Brentford in their opening game last season – but they did little to enthuse the locals. Chris Wood arrived from the bench and sent a bobbling ball wide with a first-time shot from Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected pass. Schlager replaced James McAtee for his debut, but Leeds were buoyant at the final whistle.

Only Arsenal and Manchester United scored more set-piece goals than Leeds last season, but Farke dismissed the suggestion they are more important than previously. “There is not one team who won the World Cup without a set-piece goal,” said the German, stating ability from dead balls was a factor in their summer recruitment, Wilson a case in point.

“I remember Germany 12 years ago, a crap [quarter-final] game against France: Mats Hummels header, boom, goal,” he said. “I remember magic free-kick takers: Juninho, who got this crazy curve on the ball. It is always a major part of the game, not just nowadays. Anton is perhaps not as beautiful on the eye like Juninho’s free-kicks, but bloody effective, and I quite like it.”

Sports.title: Carrick tells Manchester United to keep calm and carry on after Hull humbling
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick says he will not overreact, but has called for improvement after Manchester United started the season with a 2-0 defeat at Hull. United lost their opening game for the fourth time in the past seven years as Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy took advantage of poor defending from set-pieces.

The United head coach presented a professional exterior despite United’s performance not reaching the desired standard as they were deservedly beaten by Hull, who finished sixth in the Championship last season.

“I’m talking to you quite calmly, but I’m not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, so there’s a big difference,” he said. “I played [for United] for a long time. You don’t get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal.

“It’s 100% not that, and trust me, it’s not that. It just doesn’t mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it. Inside we’re hurting and we need to get better. But the calmness doesn’t mean there’s no emotion in it, for sure.”

He added: “The result’s the result. We got beat, we’re hurt and it’s not a nice feeling. It doesn’t mean it’s going to change the whole direction of how we’re going as a team or as a football club.

“It’s one game and results can happen in football, we all understand that. It’s not nice when they do, but it does happen.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United’s Bruno Fernandes (left) looks dejected after the match against Hull City Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

United barely threatened throughout the 90 minutes. “Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game,” Bruno Fernandes said. “We gave too much of the ball to them, in the first 20 minutes the goalkeeper had more touches on the ball, too much time. We need to press a little bit more, be more aggressive, and set-plays – we need to work on it, to be more aggressive and try not to concede these types of goals.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hull’s head coach, Sergej Jakirovic, said he and his backroom staff had spotted a weakness in the way United defended set-pieces, but would not divulge his “secret” that helped to expose it.

Hull are strongly tipped for relegation and their supporters sung “are you watching Joe Cole?” during the match after the pundit mocked their chances of survival. “I don’t have any problems with critics with opinions,” Jakirovic said. “We tried to prove them wrong and today we won the game. Now it’s 37 to go, so we will try to continue like this. I’m very, very happy because of all the people in the club.”

Sports.title: New season, new hairstyle for Haaland! Man City star Erling chops off iconic long hair and shows off new look ahead of Premier League campaign
Sports.content:
New season, new hairstyle for Haaland! Man City star Erling chops off iconic long hair and shows off new look ahead of Premier League campaign

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Erling Haaland has shocked fans by debuting a new hairstyle.

The Manchester City striker has abandoned his trademark Viking-style long locks and opted for a buzz cut.

He teased the new trim in a short Instagram video on Sunday morning and fans will get to see it in all its glory as City take on Bournemouth in their Premier League opener.

Haaland has varied his hairstyle down the years, sometimes adopting a ponytail and other times letting his plumage fall freely, but this is a new aesthetic for the 26-year-old.

'No way,' former City boss Pep Guardiola said in reaction to Haaland's new look on his YouTube channel. 'You are lucky you have hair!'

Former Barcelona and Inter Milan star Zlatan Ibrahimovic - who once told Haaland his power comes from his long hair - asked if he shaved it all off 'for a bet', while Jack Grealish admitted 'I can't stop looking at the top of your head.'

Erling Haaland has ditched his iconic long locks for a buzz cut, as he revealed on Instagram

Former City boss Pep Guardiola was stunned by his old striker's new look

The forward has enjoyed a free-spirited summer holiday since reaching the World Cup quarter-finals with Norway.

He spent time hanging out with Pretty Little Thing founder Umar Kamani on a yacht in the French Riviera and also went on a boat trip around Sicily.

Haaland also had the chance to meet basketball legend Michael Jordan, a link-up brokered by one of Kamani's friends, as exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport.

He and Kamani were merrymaking at the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, a stunning coastal resort in Antibes where suites break the bank at up to £7,058 per night.

Then again, that's merely a drop in the ocean for Haaland, who nets close to £1million per week, and Kamani, whose net worth is estimated to be around $1billion (£797m).

Haaland recently claimed on Snapchat that his brain is 'fried' after playing in 67 games for club and country last season, so a break was needed.

You could say he has been letting his hair down - but that won't be possible with this new chop.

The Norwegian has garnered plenty of popularity for his hair in the past. Former Manchester City ace Kevin De Bruyne revealed that his children were inspired by his look.

‘Erling is a superstar. All three children have long hair. I see that with the kids at [my son's] school too. They all have hair like that. It's funny,' he said in 2023.

For the Community Shield last week, Haaland sported a ponytail and proved to be ineffective.

He sported a ponytail for last week's Community Shield match with Arsenal but was ineffective

Manchester City lost 3-0 to Arsenal, submitting a languid and toothless performance which saw new manager Enzo Maresca come under fire.

Replacing Pep Guardiola after his trophy-laden decade was always going to be an uphill task.

Haaland was limited to 13 touches and had zero shots on target before being hooked against the champions.

Sports.title: Why Spurs were BULLIED by Brentford: Inexperienced youngsters exposed, a pre-season tour that has caused Roberto De Zerbi a major headache and the surprising Sandro Tonali problem
Sports.content:
Why Spurs were BULLIED by Brentford: Inexperienced youngsters exposed, a pre-season tour that has caused Roberto De Zerbi a major headache and the surprising Sandro Tonali problem

The only positive Roberto De Zerbi could pick from the debris of defeat for Tottenham at Brentford was that now people might realise the extent of the rebuilding operation.

Time is required he says to create the necessary bonds between the new set of players. In fairness to him, he said something similar before the 3-0 humbling at the Gtech Community Stadium as well as afterwards.

When invited to declare a target for his new Spurs, on Friday, he resisted. Instead, he wanted to wait until transfer business was complete and his team had settled into a rhythm or – as he says – found its soul and organised its style.

Nobody however anticipated a defeat quite so emphatic. Not after the uptick in form at the end of last season. Not after a summer spent reinforcing defence and midfield at great expense.

Brentford simply bullied Spurs. They might easily have scored more, missed a penalty and in Mamadou Sangare, a midfielder signed from Lens for £41million, had the best of the summer signings on display.

Roberto De Zerbi warned that his Tottenham side were not yet ready for the new season

Callow Spurs

Despite a transfer policy based upon targeting experienced Premier League players, De Zerbi started the first game with four players aged 21 and under. Mikey Moore at 19, Lucas Bergvall at 20, Mathys Tel at 21 and Archie Gray, the youngest captain in the club’s history at 20 years and 163 days.

The Spurs boss then admitted the youthfulness of his team had been exposed by Brentford and that he feared the worst ahead of the game.

“At the beginning of the season, at the beginning of the new project, it was right to play with Lucas Bergvall,” said De Zerbi. “I knew before the game, Lucas, 20, in this type of game, maybe he could suffer more than Rodrigo Bentancur, nine years older.”

Bentancur came on at half time to replace Bergvall, who had missed a vital tackle, trying to roll his studs over the top of the ball deep in midfield, leading to Brentford’s second in the 33rd minute.

The backdrop is that Bentancur was late back into pre-season having been granted a delayed return from the World Cup, just as Pape Matar Sarr, injured and unavailable against Brentford, had been granted a delayed return from the World Cup.

De Zerbi's youthful team were badly exposed by Brentford in West London on Saturday

Undercooked Spurs

“We are not in the right point in physical condition for a lot of reasons,” said De Zerbi. “For the players who came late after the World Cup, because in Australia we couldn’t work in the right way for the trip and we don’t take risk with a lot of things but there are no excuses.”

The Spurs boss is mentioning the pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia quite regularly.

He noted on Friday how the injury keeping Micky van de Ven out at the start of the season had been picked up Down Under. “I don’t know, the flight,” said De Zerbi. “I don’t know, something, not a big problem, but not right to work.”

James Maddison, Dominic Solanke and Mateus Fernandes are among others to have their preseason schedule interrupted by injuries, none of them serious but enough to stall the fitness work De Zerbi considers imperative.

Minor irritations such as these can melt away if the team picks up results but they grow in significance after a defeat.

Either way, the idea of a tour in New Zealand and Australia hardly seemed like the brightest idea in a World Cup summer. Not one the head coach will sign off.

Expensive Spurs

Sandro Tonali, the club’s £100m record signing, was among three new signings namechecked by De Zerbi as ‘not in the best physical condition’, which came as a surprise because he was not at the World Cup and has played through pre-season.

Tonali was certainly underwhelming at Brentford. Unable to sustain the relentless tempo generated by the home team, unable to win possession, unable to get on the ball, unable to impose himself.

The Italian has been bought for an inflated fee to lead this midfield pack by example.

Bergvall struggled alongside him, as did Conor Gallagher, advanced as a No.10. The same trio looked very strong in a friendly against Hoffenheim only six days earlier, which is a reminder of the misleading nature of friendlies.

Both Gallagher and Bergvall were hooked at half-time. Spurs improved slightly in the last half hour with Bentancur and Mateus Fernandes on, but the game was lost and they were still second best.

No less worrying was that new centre-halves Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi were tormented in the air by Brentford’s towering front three of Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara.

And new No.1 keeper Toni Kinsky failed to command his penalty area at set pieces and must take a share of the blame for the second goal, pushing a shot by Mathias Jensen down to Vitaly Janelt.

Sandro Tonali is not yet match fit, which comes as a surprise, with the Italian not involved at the World Cup this summer

Toothless Spurs

Among the mistakes De Zerbi felt the need to single out was the timing of the press by teenage winger Moore in the first half.

Moore’s talent is not in question, he is the darling of the academy and the only Spurs player who looked like scoring on Saturday, forcing two excellent saves towards the end of the game.

But the comments seemed designed to stress that De Zerbi needs experience, players who are accustomed to the complex nature of Premier League football, especially work done off the ball.

In truth, none of the front three of Moore, Richarlison or Tel could hold up the ball in the first half and help carry their team up the pitch.

Singling out Moore felt like a nudge to the board because he, like Bergvall, is still learning his trade and Spurs need masters of their trade if they are going to compete at the top of the Premier League.

Whether Savinho, Omar Marmoush and Cody Gakpo fit into this category is open to question but De Zerbi clearly wants the transfer targets in as soon as possible.

Sports.title: Man United flop Paul Pogba slashes price of £3.95m mansion in England - complete with indoor football pitch - just as his contract is torn up at Monaco
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United star Paul Pogba has drastically cut the price of his five-bedroom Cheshire mansion amid his exit from AS Monaco. The midfielder has knocked £450,000 off the original asking price of £3.95million after struggles to offload the luxurious property. Pogba, 33, initially put the mansion on the market in 2024, two years after leaving United – following six years back at the club – and was looking to secure a healthy £1million profit on the home. However, with no buyers coming forward to purchase the property, the asking price was reduced to £3.5million earlier this month. The ex-France international bought the secluded, security-gated mansion in a cut-price deal himself back in 2017, a year after his record-breaking £89million return to Old Trafford from Juventus. Pogba oversaw a great change to the house, installing a 'unique' indoor football pitch and a cinema room. He also transformed the design of the open-plan living area, kitchen and bedrooms. Paul Pogba has slashed the price of his Cheshire mansion to £3.5million He has cut the price of the property amid his the termination of his contract at AS Monaco The 7,402-sq-ft property, situated in one of Cheshire's most affluent areas, also boasts a state-of-the-art gym and treatment room, but no longer features a swimming pool or sauna. In 2022, the house was burgled while his two children were asleep in their bedrooms as he played for United against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. In a statement after the burglary, Pogba stated that it was his 'family's worst nightmare' and that the intruders stole their 'sense of safety and security' during a raid that lasted less than five minutes. Pogba is currently without a club after his contract with the Monaco was terminated a year early following a series of injuries in pre-season. The midfielder had been trying to revive his career following an 18-month doping ban but only featured in six games last season while earning £44,000-a-week in the principality. Monaco confirmed on Wednesday that an agreement has been reached with Pogba to end his contract early. The Ligue 1 club praised the midfielder's 'unwavering determination' and 'utmost professionalism' during his spell. 'Having jointly concluded that the objectives initially set were only partially achieved, AS Monaco and Paul Pogba have decided, ahead of the first match of the new season, to bring an end to the contract that was due to run until June 2027,' a statement read. The luxurious 7,402-sq-ft property boasts an indoor football pitch at the heart of it The five-bedroom house situated in one of the most affluent areas of Cheshire was originally put up for sale in 2024 for £3.95million 'The Club would like to express its heartfelt gratitude to the 2018 FIFA World Cup winner for the trust he placed in the institution and for the utmost professionalism he demonstrated throughout his time in Monaco. 'During his spell in AS Monaco colours, Paul displayed a remarkable mindset, unwavering determination and the highest standards at every moment. 'Through all his efforts, he was able to return to top-level competition after a long period away from the game, while also sharing his experience and expertise with the first-team squad. 'AS Monaco sincerely thanks to Paul and wishes him every success in the future.' Daily Mail Sport understands Pogba was offered to MLS clubs last week, as he seeks his next venture in the sport. Pogba was cleared to return to football in March 2025 after having a four-year doping ban reduced to 18 months on appeal. He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in November 2024. The Frenchman was emotional when he signed for Monaco, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'. The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.' Pogba enjoyed two spells at United and made over 230 appearances for the club, scoring 39 times and providing 51 assists.

Sports.title: England's worst-behaved footballer is set to LEAVE the country: Championship manager confirms move to Italy is imminent for star after headbutting, biting and racism shame
Sports.content:
One of English football's most controversial characters is set to leave the country after agreeing a move to Serie A.

Preston North End's Milutin Osmajic - who has served bans for biting, headbutting, and alleged racial abuse - is on his way to Genoa according to manager Paul Heckingbottom.

The striker's reported £3million exit will be seen as a blow at the Lancashire club, where he remains popular despite his misdemeanours.

And Preston will need a replacement for their star striker quickly after losing their first two Championship matches against Bolton and Wolves. His exit is not fully confirmed but appears imminent after Heckingbottom said the deal was agreed.

Osmajic arrived as Preston's record signing for around £2.1m in September 2023 but quickly became known for his thuggery on the pitch.

In October 2024, he was handed an eight-game ban for biting Blackburn's Owen Beck on the neck the previous month in a 0-0 derby draw at Deepdale.

Milutin Osmajic is set to leave Preston North End after a string of controversial incidents

The striker - who once bit Blackburn's Owen Beck on the neck - is set to move to Genoa

Beck showed off his wound in the aftermath of that incident - but that was only the start

Montenegro international Osmajic left teeth marks on the shoulder of Rovers defender but escaped a red card at the time as referee Matt Donohue had not seen the incident.

Donohue actually sent off Beck, who had kicked out at Duane Holmes moments earlier.

In February 2025, he was accused of racially abusing Burnley midfielder Hannibal Mejbri during another goalless draw at Deepdale. He strongly refuted the allegation.

It took until November of that year for a decision to be reached, with the Football Association handing him a nine-game ban.

The Regulatory Commission also slapped him with a £21,000 fine and a mandatory education course.

Reports suggested that Hannibal had reported him for calling him a 'black man,' but his defenders insisted he had said 'f*** you, bad man'.

Preston took his side in the affair, saying they were 'extremely disappointed' at the ban and adding: 'We note that the outcome was determined on the 'Balance of Probabilities' rather than one that is 'Beyond Reasonable Doubt'.

Burnley players snubbed shaking hands with Osmajic before their FA Cup fifth-round tie two weeks later. Osmajic scored in the game and mocked Burnley fans in his celebration.

He was handed a nine-match ban after being accused of racism towards Hannibal Mejbri

The Montenegro international also headbuted Hull City's John Lundstram last season

'I will not be silent about what happened today,' Hannibal wrote on social media after the first match, in which the incident took place, on February 15. 'I will always call out racism whenever I hear or see it.

'That is the only way we change as a sport and a society. I am a strong person but nobody should have to experience this disgusting abuse on the pitch.'

Then, in January last season, he further sullied his reputation by headbutting Hull City's John Lundstram during a 3-0 defeat.

The forward initially pushed Lundstram away, leading to players from both sides and referee Stephen Martin running over to the pair.

Osmajic then headbutted Lundstram directly in front of the referee, with the official quick to reach for his pocket and show him a red card after leading him away from a crowd of players.

He was seen initially smiling following the dismissal, before raising his shirt to cover his face as he made his way off the field.

Osmajic was given a three-match ban for violent conduct. The incident contributed to a melee which saw one member of staff from each side being sent off.

Heckingbottom said in the aftermath: 'A lack of discipline is totally unacceptable. In my time here if he gets three games for that, it will have been 20 games missed.

'They are different issues, don't get me wrong, but a sending off for a tackle or something to help the team is a lot different.'

'He has not learned his lesson. The issues are totally unconnected in terms of football aren't they.

'In terms of other things, the word professional, we are professional people and footballers, there is a way to act.

'Whether that's a tackle on the pitch, discipline away from it, training ground, there is a way to be professional.'

Despite his flaws, Osmajic receives a lot of support from Preston fans and will leave the club with a record of 31 goals from 102 appearances.

Sports.title: Alan Shearer hits out at 'dreadful' Man United and claims Michael Carrick's side are 'not fit' after dismal opening day defeat by Hull City - as legend pinpoints the area stars 'offered nothing'
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer hits out at 'dreadful' Man United and claims Michael Carrick's side are 'not fit' after dismal opening day defeat by Hull City - as legend pinpoints the area stars 'offered nothing'

Alan Shearer has taken aim at Manchester United following their 'dreadful' performance at Hull City, with the Match of the Day pundit accusing Michael Carrick's side of lacking fitness.

The Red Devils wilted at newly-promoted Hull on Saturday, with goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy handing the newcomers a 2-0 victory.

The manner of United's defeat has caused alarm among supporters and pundits, with Shearer offering a withering verdict on the BBC's flagship football show on Saturday night.

'Man United were dreadful in all positions I thought, particularly upfront, they offered nothing,' he said. 'At times I struggled to work out what they were trying to do.

'[There is] so much to work on, so much to improve, I know it was the first game of the season but there was without a doubt a lack of energy, they just didn't look fit, Manchester United.

'There was only one team who were going to win that today from the very first minute, you saw the energy, you saw the intensity.

Alan Shearer has torn into Man United's opening day performance against Hull City

Man United put in a woeful display at Hull City to lose their opening game of the season

'That would be the worrying thing - you know that as a team going away from home to a newly promoted team, you know what you're going to get and you have to match them as a minimum and Man Utd didn't today. They couldn't live with them.'

The defeat at Hull was Carrick's first match in charge since being given the first-team head coach role on a permanent basis - having impressed during his interim tenure following the sacking of Ruben Amorim.

Carrick has refused to hit the panic button following Saturday's result.

'We haven't lost many games in six, seven months,' the United boss said.

'So again, I get it, we've lost today and I understand there's questions to be asked, but it doesn't mean everything's wrong because we've lost a game.

'We've done a lot of good things and we did some good things today, but it gets lost, and I understand it'll get lost, but it doesn't get lost from our point of view.

'There's definitely issues playing against different systems, so we have got to find the answers for that. But just because we lose one game it doesn't mean that everything needs to be dissected and it's wrong from our point of view.'

Carrick is rarely ruffled win, lose, or draw, but behind his calm demeanour here was a coach hurting at seeing his side totally outplayed.

Shearer claims United do not look fit as he sounded the alarm on Match of the Day

'I'm talking to you quite calm, but I'm not exactly calm inside and enjoying the day, you know?

'So there's a big difference. I played here for a long time. You don't get to play here for a long time without just going day by day, the results, the ups and downs, but you just carry on as normal. It's 100% not that; trust me, it's not that.

'It just doesn't mean that we all have to shout and scream and come out and create some chaos just because of it.

'Inside we're hurting. The boys know we need to get better, but the calmness doesn't mean that there's no emotion in it, for sure.'

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso backs 'world class' Cole Palmer to return to form this season and refuses to confirm if Robert Sanchez will be his starting keeper
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso backs 'world class' Cole Palmer to return to form this season and refuses to confirm if Robert Sanchez will be his starting keeper

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Xabi Alonso is determined to unlock the 'world class' side of Cole Palmer after Chelsea's playmaker suffered his first injury-plagued season to the detriment of his club.

The 2025-26 campaign saw Palmer struggle with a groin problem in particular but he also had other issues, including fracturing his little toe after stubbing it on a door at home. His limited influence contributed to Chelsea finishing 10th in the Premier League.

Before opening their campaign away at Fulham, Alonso spoke of how Palmer is pushing to avoid a recurrence of his previous injuries. 'Cole is determined to enjoy his football,' Chelsea's manager said. 'He wants to be fit. He wants to feel healthy.

'He wants to have a good connection with the players around him. We have this goal. If we are able to reach him and he feels that flow in the game and connects well with the players, I'm sure his level is top class, world class, and that he will have a great season.

Xabi Alonso is desperate to get the best out of Chelsea playmaker Cole Palmer this season

'Sometimes you need to go through a moment with an injury or whatever to learn from that.

'Cole has gone through a difficult period with an injury and now he's working really hard to have the prevention to not feel those symptoms back. Since the first day, he's been working really hard to avoid that.'

Chelsea's trip to Fulham last season saw Marc Cucurella dismissed after 22 minutes as the 10-man visitors lost 2-1. The Blues received eight red cards in 2025-26 – the most of any club in the Premier League as their campaign was plagued by poor discipline.

Alonso has fined players before at previous clubs and said when asked how he will respond to reds at Chelsea: 'It depends on the context. You can have a red card. It's football. It can happen. There is always a context for everything but I don't have written rules for this kind of thing.

'We need to assess the particular cases. But for sure, having emotional control gives you the game control that we want to avoid these kinds of situations.'

Robert Sanchez is expected to start in goal versus Fulham over Mike Penders, though Xabi Alonso refused to confirm that. 'We want healthy competition in all the positions,' Alonso said. 'We will see. The pitch is the boss of everything. I don't decide. The players need to show me.'

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City urgently need to find a 'new Rodri' this summer - as race to complete deals before Deadline Day heats up
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca admits Manchester City urgently need to find a 'new Rodri' this summer - as race to complete deals before Deadline Day heats up

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Maresca believes Manchester City can find ‘the new Rodri’ this month as they move on without their linchpin.

The Spain captain left for Barcelona last week, with City expected to wrap up a deal for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi during the transfer window.

With Elliot Anderson already signed, Maresca is confident that the new recruits can fill the void left by Rodri.

And Maresca pointed to the fact that the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner had never lifted major silverware before joining City in 2019 – underlining that they can mould signings into becoming the best in class.

‘Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri,’ Maresca said. ‘How do we solve the problem? Try to find the new Rodri.

‘Before he arrived, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. He joined the club then he achieved many important things.’

Enzo Maresca believes Man City can find their successor to Rodri by the end of this month

The Man City boss believes new recruits can fill the void left by the Spanish star

Rodri had made it clear that he wanted to leave the Etihad Stadium and Maresca has been unequivocal that any player eying a move away can depart, mirroring the principles of predecessor Pep Guardiola.

And the Italian claimed that life will move on, reeling off how City replaced previous big-name stars.

‘When Sergio [Aguero] was here, everyone was worried and Erling [Haaland] arrived,’ he added. ‘Fernandinho? Rodri arrived. It is just about this.

‘When they leave, you need to be good in recruiting the next one. They are all similar, David [Silva], Kevin [De Bruyne], Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling. It is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things.’

Meanwhile, Maresca confirmed that he is looking for a squad of around 20 outfield players. City currently have 19 senior players, excluding summer signing Jeremy Monga, but the number includes the likes of Tottenham target Omar Marmoush, Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez and Jack Grealish.

‘It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, that is for sure,’ Maresca added. ‘But we need to adapt. There are 10 days to go, hopefully we can do the things that we need to do.

‘The normal thing in the transfer window is that you have to wait until the last week, because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money. At the end, we’ll have all the squad here for sure it will be different.’

Sports.title: Carlos Baleba to undergo Man United medical TODAY as Crystal Palace slap down Jean-Philippe Mateta enquiry and Aston Villa agree terms with free agent Leon Goretzka: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Villa agree terms for Goretzka Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer. Pending a medical, the 31-year-old is expected to sign a three-year deal this week. Taylor Harwood-Bellis was left out of Southampton's squad to face Stoke City amid Villa's interest in the defender. Aston Villa have agreed terms with former Bayern Munich midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free transfer Villa have had an enquiry for Jean-Philippe Mateta knocked back by Crystal Palace. Unai Emery's team are hunting a centre-forward with Al-Hilal pushing hard to sign Ollie Watkins. Villa are also ready to bid for Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea. Watkins has also been offered a new deal at Villa. Napoli sign Chelsea star on loan Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy. The loan fee is worth £2.5million and could rise to £3.4m with add-ons. The option price is around £23m. Chelsea could receive more than £26m from the deal if Badiashile moves permanently. They valued him at £30m in this window. Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has joined Napoli on a loan deal, with an option to buy Napoli are also one of the clubs keen on Chelsea's Marc Guiu. He is weighing up options from Spain and Germany too. Hull City are exploring a loan for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo who is also wanted at Strasbourg. Wrexham eye up move for Millwall's Azeez Wrexham are exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez. The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City. The Robins are hoping the Nigeria international will be attracted by their ambitious project despite Millwall being rival promotion contenders. Wrexham are also looking at Ipswich Town attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti. The 25-year-old Albania international only joined in January from Bristol City for £3.5m and scored his first goal for the club against Wrexham. The move would mean him giving up the opportunity of Premier League football now though Wrexham hope to be there in a year's time. Meanwhile, Wrexham's move for free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe looks to be off. The exciting 25-year-old also has interest from Brighton and Hull City Brighton enquire about Hull target Hernandez Brighton have asked about Deportivo La Coruna winger Yeremay Hernandez. The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also. Hull owner Acun Ilicali said: 'We have to get the club side done and Yeremay also wants to come but it is a very vital, critical decision for himself. 'This deal is a very hard deal but we are somewhere where it looks positive. He is young boy and it would change his life completely so he wanted to see where he would come. We will see in three, four days if this deal will be done or not. If it happens it will be a record for sure.' Brighton remain in talks with Liverpool over the sale of winger Yankuba Minteh. Though the 22-year-old wants the move, the clubs are some distance apart on valuation with Brighton wanting over £70m to reflect market prices. The 23-year-old has been in the UK to talk to Hull City who have been trying to sign him but Brighton are exploring a move also Blues keep tabs on Conceicao amid interest in Neto Juventus winger Francisco Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto. Conceicao was bought from Porto for £36million and Juventus would want some profit on their outlay for the 23-year-old Portugal international. Neto has interest from Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea are asking £100m. They also have an offer from Roma for Jamie Gittens but so far that's too low, as a loan with option. Conceicao is quick, technically good and robust for his diminutive stature. Juventus would look to utilise any money from Conceicao for targets such as Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus winger Conceicao is back on Chelsesa's radar in case they sell Pedro Neto, with Al Hilal, Tottenham and Manchester City all interested in Neto Magpies reignite interest in Spurs' Gray Newcastle United have rekindled interest in Tottenham's versatile midfielder Archie Gray. The 20-year-old is still very much part of coach Roberto de Zerbi's plans as he can cover various positions though midfield is his preference. He has also captained the team during pre-season. Newcastle are speaking to Manchester City about Nico Gonzalez but Gray is also someone they admire. After losing so much quality they are exploring a number of options to strengthen their squad and add Premier League experience. Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield. Tottenham will need to consider sales to offset their substantial summer spending, though they would prefer to sell others. Gray is valued over £60m. Since joining Spurs from Leeds for £40million, Gray has made 81 appearances, often filling in at centre-back and right-back as well as midfield and has captained the side during pre-season Joao Pedro signs eight-year Blues contract Joao Pedro has signed his new Chelsea contract until 2034. Chelsea have been determined to keep the Brazil international after he emerged as a target for Barcelona early in the summer. The Brazil international joined the Blues from Brighton in July 2025 and made an immediate impact, scoring in the Club World Cup semi-final and final as Chelsea were crowned world champions. His form continued into his first full season at Stamford Bridge, with the forward scoring 20 goals in all competitions. While the club are willing to listen to offers for Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson, the 24-year-old was named Chelsea's new No 9 last week. Joao Pedro said: 'I am very happy to sign a new contract with Chelsea. I always dreamed of playing for a big club, and it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club. 'Everyone is very excited for this season. We know we can achieve a lot of things. We have a great team, we have a coach who wants to win and has won already.' Joao Pedro, who has signed a fresh eight-year deal at Chelsea, said: 'I always dreamed of playing for a big club, it means a lot to me to give my long-term commitment to this club' Baleba prepares for Man United medical Carlos Baleba is due to undergo his medical today ahead of completing his £70million move from Brighton to Manchester United. The 22-year-old is recovering from an ankle ligament injury but is expected to be fit towards the end of next month. The deal was agreed early on Friday evening at £65m plus add-ons and a sell-on clause. Newcastle target given the green light for move Newcastle target Nico Gonzalez has been told by Enzo Maresca and Hugo Viana that he can leave Manchester City. Gonzalez was ready to fight for his place but with City looking to sign two more midfielders they are realistic about his prospects of playing regularly. Newcastle believe he is open to the move and is emerging as their priority on a shortlist of three targets. Nico Gonzalez has been told that he can move from Man City amid interest from Newcastle Newcastle have also registered interest in Christopher Nkunku of AC Milan, though RB Leipzig are more active on the situation as it stands. Man City's talks for Ayyoub Bouaddi are continuing, though Lille have been pushing for optimum price on the 18-year-old. Man City forward Omar Marmoush is still expected to complete his move to Tottenham. Liverpool fledgling books Levente loan deal Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is joining Levante on loan. The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England as yet, so is having to be loaned out to play competitive football. The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future. First team football in a top league such as LaLiga is viewed as an integral next step. He has travelled to Valencia to complete terms. Ndukwe also had interest from clubs in Portugal, France and Germany. City defender to join Coventry Manchester City defender Stephen Mfuni is in talks to join Coventry City on loan. The 18-year-old, who can play left back and centre back, was a target for Watford who had him on loan last season. Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney blasts one Man Utd star for 'schoolboy' level in Hull embarrassment

Manchester United were beaten 2-0 by Hull City on the opening day of the Premier League season, with Wayne Rooney left fuming at Luke Shaw's defending in particular

View Image Luke Shaw has been blasted for his 'schoolboy' error by Wayne Rooney (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Wayne Rooney has taken aim at Luke Shaw's defending against Hull City, labelling it 'schoolboy' after the left‑back came under scrutiny for his part in Manchester United's 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. First‑half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy earned the newly‑promoted side all three points.

‌



United were strong favourites on the opening day but were rocked when Hull struck in the 17th minute. The hosts started with real intent, forcing Senne Lammens into a series of early saves - including keeping out a dangerous header from Oli McBurnie at the far post.

‌



From the resulting corner, McBurnie’s effort was stopped, but Ajayi reacted quickest to smash in the rebound. Hull then doubled their advantage shortly afterwards from a free‑kick.

‌



Man Utd fans think they've discovered reason for Hull defeat as comments resurface READ MORE :

Micah Richards has told Sky Sports and BBC of retirement plan with Roy Keane set to quit first READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Regan Slater delivered a pinpoint ball for Mendy, whose header effectively killed the contest. Rooney was particularly unhappy with Shaw’s positioning for the second goal, criticising him for dropping too deep and playing Hull’s entire forward line onside.

Speaking on BBC's Match of the Day, the former United captain said: "[Ayden] Heaven is with [Oli] McBurnie, Ajayi is with [Bryan] Mbeumo. Heaven loses his player, it's a really good save by Lammens and there's no reaction [from Mbeumo] and they go 1-0 down - it's a very difficult game from there. This really sums it up for me from Hull's perspective.

‌



"They get the ball out wide and then [Patrick] Dorgu and Shaw, you've got a decision who goes [to press the ball]. [Youri] Tielemans is covering the runner, I think Shaw should go and press the ball, but he doesn't. He allows Dorgu to go and try to press the ball, he doesn't get close enough.

"The ball comes in the box and United clear it. Hull come alive and win the second ball. [Ryan] Giles on the other side, the ball goes out. Mbeumo doesn't get out quick enough, allows the ball to come into the box, it gets cleared again. Hull pick up the second ball again, there's no intensity, no pressing on the ball [from Mbeumo]."

‌



Rooney added: "Now [Mohamed] Belloumi comes and gets on the ball, Tielemans, who's probably fed up, he's seen the ball going from side to side, get headed out, not pick up second balls - gives away a free-kick, which leads to the second goal. And this is schoolboy defending from Shaw.

"Man United have a good line, and Hull have been waiting for this all day. Shaw drops in, he's five yards behind his back line, and if this ball is good enough - which it was - it's impossible to stop. So Hull had a game plan: get the ball in the box and pick up second balls, and Man United found it really difficult."

The Reds' head coach, Michael Carrick, showed his disappointment but insisted his side did 'a lot of good things' during their outing at Hull. "You know, we came here to win as we do in any game so to not take anything away is hugely disappointing," he said after the game.

‌



"We haven't lost many games in six, seven months. So again, I get it, we've lost today, and I understand there are questions to be asked, but it doesn't mean everything's wrong because we've lost a game. We've done a lot of good things and we did some good things today, but it gets lost, and I understand it'll get lost, but it doesn't get lost from our point of view.

"So yeah, there's definitely issues playing against different systems, you know. So we've got to find the answers for that, but it's just because we lost one game doesn't mean that everything needs to be dissected and it's wrong from our point of view. I understand from others, it happens, and that's how it is."

Sports.title: Man City eye Rodri replacement as Enzo Maresca highlights successful transfer plan
Sports.content:
Man City eye Rodri replacement as Enzo Maresca highlights successful transfer plan

Manchester City have already signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest this summer but it appears that Enzo Maresca still wants more additions ahead of the transfer window closing

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca has hinted more signings could be on the way at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca has underlined his desire to find the ‘next Rodri’ ahead of next month’s transfer deadline. The Spanish midfielder left Manchester City earlier this week in a big-money switch to Barcelona.

‌



It brought to an end a glittering seven-year spell for Rodri at the Etihad Stadium, where he helped the club to numerous Premier League titles, the Champions League, as well as claiming the Ballon d’Or for himself.

‌



City have already made a big-money addition in the heart of midfield with a £116million move for England star Elliot Anderson. But it appears that they are not done there, with talks underway with Lille for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

‌



Regardless of who is drafted in, Maresca has suggested that they are looking for someone with a similar profile to Rodri. And while the City boss is aware of the enormity of that task, he believes it’s something that they’ve managed to navigate before.

"How do we solve that problem?" asked Maresca. "We try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is.

‌



"[Before] Rodri arrived here, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. He joined the club then he achieved many important things."

Maresca added: "I was thinking on Thursday night, when David Silva was here, everyone was worried and Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio [Aguero] was here, everyone was worried [when he was going to leave] and Erling [Haaland] arrived. Fernandinho? Rodri arrived.

"When they leave, you need to be good in recruiting the next one. They are all similar, David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Erling - there is one more - it is normal, it is change, it is not a problem, go again and try to do the right things."

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City have been linked with Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi (Image: Getty Images)

Away from signings, there could also be more outgoings at the Etihad over the coming days. Savinho and Omar Marmoush are both on the verge of joining Premier League rivals Tottenham Hotspur in a double deal worth around £140m.

Should those moves be completed, the pair would join a number of high-profile players leaving the club. Tijjani Reijnders has departed for Saudi Arabian side Al-Qadsiah, while James Trafford, Nathan Ake, Bernardo Silva and John Stones have all followed former boss Pep Guardiola out of the door.

Sports.title: Josh Tarling makes heartbreaking Vuelta admission a week after brother's cycling death
Sports.content:
Josh Tarling makes heartbreaking Vuelta admission a week after brother's cycling death

Josh Tarling was in action at La Vuelta a Espana just days after his brother and fellow professional cyclist Fin Tarling died in a collision during the Volta a Portugal

View 2 Images Josh Tarling put in an outstanding performance at La Vuelta just days after his brother died (Image: Eurosport)

Josh Tarling confessed his remarkable Vuelta a España opening stage performance held little significance for him in the wake of losing his brother and fellow professional cyclist Fin Tarling. The display came mere days after Fin's heartbreaking death during the Volta a Portugal last week.

‌



Fin, 19, was killed in a high-speed crash with a van during the eighth stage of the race last Friday. The vehicle had made its way onto the course ahead of the incident, under the impression the cyclists had already passed.

‌



Josh chose to race in the Vuelta despite the heartbreaking news, to occupy his mind while grieving. The 22-year-old Netcompany Ineos rider took his place on the start line for the three-week Grand Tour and delivered a stunning opening day showing.

‌



Cycling star Kim Le Court soars to stunning stage three victory at Lloyds Tour of Britain READ MORE :

Sprint superstar Lorena Wiebes sparkles in Blackpool to grab second Lloyds Tour of Britain stage victory READ MORE :

The rider battled his way into the lead with a superb effort before being forced to watch as Ethan Hayter and then Tour de France winner Tadej Pogacar edged past him by the finest of margins. The Welshman came up just four seconds shy of Pogacar's victorious time.

However, following last week's heartbreaking news, the outcome held little meaning for Josh, who was embraced by Pogacar on the podium at the conclusion of the first stage.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



When questioned about what the ride meant to him, he told Eurosport: "Not a lot. No, I'm happy with it. And I'm happy I could try and get my head busy with other stuff.

"So yeah, obviously I'm happy and I'm thankful for the team and everything, to let me come and let me give it a good crack."

Legendary Welsh cyclist and Netcompany Ineos' racing director Geraint Thomas said he couldn't be prouder of him. Thomas described Tarling's grief as 'unimaginable', and said that the team would do their utmost to provide a sense of normality to help him through the coming three weeks.

‌



"For a start, it's just great to have him here," Thomas told TNT Sport. "You know, he was really keen to ride, he just wanted to get back to the day job, so to speak, and find comfort in the process and being around the team and everything being as normal as possible. So we fully backed him with that and it's great to have him here.

View 2 Images Joshua Tarling finished third on stage one of La Vuelta (Image: Laurent Coust / Europa Press via Getty Images)

"Obviously, it's been unimaginable what he's gone through the last week or so. But to put in a performance like that at the end of the week he's had is just fantastic, really, it just shows the class of him as an athlete and as a person. Couldn't be prouder.

‌



"I think the course suited him. Technically, he's one of the best and I think yesterday was probably the first time he's ridden a bike properly in a while, so to still put that in? It's insane, really.

"We'll just continue to be normal around him and support him as best we can. It's the start of hopefully a great trip for these eight boys on the bus."

‌



Josh's participation in Ineos' squad had the full backing of his family. "On Saturday Joshua will be riding the Vuelta," his mother Dawn posted on Instagram.

"He has chosen to do so in honour of his brother Fin, with the full support of his family, surrounded by a team who have been incredibly supportive of whatever decision he made.

"I could not have wished for two boys who were closer growing up and into adulthood we have watched with pride as Joshua has been the most loving and supportive big brother to Fin. Following this devastating news he has been an incredible strength for us all.
