Sports.title: Why Honda's new F1 engine comes with fresh but expected driveability issues
Sports.content:
Aston Martin Formula 1 driver Fernando Alonso says more work is needed to optimise Honda's more powerful engine after struggling to keep his car on the track in sprint qualifying at Zandvoort.

Alonso and team-mate Lance Stroll have received the second specification of Honda's V6 power unit, with the Japanese manufacturer having earmarked the Netherlands as the site to deploy its one in-season engine upgrade this year.

The engine was shaken down during a filming day after the Hungarian Grand Prix at the end of July, but while running the new unit in anger both drivers encountered fresh driveability issues on Friday in Zandvoort.

Alonso went off in Turn 1 during SQ1, complaining of heavy vibrations from the engine before qualifying 22nd and last, three seconds off the pace. Stroll fared little better, getting ahead of both Cadillac cars but still ending the day a distant 19th.

"Free practice was more or less okay but in qualifying we had problems on the engine," Alonso reported. "Driveability was pushing on the braking, so it was difficult to stop the car sometimes because the engine was over-delivering.

"And then apparently the SLM mode [the lower drag setting on the 2026 car] didn't work for me so I could not open the rear wing. A combination of both made the laps very tricky.

"When you brake and the throttle is open, it's difficult to stop the car."

Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Stroll similarly grappled with the behaviour of his new power unit: "We were struggling with the driveability, and there were a few other things that weren’t quite right, so we need to understand why.

"It’s really windy out there, but it’s the same for everyone. We’ll go through everything tonight, look at the data, and try to make some improvements for tomorrow.”

Honda's homework starts over

On the surface Friday's performance feels like a puzzling step backwards for Aston Martin and Honda after its huge Hungary car upgrade moved the Silverstone squad back into the heart of F1's midfield.

But Honda had already calculated that bringing the new power unit would mean that a lot of the work the Japanese brand did at the start of the season to improve its subpar driveability would have to be largely re-done for the latest specification.

"We developed our tools to optimise our driveability. We have made good progress, and we were close to what we wanted to achieve," Honda's F1 project leader Shintaro Orihara told Autosport in a wide-ranging interview.

"But when we introduce the spec 2 engine, the combustion characteristics will change. There will be a big difference.

"And then engine behaviour will be changed in the cornering phase as well, so we need to develop our driveability again."

Sports.title: The advice Marquez gave Hadjar over his wrist injury
Sports.content:
Isack Hadjar misses this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix after sustaining a wrist injury during a gym session last week. According to Racing Bulls CEO Peter Bayer, Red Bull’s sister team was informed on Friday of a potential driver change, with the situation developing further on Tuesday.

That was when Yuki Tsunoda was called up – having been on a beach in Greece when he was asked to step in – while Liam Lawson was handed another opportunity at Red Bull following his demotion after the 2025 Chinese Grand Prix.

Read Also: Formula 1 The full circle moment given to Lawson at the 2026 Dutch GP

While the situation naturally presents opportunities for both drivers, it is highly frustrating for Hadjar, who nevertheless made an appearance in the Zandvoort paddock on Friday morning.

Hadjar claimed his maiden F1 podium in the Netherlands last year and had planned to reference that achievement with a playful nod in a special helmet design this year.

Red Bull and Marquez in agreement: Take your time to recover

Hadjar – as you might expect from any athlete – wanted to go racing again straight away, but he has been advised by two different parties not to take any risks and to sit out the Dutch GP.

First of all, that message came from Red Bull. Laurent Mekies confirmed that his team did not want to take any risks with Max Verstappen's team-mate, who has performed surprisingly well this year.

Hadjar had planned a special helmet design for this weekend, inspired by Delft blue pottery and his broken trophy from last year Photo by: Red Bull Content Pool

"Isack is alright," Mekies told the official F1 website. "We have no reason to take any risk with him. He has done a fantastic start of the season, he has been stronger and stronger every time he has been driving this car out of the garage, session after session, weekend after weekend.

"We take zero risk, we let him sort out the recovery this weekend, and hopefully we’ll have him very, very quickly [back] in the car."

The advice to skip Zandvoort also came from another, more surprising source: seven-time MotoGP world champion Marc Marquez.

The Ducati rider and Hadjar share the same physiotherapist, Carlos J. Garcia. Hadjar called Marquez after sustaining the wrist injury, with the Spaniard advising him not to rush his return.

The rider currently fourth in the MotoGP standings also urged Hadjar not to rush into certain medical procedures, given that the Frenchman is still young and has a long F1 career ahead of him.

Marquez therefore felt that taking his time and recovering properly was the most sensible approach for Hadjar, which is exactly what Red Bull had already told the youngster.

Marquez himself has plenty of first-hand experience when it comes to injuries. The MotoGP icon has, among other things, broken his right upper arm and right thumb, dislocated both shoulders and suffered from diplopia.

Marquez is known for returning quickly after injury, but advised Hadjar to do the opposite Photo by: Qian Jun / MB Media via Getty Images

When can Hadjar return for Red Bull?

The key question, of course, is when Hadjar will be able to return behind the wheel of the RB22.

When asked by Autosport, Red Bull said it is still too early to provide an official update on that, although the plan is to have him back in the car at Monza for the Italian GP in two weeks' time.

"It's too early to say that definitely, but it’s our target to have him back in Monza," Mekies told Sky Sports Germany.

The Italian GP will take place on the weekend of 4-6 September. Although the iconic circuit in Monza's park is certainly not the most physically demanding track on the calendar, the Spanish GP at the new Madring follows just one week later.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Russell takes pole in tight sprint qualifying with Antonelli fifth
Sports.content:
George Russell has taken pole position for the Dutch Grand Prix sprint race with Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli down in fifth.

The Mercedes driver pipped reigning world champion Lando Norris by only 0.041s to take his third sprint pole of the 2026 season.

Russell’s pole came particularly out of the blue after topping neither SQ1 or SQ2 - respectively done by Charles Leclerc and Oscar Piastri - but a 1m11.567s in the final session was enough.

It was a very tight final session too, as third-placed Leclerc was just 0.055s off the pace for Ferrari with Norris’ McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri in fourth and 0.099s behind Russell.

A slightly bigger gap then emerged to Russell’s team-mate Antonelli though, who was 0.227s behind the Briton and suffering floor damage from an off at the penultimate corner in SQ1.

Precisely three tenths behind Antonelli was Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in sixth, one spot ahead of seventh-placed Lewis Hamilton who struggled in the sister Ferrari with a 0.624s gap to Russell.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

Alpine’s Pierre Gasly, Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto and Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad respectively rounded out the top 10 at Zandvoort ahead of Saturday’s shortened race.

It was a respectable Red Bull return for Liam Lawson, who has replaced the injured Isack Hadjar, as he qualified 11th after being eliminated by his usual team-mate Lindblad.

“I have no idea what happened,” reported the New Zealander, who was four tenths off SQ3, and will share the sixth row with his Racing Bulls stand-in and F1 returnee Yuki Tsunoda.

Franco Colapinto will be on the seventh row in 13th, shared with 14th-placed Nico Hulkenberg, while Esteban Ocon and Alex Albon respectively rounded out the SQ2 drop zone.

In SQ1 a late improvement from Oliver Bearman put him 17th and one spot above Williams man Carlos Sainz, who was pushed into the elimination zone by Bearman’s Haas team-mate Ocon.

The last four spots were occupied by the usual suspects: Aston Martin’s Lance Stroll in 19th, Cadillac duo Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez 20th and 21st and Fernando Alonso in 22nd.

Alonso particularly struggled as he locked up at Turn 1 and finished last despite a tow from a Cadillac and it was later confirmed that the Straight Line Mode on his rear wing didn’t work.

F1 Dutch GP - Sprint Qualifying results

Sports.title: Rolly Romero Demands Teofimo Lopez Rematch
Sports.content:
“It’s like I never get a fair shake. It’s apparent. I clearly outboxed the dude that’s supposed to be one of the best boxers. He’s an Olympian and all this stuff. I clearly outboxed him. I cut him. I hurt him multiple times. It’s clear as day. I deserve a rematch,” said Romero at the post-fight press conference.

Regarding the verdict, Romero placed no personal blame on Lopez. He referred to Teofimo as his “little brother,” noting that their embrace before the 12th round reflected genuine friendship. He directed his frustration entirely at the officials, calling the scoring “political.”

The former champion stated one of the punches that stunned Lopez should have produced a knockdown. He also claimed Teofimo was badly shaken by another shot near the end of a round, surviving only because the bell saved him before Romero could finish the job.

Without a contractual clause in place, Romero remains dependent on Teofimo and the promoters agreeing to negotiate again. He maintains that the tight margin on the official cards justifies another look.

“Of course, I am owed a rematch. You don’t get a 114-114, 115-113 and not get a rematch.”

Rolly’s case is weakened by his own admission that he could have applied more pressure. While he landed the more damaging punches, prolonged inactivity allowed Teofimo to collect close rounds without taking major risks. That passivity may have cost Romero his belt. Feeling aggrieved will not guarantee him another opportunity, especially with other contenders pursuing Lopez, but the narrow scoring leaves him with a legitimate claim.

Sports.title: Hearn Says Anthony Joshua Contract Has Already Been Breached
Sports.content:
“What they want to do is they want to pay Anthony Joshua less money because that’s how it will work out with the difference in location. They want him to do a load of additional stuff. I’m not going to blow things up, which I could do so easily, but there has been breaches in AJ’s contract already which we’ve let slide because these guys are our partners and our friends, or were,” said Hearn.

Correcting “are” to “were” when describing the organizers as friends shows how badly the relationship has deteriorated. Hearn’s position is that Joshua signed for a British event and cannot be blamed for refusing to accept less money and additional duties merely because the preferred location changed.

Much of his anger was directed at a leaked Matchroom email containing a list of unresolved issues. Hearn believes it was deliberately circulated to journalists and falsely presented as Joshua’s demands for agreeing to fight in America.

None of the items in that email were included in the addendum Matchroom submitted for the proposed US move, he said. In Hearn’s view, the leak was intended to support Fury’s accusation that Joshua and Matchroom were being greedy and holding up the fight.

There were also claims that some people were financially encouraged to repost Fury’s version of events. Hearn offered no evidence during the press conference, so that allegation remains entirely his account. Still, anyone reading an alleged list of new demands without knowing it came from a separate email would naturally conclude that Joshua was asking for more.

The dispute extends to Dana White. Hearn says the agreement excludes TKO and Zuffa from promoting the event, despite White publicly identifying himself as its promoter. Nick Khan contacted Hearn about finding a way for TKO to participate, but White’s public approach had damaged those talks.

Time is nearly gone. The coming week was described as the deadline for preserving the proposed November date. Netflix needs time to promote the event, while Madison Square Garden may release the date and book something else. Joshua remains committed to fighting Fury, but the argument over location, money, and promotional control must be resolved within days.

Sports.title: Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory
Sports.content:
During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Catterall Threatens Teofimo Lopez’s Big-Money Welterweight Plans
Sports.content:
A majority decision over Rolando Romero at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas gave Lopez the belt. His steady pressure, jab and body work earned scores of 116-112 and 115-113, while the third judge returned a 114-114 card.

Watching from outside the ring, Catterall made his opinion clear on social media.

“I beat either of these pair no doubt in my mind,” said Catterall on X about Teofimo and Rolly.

That confidence is not difficult to understand after Lopez’s welterweight debut. Romero spent long stretches moving backward and waiting for one power counter. His low output allowed Lopez to win rounds through activity without producing a dominant offensive performance.

When Romero finally attacked in the fifth, he hurt Teofimo with a left hand and opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Lopez recovered and regained control, but he never seriously hurt Romero despite landing the cleaner punches for much of the fight.

A more difficult test comes from Catterall. The British southpaw will not concede as many quiet rounds. His timing, counters and disciplined defense can disrupt Teofimo’s lead hand and force him to reset before attacking. He also has the patience to punish the wide punches Teofimo throws when he becomes frustrated.

The WBA ordered its Super champion to face the winner of Jack Catterall vs. Shakhram Giyasov within 180 days of their May 23 bout. Catterall won that fight and holds the secondary WBA welterweight title, placing him next in line for a consolidation bout. The period ends on November 19, although the WBA has not issued a new public order naming Lopez since he defeated Romero. The original WBA ruling established the timetable.

The cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow may delay the consolidation fight. November 19 is less than three months away, leaving limited time for the wound to heal before he resumes sparring and completes another camp. His team can request a medical extension if contact training places the cut at risk of reopening. Any added time would only postpone the obligation unless Catterall accepts a step-aside agreement or the WBA grants Lopez permission to take another fight. That delay may allow Lopez’s team to pursue Garcia, Benn or Haney.

Less money and greater risk make Catterall an opponent Teofimo has little reason to welcome. Based on Saturday’s performance, Lopez will need more than steady pressure and a busy jab against a disciplined southpaw who will make him pay for every mistake.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Defeats Rolly Romero, Captures WBA Title
Sports.content:
That was Romero’s best stretch of the fight. Lopez recovered in the sixth and resumed moving forward behind his jab while attacking the body. Although the cut began bleeding again late in the contest, he continued outworking a champion who spent too much time waiting for isolated counterpunching opportunities.

Needing a strong finish, Romero remained cautious during the 12th. Lopez stayed on the front foot and completed the fight as the busier boxer. The victory raised his record to 23-2 with 13 knockouts, while Romero dropped to 17-3 with 13 stoppages.

Gary Antonio Russell Takes Santillan’s Interim Belt

A dominant unanimous decision over Victor Santillan gave Gary Antonio Russell the interim WBA super bantamweight title. Scores were 119-108 twice and 118-109.

Superior speed, a sharp jab and faster combinations allowed Russell to control the fight. The matchup between two southpaws produced frequent clinches, but Russell consistently landed the cleaner punches whenever space opened between them.

A right hook to the top of the head dropped Santillan during the 12th round. He beat referee Robert Hoyle’s count and held repeatedly to survive until the final bell. Russell moved to 22-1 with 13 knockouts, while Santillan fell to 16-3 with seven stoppages.

Hernandez Receives Majority Decision Over Veron

A majority decision over Francisco Daniel Veron gave Yoenli “El Diablo” Hernandez the victory in their 10-round middleweight bout. Two judges scored it widely for Hernandez at 99-91 and 98-92, while the third returned a surprising 95-95 card.

Heavier and more accurate punches gave Hernandez control during the opening rounds, while Veron tried to compensate with pressure and a high work rate. Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes.

The Cuban regained control by attacking the body and landing right hands and uppercuts. Veron continued advancing and throwing through the final bell, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Utria Edges Mercado By Split Decision

A disputed split decision over Israel “Bad Ways” Mercado kept Carlos Utria’s perfect record intact after their 10-round light welterweight fight. Scores were 96-94 for Utria, 96-94 for Mercado and 97-93 for Utria.

Much of the early action belonged to Utria before Mercado closed the fourth with a combination. The fight remained close through the middle rounds, with neither boxer establishing a lasting advantage.

Strong work during the ninth carried Mercado into a decisive final round. He believed he had done enough to win, and sections of the crowd expressed their displeasure when Utria was announced as the victor.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell In First

A sustained attack from Marco Romero forced a first-round stoppage against Kahlil “Killa” Mitchell in their scheduled eight-round bout.

Unable to defend himself, Mitchell was trapped as Romero unloaded a combination during the final minute. Referee Allen Huggins stopped the contest at 2:33.

Johnson Decisions Rodriguez

A six-round decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez gave Benjamin Johnson another welterweight victory. Johnson moved to 8-0 with seven knockouts, while Rodriguez dropped to 4-4-1.

Tony Weeks served as the referee.

Brown Sweeps Wiggins Over Six Rounds

Every round went to Joseph “The Prodigy” Brown in a slow six-round middleweight contest against Alton Wiggins. All three judges scored the fight 60-54.

Cleaner punches separated Brown from Wiggins, whose frequent holding prevented the exchanges from developing. The same pattern continued through the sixth.

Blancas Drops Mamone, Wins Decision

A knockdown helped Aldo Blancas secure a unanimous decision over Ricky Mamone in their four-round light welterweight bout. Scores were 39-36 twice and 40-35.

A left hook to the body from Blancas produced a delayed knockdown late in the second. Mamone beat referee John McCarthy’s count and continued despite bleeding from the nose during the third.

Unable to secure the stoppage, Blancas settled for the decision after Mamone survived the final round.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Wins Third Belt As Rolando Romero Barely Fights
Sports.content:
Romero’s strategy depended almost entirely on catching Lopez as he moved inside. That opportunity arrived in the fifth round when a left hand opened a cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow and hurt him. Romero followed with a flurry and had the challenger under pressure as “Rolly” chants spread through the arena.

It should have changed the fight. Instead, Romero returned to waiting.

Lopez recovered in the sixth, reestablished his jab and resumed attacking the body. Blood continued leaking from the cut during the later rounds, but it never prevented him from moving forward or maintaining his output. Romero landed isolated counters without putting enough punches behind them to take control.

The champion’s corner urged him to hold the center of the ring before the final round. He continued moving away and never produced the desperate attack required from a fighter in danger of losing his belt. By then, the crowd had grown restless after repeatedly waiting for Romero to open up.

Lopez deserves credit for remaining disciplined after being hurt. He avoided turning the fight into the reckless exchange Romero needed, kept scoring with straightforward work and closed the championship rounds on the front foot. The performance was controlled rather than destructive, with Lopez winning through activity, positioning and better decision-making.

His welterweight debut also raised a question about his punching power at 147 pounds. Lopez landed plenty of clean shots but never seriously hurt Romero. That may become important against the stronger and more active fighters in the division.

Still, Lopez accomplished what he came to Las Vegas to do. He won a title in a third weight class, while Romero surrendered his belt through passivity after finding the punch that briefly gave him a chance to take over the fight.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Beats Franciso Veron, But Draw Card Stuns
Sports.content:
Early confidence led the Cuban to lower his hands, pose and attack with wide power shots. He controlled the distance when he used his jab and footwork, then punished Veron with right hands, uppercuts and combinations to the body whenever the Argentine moved inside.

Veron’s persistence created one dangerous moment. A check hook late in the fifth round caught Hernandez cleanly, briefly wobbling him and forcing him toward the ropes. It was the clearest round for Veron and a reminder that Hernandez was taking unnecessary chances against an opponent who refused to retreat.

The favorite responded by tightening his defense and resuming his body attack. Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the eighth, followed with uppercuts and continued landing the stronger punches through the championship rounds. Veron absorbed the punishment and kept throwing, but his aggression rarely produced clean scoring shots.

That inability to secure the stoppage will give Hernandez something to study. He had the size, power and technical advantage, yet spent too much time looking for single explosive punches instead of breaking Veron down with sustained combinations. His performance was convincing without being the destructive statement his team likely wanted.

None of that explains the draw score. Hernandez clearly won more than five rounds, and the 95-95 card turned an otherwise straightforward result into an unnecessary controversy. The two wide scores properly reflected a fight controlled by Hernandez, even if Veron’s toughness forced him to work until the final bell.

Sports.title: Rolando Romero vs Teofimo Lopez Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 12

An unusual embrace opened the final round as the challenger whispered something to Romero before being pushed away. Lopez then resumed pressing forward and kept the champion from producing the desperate attack he needed.

Romero’s corner instructed him to hold the center of the ring, but he continued moving away and never forced a sustained exchange. Lopez closed the fight with greater activity and control, completing what should be a wide decision victory.

10-9 Lopez, 118-110 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 11

The challenger continued pressing behind his jab despite blood dripping from the cut over his right eye. Romero opened with a right to the body, added a shovel hook and later connected with another clean right hand.

Those isolated punches were not accompanied by enough urgency. Romero spent much of the round circling away before both fighters traded near the bell. Lopez’s higher output and forward pressure earned him another round, leaving the champion needing a knockout in the 12th.

10-9 Lopez, 108-101 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 10

Another slow round favored the challenger, who continued attacking the body and landed a clean right hand upstairs. He remained busier and controlled the range despite the cut over his right eye beginning to bleed again.

Romero increased his jab slightly but continued retreating and failed to apply the pressure needed to change the fight. The champion’s cautious approach cost him another round despite having much of the crowd behind him.

10-9 Lopez, 98-92 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 9

An early attempt by the champion to move forward produced little offense. Lopez quickly resumed control behind his jab, worked the body and maintained the distance while operating comfortably from the front foot.

Long stretches passed without a meaningful exchange as Romero kept his hands low and waited for counters that never developed. The earlier “Rolly” chants faded, and the crowd became restless with the champion’s passive approach.

10-9 Lopez, 88-83 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 8

Greater activity allowed the challenger to control another round. He moved forward behind combinations, landed clean hooks upstairs and blocked many of Romero’s counters before answering with punches of his own.

Romero continued picking isolated moments to exchange but remained too cautious to match Lopez’s output. The cut over Lopez’s right eye stayed under control as he extended his lead with cleaner and more consistent work.

10-9 Lopez, 78-74 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 7

Steady pressure from the challenger forced Romero to spend much of the round moving laterally and looking for counters. Both landed right hands early before Lopez attacked the body with a flurry. One punch strayed low and brought a warning from the referee.

Romero connected with a left hook at the bell that appeared to wobble Lopez. The late punch gave the champion another dangerous moment, but Lopez’s activity and control over most of the round narrowly earned it.

10-9 Lopez, 68-65 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 6

The challenger regained his composure after being hurt in the fifth and returned to applying pressure behind the jab. Working patiently from long range allowed him to control the distance and slow the pace.

Romero looked for counters but could not build on his success from the previous round. Lopez’s disciplined boxing and greater activity steadied the fight and secured the sixth.

10-9 Lopez, 58-56 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 5

The champion produced his strongest round yet, hurting Lopez with a left hand that opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Romero followed with a flurry and hurt him again with about a minute remaining.

Lopez answered late as the fighters exchanged punches and words, but Romero’s power and increased activity created the first major change in the fight. Chants of “Rolly” spread through T-Mobile Arena as the challenger finished the round under pressure.

10-9 Romero, 48-47 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 4

A stronger stand from the champion produced his best round of the fight. Several left hands connected cleanly, including one that briefly disrupted Lopez’s balance. The challenger continued pressing forward, but the sharper counters interrupted his rhythm and prevented him from controlling the exchanges.

Lopez’s activity kept the round competitive, although the more meaningful punches came from Romero.

10-9 Romero, 39-37 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 3

Teo continued moving forward, although Romero showed more willingness to hold his position and engage. Neither fighter landed a damaging punch as much of the action consisted of tentative jabs, feints and missed attempts from long range.

Romero remained focused on finding a counter, but Lopez’s greater activity and control of the distance narrowly gave him another quiet round.

10-9 Lopez, 30-27 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 2

Lopez continued setting the pace behind an active jab while forcing Romero to give ground. A clean right hand and several body shots helped Lopez establish his rhythm. Romero remained patient and looked for counters, including a check left hook, but spent too much of the round waiting for openings.

Both fighters missed during a wild exchange near the bell. Lopez’s higher output, effective jab and cleaner punches secured another round.

10-9 Lopez, 20-18 Lopez

Rolando Romero vs. Teofimo Lopez – Round 1

Both fighters opened cautiously at long range, using their jabs to measure distance without committing to extended combinations. Lopez applied more forward pressure and landed the cleaner jabs, while Romero remained patient and looked for counterpunching opportunities.

A counter right from Lopez connected late as Romero moved forward. Romero answered with a right hand before the bell, but Lopez’s greater activity and sharper work gave him the close opening round.

10-9 Lopez

Yoenli Hernandez defeats Francisco Veron

A surprisingly wide disagreement among the judges ended with Yoenli Hernandez defeating Francisco Daniel Veron by majority decision in their 10-round middleweight co-feature. Hernandez won by scores of 99-91 and 98-92, while the third judge produced a questionable 95-95 card.

Cleaner and heavier punches allowed Hernandez to control most of the fight. The Cuban attacked the body, landed sharp right hands and repeatedly caught Veron with uppercuts at close range. Veron pressed forward and maintained a high output, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes. Hernandez recovered and regained control, hurting Veron with a right hand early in the eighth before dominating the final two rounds.

The challenger’s chin carried him to the final bell despite absorbing numerous power punches. Hernandez never found the stoppage he wanted, but his accurate work made the 95-95 score difficult to explain.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 9

Hernandez continued landing the cleaner punches, although some of his shots lacked full force. Veron walked directly into a right hand but absorbed it well and kept pressing forward. His toughness kept him in the fight, but he could not produce enough accurate offense to take the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 89-82 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 8

Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the round and moved in for the finish, but Veron avoided the follow-up attack. Hernandez returned to the body before landing a combination upstairs and two uppercuts that lifted Veron’s chin. Veron answered once again, although Hernandez’s cleaner and harder punches secured the round.

10-9 Hernandez, 79-73 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 7

Hernandez landed a right hand at close range before partially connecting with an uppercut and following with another right. The Cuban then increased his body attack and struck Veron with clubbing punches on the inside. Veron absorbed everything without going down, but Hernandez controlled another round with the heavier work.

10-9 Hernandez, 69-64 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 6

Hernandez connected with several chopping punches, but Veron continued answering with a high volume of shots. Most of Veron’s punches missed or struck the guard, while Hernandez landed the cleaner work during the exchanges. CompuBox credited Veron with only 24 connects from 171 punches across rounds five and six. Hernandez landed 42 of 128 during the same stretch.

10-9 Hernandez, 59-55 Hernandez

After Five Rounds: Hernandez Remains in Control

Hernandez has controlled most of the fight, but Veron’s check hook at the end of the fifth showed that he remains dangerous. Hernandez needs to continue attacking the body without becoming careless while pressing for a stoppage. A convincing victory would place him near a world-title opportunity, but getting reckless against Veron could undo an otherwise strong performance.

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 5

Hernandez landed a heavy right hand during the opening minute, but Veron absorbed it and immediately answered. Hernandez avoided the return before attacking the body and connecting with a right uppercut, a two-punch combination and a left hook. Just when Hernandez seemed to be taking full control, Veron caught him with a check hook that badly wobbled him and stole the round.

10-9 Veron, 49-46 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 4

An overhand right from Hernandez shook Veron at close range before a body shot and two more power punches disrupted his balance. Hernandez continued working downstairs and found the target with a left hook. Veron landed a late flurry, but Hernandez took the punches without showing any effect.

10-9 Hernandez, 40-36 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 3

Hernandez briefly lost his balance after taking a right hand, then answered with a long right and a hard one-two that forced Veron backward. Hernandez continued applying pressure, although many of his heavier punches struck Veron’s guard rather than landing cleanly. Veron’s responsible defense kept him competitive.

10-9 Hernandez, 30-27 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 2

Hernandez pushed Veron backward with power punches, but much of his work landed on the guard. An uppercut-left hook combination came close before Hernandez connected with a sharp right hook at close range. He continued closing the distance and controlling the exchanges.

10-9 Hernandez, 20-18 Hernandez

Yoenli Hernandez vs. Francisco Daniel Veron – Round 1

Hernandez attacked immediately, landing an overhand right that knocked Veron slightly off balance. A straight left split the guard before Hernandez went to the body and followed with punches upstairs. Veron answered with a double left at close range, but Hernandez’s right uppercut and cleaner power shots gave him the round.

10-9 Hernandez

Russell Dominates Santillan

Gary Antonio Russell captured the interim WBA super bantamweight title with a one-sided unanimous decision over Victor Santillan. The judges scored the 12-round bout 119-108, 119-108 and 118-109.

Russell (22-1, 13 KOs) controlled the distance with his faster hands, accurate jab and sharp combinations. Santillan (16-3, 7 KOs) struggled to deal with Russell’s movement and spent much of the fight being beaten to the punch. Russell completed the dominant performance by dropping Santillan during the final round and nearly forcing a stoppage before the bell.

Carlos Utria Edges Israel Mercado by Split Decision

A difficult U.S. debut ended with Carlos Utria narrowly defeating Israel Mercado by split decision after 10 competitive light welterweight rounds. Mercado disrupted the Colombian prospect’s rhythm, pressed forward and made the heavy favorite work harder than anticipated. Utria found success with body punches and short combinations, but he never gained complete control of the fight. Scores were 96-94 and 97-93 for Utria, while the third judge gave Mercado a 96-94 card.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell in First Round

A fast start allowed Marco Romero to overwhelm Kahlil Mitchell and force a stoppage at 2:33 of the opening round. The 20-year-old middleweight landed hard combinations almost immediately, giving Mitchell little time to settle into the fight. Referee intervention ended the scheduled eight-round bout before the first bell.

Benjamin Johnson Decisions Jose Gabriel Rodriguez

The opening fight of the evening ended with Benjamin Johnson earning a unanimous decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez after six welterweight rounds. Johnson used his 6-foot-2 frame and 76-inch reach to control the distance against the shorter Ecuadorian. Rodriguez remained durable and became the first opponent to take the 21-year-old prospect to the final bell. Johnson had stopped each of his first seven opponents before Saturday night.

Joseph Brown Sweeps Alton Wiggins

A six-round shutout gave Joseph Brown a unanimous decision over Alton Wiggins in their junior middleweight bout. The 19-year-old controlled the distance with his height and reach, winning each round without scoring a knockdown. All three judges returned scores of 60-54.

Aldo Blancas Decisions Ricky Mamone

Aldo Blancas used his height, reach and strong left hand to defeat Ricky Mamone by unanimous decision in a four-round light welterweight bout. Blancas dropped Mamone with a left to the body in the second round and controlled most of the action from distance. Mamone recovered and made it to the final bell, but he could not overcome the early knockdown or Blancas’ higher output. The judges scored it 39-36, 39-36 and 40-35.

Ghana News.title: GNFS dismisses reports of unpaid 2025 rent allowance
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has dismissed reports circulating on social media that it has failed to pay personnel their 2025 rent allowance.

In a statement issued on Friday, August 21, 2026, the Service described the reports as “false and unfounded”, clarifying that the final tranche of the full 2025 rent allowance was paid in April 2026.

“Management wishes to state categorically that the information is false and unfounded, as the last tranche of the full payment of the 2025 rent allowance was effected in April 2026,” the statement said.

On the 2026 rent allowance, the GNFS said a committee had been constituted to facilitate the mechanisation process and ensure payments are made soon.

The Service thanked personnel for their patience and assured them of management’s commitment to addressing their welfare concerns, including compensation.

The GNFS also reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and an open-door policy in communicating with personnel and the public, while urging everyone to disregard the report and refrain from circulating what it described as misinformation.

Ghana News.title: Gordon Asare-Bediako steps down from NPP Communications Director race, backs Dennis Aboagye
Ghana News.content:
Gordon Asare Bediako

New Patriotic Party (NPP) National Communications Director aspirant, Gordon Asare-Bediako, has withdrawn his bid for the position and endorsed fellow contender Dennis Miracles Aboagye.

Mr Asare-Bediako announced the decision in a Facebook post on Sunday, August 23, 2026, explaining that it followed extensive consultations with his family, friends and key stakeholders within the party.

According to him, the decision was taken after careful consideration of what would best serve the NPP.

He said although his desire to lead the party’s communications team remained strong, he had concluded that unity was more important than pursuing individual ambitions.

“That desire has not diminished, but I have come to the firm conviction that our party’s interest is best served by unity of purpose, not a division of energies,” he said.

Mr Asare-Bediako subsequently pledged his “full and unreserved support” to Dennis Aboagye and called on his supporters and delegates to back his candidature.

He described Mr Aboagye as “battle-tested”, citing his communication abilities, strategic depth and experience in frontline advocacy for the NPP.

He expressed confidence that Mr Aboagye would strengthen the party’s communications machinery and make it more effective.

“I have no doubt that under his leadership, the NPP’s communication front will be sharper, louder, and more effective than ever before,” he said.

Mr Asare-Bediako further urged party delegates to put the NPP’s broader objective ahead of individual aspirations, stressing that the ultimate goal should be to return the party to power.

“Our mission is bigger than any individual ambition: it is the retrieval of power for the New Patriotic Party and the restoration of hope for the good people of Ghana,” he added.

Ghana News.title: GES dismisses requirement for newly promoted teachers to submit documents for salary adjustments
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Education Service (GES) has clarified that newly promoted teachers are not required to submit application letters, promotion letters or other documents to have their salaries adjusted to reflect their new ranks.

The clarification follows concerns raised by some newly promoted teachers who said they had been directed to submit various documents to facilitate the processing of their salary adjustments.

In an immediate release issued on Saturday, August 22, 2026, the GES said teachers promoted to new ranks are normally placed automatically on the appropriate salary scale, in line with their new positions.

“This existing practice has not changed,” the Service stated.

The GES has, therefore, directed teachers to disregard requests to submit documents for salary adjustments.

“Teachers are, therefore, to ignore the request to submit any documents for salary adjustments,” the statement said.

Management also appealed for calm as it engages the few regions and districts reportedly requesting such documents.

The GES said it remains committed to ensuring that the established process for salary adjustments following promotions is maintained.

Ghana News.title: Meko Bono 2026: Vice President pledges agricultural revival as Atebubu hosts grand homecoming
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Prof Jane Naana Opoku Agyemang has delivered a strong assurance to the farming communities of the Bono East Region, pledging government commitment to minimising post-harvest losses and boosting agricultural productivity under the flagship Feed Ghana programme.

She made the pledge on Saturday when she graced the grand climax of the Meko Bono Homecoming and Festival 2026 in Atebubu, where she was received with traditional pomp and pageantry.

The Vice President, who was the special guest of honour, used the platform to connect directly with the predominantly agrarian population, acknowledging their struggles and outlining tangible interventions to improve their livelihoods.

"We hear your concerns, and we are acting," Prof. Opoku Agyemang told the cheering crowd. "Through the Feed Ghana initiative, we are not only minimising post-harvest losses but also improving general agricultural productivity to create more jobs and generate substantial wealth for our people."

Her address struck a chord with the thousands of farmers gathered, who have long grappled with the challenge of losing significant portions of their harvest to poor storage and logistical constraints. The Vice President's assurance signals a renewed push by the government to make agriculture a more sustainable and profitable venture for the region's backbone workforce.

A celebration of heritage and unity

Beyond the political messaging, the Vice President took time to underscore the cultural significance of the Meko Bono festival, which has grown into a vital platform for celebrating the rich Bono heritage, reconnecting the diaspora with their roots, and fostering partnerships for tourism, investment, and community development.

She admonished the people to let the festival serve as a vessel for preserving history and tradition through togetherness.

"Let this festival preserve the history and tradition of the Bono people through togetherness, thereby creating partnerships for development," she added, drawing thunderous applause from the assembled chiefs, elders, and youth.

Chiefs welcome Veep, rally for development

Hosting the Vice President was HRM Ohempon Dr Yeboah Asiamah, the Atebubumanhene and Chairman of the Meko Bono Advisory Board, who welcomed her and the thousands of visitors with open arms.

In his address, the Paramount Chief emphasised the festival's growing relevance as more than a cultural showcase, but a strategic vehicle for sustainable community development.

"The Meko Bono spirit is the thread that binds us across generations," the Chief stated.

"We must leverage this unity to attract investment and build a prosperous future for our children."

Adding his voice, Osagyefo Oseadeeyo Dr Nana Agyemang Badu II, President of the Bono Regional House of Chiefs, lauded the remarkable cohesion displayed by the Bono people, describing their togetherness as a shining example worthy of emulation across the nation.

"The togetherness we see here today is not by chance; it is the result of shared values and mutual respect," he remarked. "This is the kind of unity that builds nations, and I call on all Ghanaians to learn from the Bono example."

A spectacle of culture and colour

The festival grounds in Atebubu came alive with breathtaking cultural displays that captivated the Vice President and all in attendance. The thunderous rhythms of Fontomfrom drums filled the air, while gracefully choreographed Adowa dancers mesmerised onlookers with their intricate footwork and vibrant regalia.

From elders adorned in rich, hand-woven smocks to the energetic youth participating in traditional war dances, the event was a stunning reminder that Ghana's cultural heritage remains a living, breathing force that unites generations.

Looking ahead

As the sun dipped below the horizon over Atebubu, it was clear that the Meko Bono Homecoming 2026 had achieved far more than a cultural reunion. With the Vice President's agricultural assurances and the chiefs' rallying calls for unity, the people of Atebubu left the festival grounds not just with memories of a spectacular celebration, but with renewed hope for a future built on the solid foundation of their illustrious heritage.

The festival has once again proven that the Bono people are not merely preserving their past; they are actively shaping their future through participation, partnership, and unwavering togetherness.

Ghana News.title: Russian skydiver Sergey Boytcov sets world record with 11,551-metre stratosphere jump
Ghana News.content:
Russian skydiver Sergey Boytcov has set a world record after completing a jump from a hot-air balloon at an altitude of 11,551 metres in support of the 2026 International Festival of Youth.

The record-breaking jump, undertaken ahead of Russia’s National Flag Day, surpassed the previous mark of 10,060 metres set by Polish extreme athletes.

Boytcov, a multiple Russian and world record holder, completed the feat under the Stratum Jump 11–12 project, an initiative by Russian company Created by the Heavens aimed at reaching an altitude above 11,000 metres.

During the jump, his free-fall speed exceeded 500 kilometres per hour, with the entire descent lasting seven minutes and 19 seconds.

His parachute was successfully deployed at an altitude of 1,565 metres before he landed safely in the Ust-Kalmanka District of Russia’s Altai Territory.

The hot-air balloon was piloted by Ivan Menyaylo, President of the Balloon Federation of Russia and a world champion, with flight engineer Denis Efremov also on board. The balloon remained airborne for more than three hours before the crew landed safely.

The balloon itself reached a maximum altitude of 11,610 metres, setting a new Russian national record and surpassing the previous mark of 10,678 metres established in 2025 by Russian explorer Fyodor Konyukhov and Menyaylo in the same region.

Boytcov, who celebrated his birthday on August 15, described the achievement as the most memorable experience of his life.

“We achieved something that not long ago seemed impossible,” he said.

He attributed the feat to the collective efforts of engineers, pilots and other members of the project team, adding that he was particularly proud that the record was achieved in Russia using domestically manufactured equipment.

Boytcov dedicated the achievement to his country ahead of National Flag Day and to the International Festival of Youth – 2026.

“I hope our example shows young people all over the world that even the boldest goals become reality when they are backed by knowledge, hard work, a team, and belief in the outcome,” he said.

Preparations for the attempt involved navigating extreme conditions at more than 11 kilometres above the ground, where temperatures dropped to minus 59 degrees Celsius.

With support from Russia’s Roscosmos State Corporation, Boytcov underwent a test ascent in a pressure chamber at the Cosmonaut Training Centre, simulating conditions at an altitude of 12 kilometres.

Equipment was also tested at temperatures as low as minus 60 degrees Celsius, while the athlete rehearsed aspects of the jump in a wind tunnel.

Boytcov, from Klin in the Moscow Region, has more than 25 years of experience in the sport and has completed over 2,000 jumps. He is also chief executive of Created by the Heavens and holds a USPA Category D licence.

The project received support from several Russian institutions, including the Ministry of Sport, Russian Olympic Committee, State Duma Committee on Physical Culture and Sport, Roscosmos and the Federal Air Transport Agency.

The record attempt was held in support of the International Festival of Youth, scheduled to take place in Ekaterinburg from September 11 to 17, 2026.

The festival, being organised under Russia’s Youth and Children national project, is expected to bring together 10,000 young leaders from 191 countries.

Organisers say participants will comprise 5,000 Russians and 5,000 foreign nationals, including 1,000 teenagers aged between 14 and 17.

Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree establishing the international youth event on December 29, 2025.

The 2026 festival will be held under the theme, “Follow Your Dream”.

Ghana News.title: Ablakwa-led committee submits five reports to Mahama ahead of 2027 AU chairmanship
Ghana News.content:
A committee tasked with developing a strategy document, priority pillars and work programme for President John Mahama’s 2027 African Union (AU) chairmanship has completed its work and submitted five reports to the President.

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, who chaired the committee, said the reports were formally presented to President Mahama at the Presidency on Friday, August 21.

Mr Ablakwa also presented highlights of the committee’s work to the President as part of preparations for his assumption of the continental role.

He disclosed this in a social media post on Sunday, August 23.

According to the Foreign Affairs Minister, the preparatory work is aimed at positioning President Mahama’s tenure to deliver meaningful and lasting results for Africa.

“President Mahama’s tenure is expected to be transformative and impactful due to the rigorous preparatory work underway and his bold vision for our continent,” Mr Ablakwa said.

He expressed appreciation to the members of the committee for the opportunity to contribute to Ghana’s preparations and to the broader development of the African continent.

“We are grateful for the opportunity to serve Ghana and Africa,” he added.

The committee also extended its best wishes to President Mahama ahead of his assumption of the AU chairmanship in January 2027.

Ghana News.title: Africa not seeking Western cash in reparations campaign – Ablakwa
Ghana News.content:
Screenshot

Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa says Africa's campaign for reparatory justice over the transatlantic trafficking and enslavement of Africans is not primarily about securing cash payments from Western countries.

Rather, he said African countries were seeking meaningful support for policies, programmes and development initiatives capable of addressing the enduring consequences of slavery and historical inequalities, particularly through investments in the continent's young people.

Mr Ablakwa made the remarks while responding to questions from the international press in Moscow about the kind of world Ghana and its partners hoped to build following the adoption of a landmark United Nations resolution declaring the trafficking of enslaved Africans and racialised chattel enslavement as the gravest crime against humanity.

Details of the engagement were released on Sunday, August 23, to mark the International Day for the Remembrance of the Slave Trade and its Abolition.

He stressed that the reparatory justice campaign should not be reduced to demands for direct financial payments to African governments.

Instead, he said, Africa wanted Western partners to support causes and initiatives that could help correct historical inequalities, expand opportunities and reposition the continent for sustainable development.

“Reparatory justice goes beyond financial compensation. Of course, it is legitimate, and we are not saying give African leaders financial payments. We are not interested in the money of the West; we are saying support causes.

“And that is why we commend what the Archbishop of Canterbury has done, announcing a hundred million pounds to support causes of young Africans, young entrepreneurs to go into businesses and invest. That is the kind of arrangement we want to see,” he said.

Historic UN resolution

Ghana has been at the forefront of efforts to advance reparatory justice for Africa and people of African descent.

On March 25, 2026, the United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution A/RES/80/250, declaring the trafficking of enslaved Africans and racialised chattel enslavement of Africans as the gravest crime against humanity.

The Ghana-led resolution received the backing of 123 UN member states, while the United States, Israel and Argentina voted against it. Fifty-two countries abstained.

The resolution, championed by President John Dramani Mahama in his capacity as the African Union Champion for Reparations, also called for good-faith dialogue on reparatory justice and the restitution of cultural properties taken from affected countries.

Watch the video of the Minister's comment below.

Accra hosts ‘Next Steps’ conference

Following the UN vote, Ghana hosted the High-Level Consultative Conference on the Next Steps to the Landmark UN Resolution in Accra from June 17 to 19, 2026.

The conference brought together political leaders, diplomats, academics, civil society representatives and members of the African diaspora to develop practical measures for translating the resolution into action.

At the end of the three-day meeting, participants adopted the Accra Next Steps Commitments on Reparatory Justice, outlining a framework covering cultural restitution, education, economic transformation, global governance reforms, debt relief, climate justice, technology access and stronger connections between Africa and its diaspora.

The conference also backed mechanisms to sustain the global reparatory justice campaign, including advisory, legal and cultural restitution structures.

Mr Ablakwa's latest comments reinforce Ghana's position that reparatory justice should go beyond direct financial compensation and focus on long-term interventions capable of addressing structural inequalities and creating a more equitable relationship between Africa and the rest of the world.

Ghana News.title: Production decline, reserve depletion threaten Ghana’s upstream sector – Jinapor
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor

The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has identified declining oil production and dwindling reserves as the biggest immediate threats confronting Ghana’s upstream petroleum sector.

He said although Ghana’s petroleum reserves remained above the targeted levels, the trend was worrying and required urgent action to ensure that new discoveries and developments increasingly replaced the barrels being produced.

Dr Jinapor said the government would work with the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), the Petroleum Commission and industry operators to accelerate field development, appraisal and exploration, while improving regulatory approvals and addressing infrastructure bottlenecks.

“We will therefore work with GNPC, the Petroleum Commission and industry operators to accelerate field development, appraisal and exploration, improve the pace of approvals, address infrastructure bottlenecks and create a more predictable investment environment,” he said.

Government targets reserves replacement

Dr Jinapor said Ghana needed a deliberate shift in its approach to exploration and upstream investment to strengthen its reserves replacement strategy.

He described several projects being pursued by GNPC as strategically important to the future of the sector.

“GNPC’s focus on Pecan, Eban-Akoma, Afina, Pecan North, Almond and Beech, together with the Eban-Akoma Plan of Development, the amended TEN Plan of Development and near-field opportunities, is therefore strategically important,” he said.

He said government would pursue policies to facilitate the commercialisation of these resources while protecting Ghana’s national interests.

Focus on marginal and frontier resources

The Minister also called for innovative approaches to developing marginal and stranded petroleum resources, including the use of production hubs and shared infrastructure.

He further encouraged technically sound exploration of frontier areas such as the Voltaian Basin as part of efforts to expand Ghana’s petroleum resource base.

“Our objective is exploration capable of generating commercially viable reserves and sustainable production,” Dr Jinapor said.

He said the government’s approach would be aimed not only at increasing exploration activity but also at ensuring that new discoveries could be developed commercially to support sustainable production and strengthen the long-term viability of Ghana’s upstream petroleum industry.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
