World.title: ANC mayoral candidate delay raises questions over party unity
World.content:
The ANC's decision to postpone the announcement of its mayoral candidates until September could point to unresolved internal processes and concerns about party unity. Image: X @myanc

The ANC’s decision to postpone the announcement of its mayoral candidates until September could point to unresolved internal processes and concerns about party unity, political analyst Professor Levy Ndou says.

The party is preparing for a difficult contest in key municipalities ahead of the 4 November local government elections, with service delivery failures, financial pressures and coalition instability expected to feature prominently in the campaign.

The ANC has, for now, enlisted its current mayor, Dada Morero, his deputy, Loyiso Masuku, and party veteran Reverend Frank Chikane as its possible Johannesburg candidates ahead of the local government elections.



[WATCH] ANC SG Fikile Mbalula interview with SABC https://t.co/CwSMFehu5Y — ANC – African National Congress (@MYANC) August 22, 2026

Regain the confidence of voters

Ndou says the delay could reflect challenges within the ANC as it attempts to finalise candidates who will be able to regain the confidence of voters and effectively govern municipalities.

“I see that as a confirmation by the leadership of the ANC that there could be trust issues within the party,” Ndou said.



He suggested that the party may also be grappling with concerns about members whose political involvement is closely linked to opportunities for deployment into government structures.

“There are certain people who can only be in the ANC only once they’re being deployed to serve in government structures. And that is an issue that the ANC has to look at,” he said.

Internal processes under scrutiny

Ndou said another possible explanation for the delay is that the ANC’s internal candidate-selection processes have not yet been completed.



While some potential candidates may already have been presented to communities and received their approval, the party still needs to complete its own internal procedures before formally announcing its choices.

“Even though some of the candidates could have been taken to the communities and being approved by communities, the ANC still has to go through its own processes,” Ndou said.

“Such processes could not have been completed. And that is why they all have decided to delay this exercise.”



Tough election battle ahead

The ANC faces a challenging electoral environment in several major metros, where residents have expressed frustration over deteriorating infrastructure, unreliable services and municipal financial problems.

Ndou says these issues have contributed to the party’s declining electoral support and will place significant pressure on its mayoral candidates.

He believes the ANC needs to select candidates who are not only politically credible but also capable of improving service delivery, restoring public confidence and navigating coalition governments.



The party’s choices will therefore be closely watched as it attempts to strengthen its position ahead of the November elections.

The delayed announcement gives the ANC additional time to finalise its candidates, but it also risks reinforcing questions about the party’s internal cohesion and readiness for the electoral battle.

World.title: Big change for Gauteng e-hailing drivers as new registration begins
World.content:
Gauteng has started a new registration process for e-hailing drivers as the province tightens oversight of the sector. Image: Flickr

Gauteng has started registering e-hailing drivers on a provincial transport system as South Africa’s push to regulate the industry enters its next phase.

The provincial government has called on e-hailing companies to ensure their drivers register on the Gauteng Integrated Public Transport Administration System (GIPTAS).

According to a report, the process will require drivers to provide key personal, vehicle and licensing information.



The development could affect hundreds of thousands of drivers as authorities move to formalise the rapidly growing sector.

What e-hailing drivers will need

GIPTAS stores information Gauteng uses to manage and monitor public transport operations and regulate the issuing of public transport licences.

Drivers registering on the system will need to provide key licensing documents.

These include their Professional Driving Permit (PrDP), vehicle registration details and identity numbers.

Foreign nationals who do not have South African ID numbers can use a Traffic Register Number (TRN) when registering.

A TRN allows people without a standard 13-digit South African ID number to conduct road traffic transactions through the country’s eNaTIS system.



Ashif Black, inDrive’s South Africa country representative, in an interview, said that the provincial government had started engaging e-hailing operators about the process.

The government wants to strengthen its database of drivers operating in Gauteng as the industry adjusts to tougher regulation.

No registration deadline yet

Drivers do not, however, face an immediate registration deadline.

Black said the GIPTAS process remained in its early stages and authorities had not yet set a deadline.

He said operators were still engaging government over some of the requirements and seeking clarity on parts of the process.

The registration of drivers follows an earlier push to bring e-hailing platforms themselves into the regulatory system.

In November 2025, the Gauteng Department of Roads and Transport called on e-hailing app providers operating in the province to register legally.

It was previously reported in June that inDrive had subsequently secured approval to operate under South Africa’s new regulatory framework.

South Africa tightens e-hailing rules

The changes form part of broader efforts to regulate e-hailing under the amended National Land Transport framework.

The new regulatory system formally recognises e-hailing as a public transport category and places greater compliance obligations on platforms, drivers and vehicles.

Requirements include operating licences for drivers and vehicles, approved vehicle identification and additional safety measures.

The Gauteng government’s official operating licence application documentation also states that operating licences are granted per vehicle.

The latest move shifts the focus towards individual drivers and the information authorities hold about people providing e-hailing services.

According to another report on Sunday, the Gauteng government had urged e-hailing companies to ensure their drivers register on GIPTAS.

For drivers, the key issue now is to ensure their PrDP, vehicle registration and identification documents are in order while the registration process unfolds.

Authorities have not announced a final deadline, meaning drivers should watch for further instructions from the province and their respective e-hailing platforms.

World.title: ANC delays mayoral candidate announcement until September
World.content:
The African National Congress (ANC) says it will now announce its mayoral candidates for the 4 November local government elections in September.

The party had indicated that it would announce its candidates at the Sandton Convention Centre on Saturday, 22 August. However, instead of announcing the final candidates, the ANC revealed the potential candidates who had been interviewed for the positions.

Speaking at the event, ANC secretary-general Fikile Mbalula said the party’s election campaign was not dependent on individual candidates, but was driven by the party, with President Cyril Ramaphosa serving as the face of the campaign.



Mbalula said the party was confident in its candidate selection process and had raised the bar when it came to choosing mayoral candidates.

“In the past, what used to happen is that you would have a candidate after the election and whether that candidate is qualified or not, they would become the mayor. Now we are fixated on the idea that a mayor must have certain qualities and a solid education. We already have our mayors but what is important to us is the process,” he explained.

Reacting to the development, political analyst Professor Levy Ndou told the SABC that there had been high expectations that the ANC would finally announce its mayoral candidates.

Ndou said ANC chairperson Gwede Mantashe’s remarks that announcing the candidates immediately could potentially result in some ANC members defecting to other parties indicated that there were trust issues within the party.

“Another aspect would be the dynamics in the party, that even though some of the candidates could have been taken to the communities and approved by communities, the ANC still has to go through its own processes and such processes could not have been completed and that is why they have decided to delay the announcement,” he explained.

Since the 2016 local government elections, the ANC has continued to poll below 50%, particularly in metropolitan municipalities in Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, which were once considered party strongholds.



Some of the ANC’s potential candidates for Johannesburg include veteran Reverend Frank Chikane, current mayor Dada Morero and deputy mayor Loyiso Masuku.

In eThekwini, the potential candidates include current mayor Cyril Xaba and council Speaker Thabani Nyawose, among others.

PARTY TO LAUNCH MANIFESTO

Meanwhile, the ANC is set to launch its manifesto for the local government elections on Sunday, 23 August.

President Cyril Ramaphosa will officially launch the manifesto in Riverside, Diepsloot, in Gauteng.

The manifesto launch is expected to outline the party’s plans and priorities for local government over the next five years.

World.title: ‘I'm absolutely livid’ - Cachalia on IDAC corruption exposed at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia is outraged by the extent of corruption exposed at the Madlanga Commission involving IDAC.

The revelations that the NPA unit was used to target innocent people have been deeply disheartening for Cachalia.

On Friday, the NPA unconditionally withdrew charges against Crime Intelligence head Dumisani Khumalo, Dineo Mokwele and several others.

“So, some charges have been withdrawn against General Khumalo, for instance. That was the outcome of a review process initiated by the head of the NDPP, Andy Mothibi. I'm waiting for that process to be concluded before it is clear what other steps need to be taken.

“But I have to say, what I see being under scrutiny before the Madlanga Commission at IDAC, you know, I just feel complete outrage.

“People in positions of leadership have behaved with a shocking combination of incompetence, at the very least. But clearly there are suggestions that there were ulterior purposes. The damage that they have done to the fight against corruption is enormous. I'm absolutely livid."

World.title: ‘We want the mastermind’ - Deokaran family
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Who paid for the hit on Babita Deokaran?

That's the question that continues to plague the family and friends of the anti-corruption whistleblower.

Today marks five years since Deokaran was gunned down outside her home.

She was killed for uncovering suspicious and irregular payments at Tembisa Hospital, totalling over R850 million.

READ: ‘People who benefited from her death are in power’ - Cachalia on Deokaran murder

Her work helped expose what became a much larger corruption scandal.

Her brother, Rakesh Deokaran, said their focus is not on the people already in the dock for her murder.

"We are not interested in the six arrested. We want the mastermind. A hitman doesn't hire himself. It's unfortunate that, five years later, by her not being here, they thought it was the end. Unfortunately for them, we did not stay quiet,” he said.

World.title: ANC launches election manifesto in Diepsloot
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC manifesto will address lessons learnt and come up with better solutions.

That's the promise from provincial convener and Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi.

The party is launching its manifesto in Diepsloot faced with declining support,

and unhappiness over lack of services.

Party Gauteng provincial convener Panyaza Lesufi said the manifesto shows that they have learned from their mistakes.

"This manifesto will see the hallmark of it is to say we have learned from our mistakes. The hallmark of it is that we have accepted the limitations, the capacity, the leadership that we have deployed and some of the municipalities need assistance.

“And Emfuleni is high on the agenda. But take the 11 municipalities that are in Gauteng. If you isolate Emfuleni in Merafong, we've got nine solid municipalities that are run by the African National Congress in partnership with other coalition partners.

“That alone demonstrates the desire, the ability, the skill and the talent for us to run these municipalities.

“There's a municipality, it's a stone's throw away, called Rand West, with two consecutive clean audits. The ability to know where you have made a mistake will be demonstrated here, where the President outlined that we know where we have made a mistake at leadership level, at infrastructure level, at capacity level, and therefore this manifesto that we are launching today is rectifying those limitations,” Lesufi said.

World.title: ‘People who benefited from her death are in power’ - Cachalia on Deokaran murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The masterminds behind the brutal murder of anti-corruption whistleblower Babita Deokoran are free because they are in positions of power.

That's the view of acting police minister Firoz Cachalia.

Today marks five years since Deokoran was gunned down outside her home for uncovering widespread looting at Tembisa hospital.

“The people who benefited financially from her death, and the reason why we don't have justice, is because those people are in power and can protect themselves. That problem of corruption is the disease and illness eating at our country’s hopes,” Cachalia said.

World.title: Gauteng PKTT arrests five Emfuleni Municipality employees
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Five employees of Emfuleni Municipality have been arrested in connection with allegations of fraud, theft and tampering with essential infrastructure.

The arrests, conducted by Gauteng's Political Killings Task Team, follow Friday's takedown operation in Vanderbijlpark.

The suspects are attached to the Revenue and Electrical Departments.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the suspects operated a scheme in which they misrepresented themselves to municipal clients as authorised officials who could reconnect electricity supplies.

Clients were then allegedly instructed to pay various amounts of money directly into the suspects’ bank accounts.

The five arrested suspects are expected to make their first appearance in court tomorrow.

World.title: Greater focus on small towns and villages – SA Tourism
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South Africa's tourism conference has wrapped up and the message and direction are clear.

There will be greater attention paid to small towns, villages and dorpies that make the country beautiful.

To achieve this, SA Tourism interim CEO Sechaba Motsieloa said partnerships between SA Tourism and municipalities need to be strengthened.

"We are working with municipalities to improve infrastructure. The ability to allow people to visit the less visited provinces is going to be critical because there is quite a lot that is still there to offer.

“Also, remember that with the tourists coming into the country, we are a faraway destination.

“So, when we are here, we want them to stay a bit longer so that they can visit the different parts. You will see in those small villages, townships, as well as small dorpies. When we have people staying a little bit longer, talking a little bit more about the country, it does help quite a lot to ensure that the messaging and the experiences are shed quite evenly."

World.title: ANC mayoral candidate announcement on hold
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG – Despite making public statements about announcing mayoral candidates, the ANC has done an about turn, saying they would only announce their candidates in September.

The party was set to announce mayoral candidates on Saturday ahead of launching their election manifesto on Sunday.

In a press statement released on 19 August, the party described the announcement of mayoral candidates as a milestone.

“The African National Congress (ANC) will host two key milestones as part of its preparations for the 2026 Local Government Elections, namely the official announcement of its mayoral candidates and the launch of its 2026 Local Government Elections Manifesto.

“The mayoral candidate announcement will provide an opportunity for the ANC to introduce the men and women who will carry the organisation’s mandate of building capable, accountable and responsive local government.

“The event forms part of the ANC’s commitment to presenting communities with leadership that is ready to serve, rebuild confidence and accelerate the delivery of better communities.”

On the day, however, ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula arrived only to announce the names of the shortlisted candidates, the nominees.

He said the party’s campaign does not revolve around candidates and that they would only make the announcement in September.

“We have done what needed to be done in terms of interviewing everybody. We are revealing the people who have the potential to be mayoral candidates. The ANC campaign is not dependent on candidates. It is driven and dependent on the face of the campaign, who is the President.

“The add-on is the candidates, which is the decision that has been taken by the leadership and therefore in this particular instance, we are following that. We are doing it in a systematic way and that is what we are following as the African National Congress."

Leadership expert Mazwe Majola said this was a bad move.

"It is very underwhelming, very disappointing. Remember, the ANC promised the nation that they would be announcing the mayoral candidates...for them not doing that, it's got a risk of being viewed as disorganized, evasive, dilly-dallying, or even really exposing some internal divisions and dynamics within the ANC. So, it's not good for them," Majola said.

Ntsikelelo Breakfast, a political analyst, said the move was political gimmick.

Breakfast thinks this is to prevent party factions from splintering before the elections.

"I think the reason why they don't want to put forward the names of the final candidates is to avoid discouraging those who would have been omitted from mobilizing on behalf of the ANC because maybe they will be left with broken hearts.

“You don't want to escalate tensions within the ANC now. So I think it is strategic then to say that in this municipality, this is the list. Then, when the elections are over, the ANC will make the call in terms of how they're going to pick and choose.”

World.title: All Blacks upset Springboks in first Test
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - New Zealand have taken a 1-0 lead in the Greatest Rivalry Test Series after defeating the Springboks 33-16 at Ellis Park.

A tightly contested match unravelled for the hosts in the second half.

Poor discipline and handling saw the All Blacks take the game away from the Boks.

The Springboks led 13-12 at half-time only to be dominated after the break and finished with 13 players after Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were yellow-carded.

World.title: Uhuru hits back at Ruto: Kenyans will choose their president in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Retired President Uhuru Kenyatta arriving at the late Kijana Wamalwa's home in Kitale. [Osinde Obare, Standard]

Retired President Uhuru Kenyatta has said Kenyans will have the final say on who will lead the country after the 2027 General Election, insisting he has no interest in returning to active politics.

Speaking on Sunday during the memorial service for former Vice-President Michael Kijana Wamalwa in Kitale, Uhuru said voters would be free to choose whichever candidate they want as president.

The former President made the remarks while listing political leaders, prompting cheers from the crowd when he mentioned Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

"Wakenya wana haki ya kujichagulia viongozi wanaowapenda. Kama wanataka Kalonzo ni Kalonzo, wakisema wanataka Ruto, ni Ruto, wakisema wanataka Matiang'i ni Matiang'i, na wakisema wanataka SIfuna, ni Sifuna," Uhuru stated.

Uhuru jokingly cautioned the crowd against fuelling claims that he was sponsoring Sifuna or the Linda Mwananchi movement.

“Jameni chungeni, sitaki kuitwa sponsor,” Uhuru said, drawing laughter from the audience.

His remarks came amid claims by President William Ruto and his allies that Uhuru is financing opposition politicians seeking to challenge the President's bid for re-election in 2027.

On his part, Sifuna has denied the allegations, maintaining that the movement is funded through contributions and support from ordinary Kenyans and other well-wishers.

"Yule jamaa amebeba akili yote ya Kenya aliulizwa swali mboga sana, atoe evidence Uhuru ndio sponsor ya upinzani akasema hata yeye alisoma kwa gazeti…na anadai sisi ndio mafala," Sifuna stated earlier on his social media accounts. Uhuru also launched 'My Country First,' a book honouring the late Michael Kijana Wamalwa. [Osinde Obare, Standard]

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Ruto denies Sh104bn SHA technology contract
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto has dismissed claims that the government entered into a controversial Sh104 billion contract with Safaricom and Apeiro Limited for the Social Health Authority (SHA) technology system.

Speaking on Tuesday evening at the Presidential Townhall held during the National Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto defended the government's investment in digital health, saying the technology was designed to improve transparency and accountability in the management of SHA services.

“There is no Sh104 billion contract. What we have done is design a digital system to make sure that everything is visible. Every treatment must be traceable, and every payment must be accounted for,” Ruto said.

He explained that the government had not purchased the technology outright but had engaged investors who own the equipment, with the State paying for the services provided.

His remarks were echoed by Digital Health Agency Chief Executive Anthony Lenaiyara, who rejected claims that SHA had committed Sh104 billion to technology upgrades.

“It is not correct or true that SHA has undertaken any upgrade or invested Sh104 billion in technology upgrades. What we did is build a digital superhighway comprising 43 systems to support Universal Health Coverage,” Lenaiyara said.

Lenaiyara said the technology infrastructure had been rolled out without requiring health facilities to purchase the devices, adding that the system had transformed the processing and accountability of SHA claims.

He contrasted the new system with the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) model, where claims were processed using physical files that moved between different offices for verification and approval.

Ruto also addressed other government programmes, saying the State had mobilised resources to construct 23,000 additional classrooms to ease pressure caused by shortages of learning spaces.

World.title: 'That was not healthcare, it was theft'- Ruto on old health system
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during the official opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC), Nairobi, August 18,2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has accused the defunct National Health Insurance Fund (NHIF) system of enabling theft from sick Kenyans, citing claims for procedures that never happened.

Speaking on Tuesday, August 18, at the opening of the Kenya Health Summit at the Kenyatta International Convention Centre (KICC) in Nairobi, Ruto described the old system as opaque and vulnerable to abuse.

"We heard of claims for procedures that never happened, fictitious patients and inflated bills. That was not healthcare, it was theft, and theft from sick Kenyans," said Ruto.

He called digital health systems the backbone holding the reforms together and said they would close loopholes that let people profit from the system's weaknesses.

Ruto ranked Universal Health Coverage (UHC) alongside the Affordable Housing Programme as one of the government's most consequential social transformation efforts, crediting collaboration between national and county governments for changes in how healthcare is financed, delivered and accounted for.

The two-day summit, themed "Reforms Delivered, Health as a Right," has drawn more than 5,000 delegates to audit progress under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and set priorities for the remainder of Ruto's term, according to Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale.

Ruto said 32.3 million Kenyans are now registered with the Social Health Authority (SHA), which replaced NHIF in October 2024.

Eight million have received treatment, more than 1.2 million mothers have been supported to deliver safely and more than 500,000 surgical procedures have been supported, he added.

He put Kenyans' previous annual out-of-pocket health spending at Sh150 billion ($1.16 billion), saying families had borrowed, sold assets or organised harambees to cover medical costs before the reforms.

"Millions paid out of pocket, borrowed, sold assets, organised harambees or stayed away from hospital because they could not afford care," said Ruto.

Since October 2024, SHA has received more than Sh209 billion ($1.62 billion) and paid more than Sh178 billion ($1.38 billion) to contracted facilities across all 47 counties, Ruto added.

He credited 107,800 Community Health Promoters, deployed under a shared financing arrangement between national and county governments, with reaching more than nine million households and referring over 750,000 people for further treatment.

On supply chains, Ruto said the Kenya Medical Supplies Authority's (KEMSA) fill rate had risen from about 40 per cent to 91 per cent, helped by a Sh1.5 billion ($11.6 million) recapitalisation and a Sh10 billion ($77.4 million) credit line.

The reforms rest on four laws Ruto signed on 19 October 2023: the Primary Health Care Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, the Digital Health Act and the Facilities Improvement Financing Act.

Ruto acknowledged gaps remained in registration, benefit clarity, claims processing and digital systems.

"The ultimate measure of reform is not the laws we pass or the numbers we register, but the experience of the patient in terms of dependable, affordable and dignified care," said Ruto.

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki, Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, Duale and Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja attended the opening session, alongside county governors, principal secretaries, members of Parliament and development partners.

The summit runs through Wednesday.

World.title: Gachagua: Opposition does not need Uhuru's money to send Ruto home
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu on August 16, 2026. [Kimaku Chege, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims that former President Uhuru Kenyatta is financing opposition activities against President William Ruto.

Addressing the allegations that Kenyatta was financing opposition campaigns, Gachagua insisted that the movement did not require money from the former President.

Gachagua says the movement seeking political change is driven by Kenyans and does not depend on financial sponsorship.

“Nasikia kwamba Uhuru is sponsoring us to campaign against you. Uhuru is not sponsoring us, we don't need any sponsorship, this is a mass movement for change which does not need funding,” he said.

He was speaking on Sunday, August 16, 2026, during a church service at PCEA Rev. Samuel Marima Memorial Church in Gatundu South, Kiambu County.

Gachagua further said the opposition had sufficient public support to challenge the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election, insisting that Kenyans themselves were the driving force behind calls for a change of government.

He added that the public itself would determine the political fate of the Ruto administration.

“We don't need money but Kenyans will send you home,” Gachagua said.

The comments come against the backdrop of renewed debate over political alliances and the role of former leaders in Kenya's 2027 succession politics. Kenyatta, who served as President from 2013 to 2022, has largely remained outside the day-to-day administration of government since handing over power to Ruto.

Gachagua also defended Kenyatta against what he described as attempts to drag the former President into the current political contest.

“Uhuru Kenyatta asiguzwe na mtu yeyote. Alindwe na atetewe na apatiwe amani. Uhuru alifanya kazi yake na akastaafu,” Gachagua said.

The former Deputy President said Kenyatta should not be treated as a political candidate or blamed for the activities of opposition politicians.

“Nimemwambia Ruto unauliza Uhuru nini na sio candidate in the next election. I am your main opponent,” Gachagua said.

His remarks came amid an increasingly heated political contest over the direction of the country ahead of the 2027 elections.

Ruto and his administration have faced criticism from opposition figures over the economy, cost of living and the government's record since taking office.

Gachagua's comments also followed his broader criticism of the government's economic record.

Earlier in the church address, he challenged Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi's argument that increased consumption of soft drinks could indicate improved household incomes.

Gachagua argued that ordinary Kenyans were experiencing economic difficulties despite government claims of improved economic indicators. He said declining church offerings would provide a more meaningful indication of household financial wellbeing.

“If you want to know if the economy is doing well, ask the pastor about the offering; it will tell you how the economy is moving,” he said.

He further urged Kenyans to prepare for political change in 2027, arguing that the country required new leadership.

“Let us get in line. We look for new leadership that will fix our country and return it to where Uhuru Kenyatta left us,” Gachagua said

World.title: Gachagua: We will protect ourselves against goons
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua addresses residents of Naivasha where he lashed out at President William and told him to keep of former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [Antony Gitonga, Standard]

Former Deputy President and DCP party leader Rigathi Gachagua has vowed to fight back against goons allegedly disrupting his political rallies, saying his supporters will defend themselves if the police fail to protect them.

Speaking during the opening of DCP offices in Nakuru, Gachagua said they had received intelligence that the National Police Service (NPS) had been instructed to keep off areas where his rallies were being held.

Gachagua spoke a day after goons attacked his convoy at Kaptembwo in Nakuru West Sub-County, forcing him to abandon a DCP campaign rally and flee the scene alongside other leaders.

Six vehicles belonging to leaders, including Ol-Kalou MP Samuel Waweru, were vandalised during the incident as DCP leaders and supporters scrambled for safety.

Gachagua accused President William Ruto of allegedly planning the chaos through a Nakuru MP who, he claimed, had paid goons to disrupt his rallies.

“President William Ruto planned the chaos using a Nakuru MP who paid goons to attack us. This was despite his assurance that our campaign rallies would be protected,” Gachagua said.

He claimed he had received credible intelligence that police officers had been advised to keep away from Kaptembwo during the attack.

Gachagua further alleged that although the MP was associated with the Jubilee Party, he was being used by President Ruto to cause chaos.

“I have also spoken to Jubilee Party leaders to put their house in order. If it is proven that the MP is being used by the President, then he should be removed. That will inform how we relate to the Jubilee Party,” he said.

The former Deputy President said goons had allegedly been deployed to cause chaos at various stopovers, but some police officers who were unhappy with the Kenya Kwanza administration had provided his team with intelligence.

“We stood down our guard, hoping for protection from the government, but we are now on high alert and we will protect ourselves,” Gachagua said.

He also accused senior police officers in Nakuru of allegedly working with goons to disrupt his rallies.

According to Gachagua, junior police officers were unhappy with being allegedly forced to work with goons to cause chaos, steal property and kill Kenyans.

“These police officers have reduced salaries, they are not funded, they lack fuel and they are suffering,” he said.

World.title: NFSA: Egypt’s food exports reach 208,000 tons in one week,
World.content:
Egypt exported 4,370 food shipments totaling 208,000 tons between August 15 and 21, 2026, shipped by 1,410 exporting companies and covering around 758 food products, the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) said on Sunday, August 23, 2026.

In its 31st weekly report for 2026, the authority said the exports included vegetables and tubers, fruits, preserved fruit and vegetable products, flour and grain products, and various other food items.

Vegetable exports totaled 50,000 tons across 45 varieties. Sweet potatoes topped the list at 20,000 tons, followed by onions at 10,000 tons and potatoes at 5,000 tons.

Fruit exports reached 36,000 tons across 34 varieties, led by strawberries at 13,000 tons, followed by citrus fruits at 7,000 tons and mangoes at 6,000 tons.

Tunisia was the largest importer of Egyptian food products during the week, followed by Italy, Syria, Saudi Arabia and the Netherlands, among 182 countries importing Egyptian food products.

Alexandria Port ranked first in the number of food export consignments, with 740 shipments, followed by Safaga Port with 703 and Damietta Port with 630.

As for food imports, Egypt received 1,917 food consignments totaling around 220,000 tons, imported by 858 companies. The shipments included wheat, soybeans and various oils.

Russia topped the list of food suppliers to Egypt during the week, followed by Indonesia, the United States, Australia and China, among 84 countries exporting food products to the Egyptian market.

Alexandria Port also ranked first in food import consignments with 679 shipments, followed by Cairo International Airport with 381 and Port Said Port with 220.

World.title: 262nd aid convoy enters Gaza via Rafah terminal
World.content:
The 262nd convoy of the “Zad Al-Ezza: From Egypt to Gaza” humanitarian aid campaign entered the Gaza Strip on Sunday, August 23, 2026, through the Rafah land crossing toward the Karm Abu Salem crossing in southern Gaza, following a two-day halt on Friday and Saturday for the weekly weekend break.

The convoy’s trucks are carrying humanitarian and relief supplies, including meat, food baskets, flour, medical supplies, relief materials, petroleum products and fuel.

The trucks are being inspected by Israeli authorities at the Karm Abu Salem crossing before being allowed to enter the Gaza Strip.

The Egyptian Red Crescent has maintained its presence along the border since the beginning of the crisis, remaining on standby at all logistical centers and continuing efforts to facilitate the entry of humanitarian and relief aid. More than 75,000 volunteers have contributed to the organization’s efforts.

World.title: Farida Osman wins bronze in 50m butterfly at Taranto 2026
World.content:
Egyptian swimmer Farida Osman won the bronze medal in the women’s 50m butterfly at the Taranto 2026 Mediterranean Games after finishing the race in 26.32 seconds, giving Egypt its second medal at the Games.

Osman’s bronze came after Abdelrahman Sameh won the gold medal in the men’s 50m butterfly in 23.18 seconds, securing Egypt’s first gold medal of the Games and breaking the competition record.

The 20th edition of the Mediterranean Games is being held in the Italian city of Taranto and will continue through Sept 3, with 3,803 athletes from 26 countries taking part.

The Egyptian delegation is competing in 23 sports, including archery, athletics, badminton, 3×3 basketball, boxing, canoeing and kayaking, equestrian, fencing, swimming, gymnastics, handball, judo, karate, padel, rowing, sailing, shooting, table tennis, volleyball, weightlifting, wrestling, fin swimming and inline skating.

The Egyptian delegation is seeking to continue its medal-winning run and achieve strong results at the Games, maintaining Egypt’s position among the leading medal-winning countries in Mediterranean Games history.

Egypt ranks sixth among the countries with the most medals in the history of the Mediterranean Games, with a total of 620 medals, including 156 gold, 209 silver and 255 bronze.

World.title: Egyptian FM, Palestinian VP urge preserving territorial unity in Gaza, West Bank
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and Palestinian Vice President Hussein Al-Sheikh stressed on Sunday, August 23, 2026, the importance of preserving the territorial unity of the Palestinian territories in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank and enabling the Palestinian Authority to assume its responsibilities.

The two officials discussed the latest developments in the Palestinian territories during a phone call held as part of ongoing coordination.

Abdelatty condemned Israel’s expansion of settlement activities, the escalating violence by settlers and violations in East Jerusalem and at Al-Aqsa Mosque. He reiterated Egypt’s categorical rejection of the settlement project in the “E1” area, warning that it threatens to divide the West Bank, encircle and isolate East Jerusalem, and undermine prospects for establishing an independent Palestinian state along the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The talks also covered ongoing efforts to complete the commitments of the first phase of US President Donald Trump’s peace plan in accordance with the roadmap and move to the second phase. These efforts include ensuring the flow of humanitarian aid into Gaza and enabling the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza to begin carrying out its duties from within the Strip.

Al Sheikh, for his part, praised Egypt’s support for the Palestinian cause and its efforts to uphold the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, stressing the continuation of coordination and consultations during the coming period.

World.title: Trump wants South Korea to defend itself. His overtures to Kim Jong Un could delay that
World.content:
By suddenly scaling down war games with South Korea, US President Donald Trump risks working against his own stated goal of having Seoul assume more responsibility for its own defense.

The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, involving tens of thousands of troops, have been cut in half at Washington’s request, after Trump said last weekend that the exercises antagonized his friend, North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un, while also costing the US a lot of money.

These exercises “send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile,” Trump posted on Truth Social on Sunday in what appeared to be an attempt to appease the reclusive Kim, who Trump is eager to meet with again.

The “hostile” part is hard to reconcile with the defensive nature of the exercises and is strikingly similar to how North Korea’s state media have described the drills. Washington and Seoul have said repeatedly they are about deterrence and defense, not about taking territory north of the demilitarized zone that has divided the Koreas since the armistice struck in 1953.

Contained within the military exercises is training to give South Korea something it hasn’t had since the Korean War began in 1950: wartime operational control of the combined South Korea-US forces on the peninsula, analysts point out.

It’s a key goal for both countries. Once Seoul shows it can take on that burden, Washington can take a backseat in any future conflict, providing some firepower but letting South Korea assume most of the responsibility and cost of its defense.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Wednesday said he agreed with Trump’s opinion that South Korea should take responsibility for its own security in the Korean Peninsula, by rapidly increase its defense spending to 3.5% of GDP.

He also said the decision by Trump to shorten the drills “feels like a major decision filled with deep consideration for creating peace on the Korean Peninsula, beyond hostility and confrontation.”

The current control set-up came about shortly after the start of the Korean War, when South Korea turned command of its forces over to Washington, which – vastly better equipped and more experienced – was more suited to dealing with the communist threat at the dividing line.

Control of South Korean troops was assumed by United Nations Command, and in 1978, by the Combined Forces Command (CFC), which has always been led by an American general.

16th August 1950: An American tank firing on enemy positions in the area around Masan in Korea. Keystone/Hulton Archive/Getty Images

The CFC gave peacetime operational control of South Korean forces to Seoul in 1994, but wartime control has remained with Washington. Calls for change and timelines to accomplish it have been pushed back several times since, leaving in place a status quo that is no longer needed.

Over the past several years, South Korea has emerged as a world-class military power – not quite on the level of the US or China, but certainly capable of defending itself against North Korea.

Citing that ability, Lee on Tuesday used the launch of this year’s exercises to try to bring new momentum to a campaign promise he made in 2025 to bring wartime operational control back into Seoul’s hands by 2030.

“From the aspect of weapons systems and military strength, our capabilities to defend ourselves is already among the top few in the world. It’s not an exaggeration to say that we are more than capable,” Lee said Tuesday.

But Trump has thrown a spanner into the works.

The plan was to use the Ulchi Freedom Shield drills to assess systems so Seoul could assume wartime operational control, Yu Ji-hoon, a research fellow at the Korea Institute for Defense Analyses, wrote in The Diplomat.

“A major last-minute change could therefore affect more than readiness; it could complicate an alliance project that Washington itself has long encouraged,” Yu wrote.

“Curtailing (the exercises), especially without prior discussion, makes burden-sharing harder to implement, even as Washington demands more of it,” he said.

Lee Jeong-kyu, a visiting research fellow at South Korea’s Sejong Institute, wrote earlier this year of momentum building for more South Korean control, with it laid out in black and white in the US National Defense Strategy released in January.

The document was “a clear signal of intent to strengthen alliance burden-sharing that is expected to provide grounds for accelerating the conditions for (operational control) transfer,” Lee wrote.

With his deference to North Korea’s Kim, Trump has put a nuclear-armed adversary of the US above a treaty ally that wants to do what Trump has asked of it.

That keeps US forces tied up with responsibilities on the peninsula at a time when they could be sorely needed in a place like Iran or possible future conflicts, both in Asia and around the world. And it means future defense budgets can’t factor in cost savings in Korea when demand for new weapons is only growing.

South Korea has long been a close American ally; since the end of the Korean War the two nations have had a mutual defense treaty primarily designed to protect the South from North Korea.

But Trump’s touted personal relationship with North Korea’s Kim –– who has significantly expanded his country’s military capabilities since Trump’s first term and is now believed to have dozens of nuclear warheads –– has tested the long-standing partnership.

For its part, North Korea has not responded positively to Trump’s new olive branch. Kim’s powerful sister Kim Yo Jong, a top official, said that reducing the scale of the drills does not change “the provocative and offensive nature” of them, and should not be seen as “measure of goodwill.”

Before news of the curtailment broke Wednesday morning, North Korean state media KCNA called the exercises “the most immediate and open threat” to Pyongyang, and regional security.

Trump’s sudden involvement appears to be forcing a rethink wider than just the exercises, with Seoul’s military chiefs saying Wednesday the two sides would now need to discuss “combined defense posture going forward.”

North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un shakes hands with US President Donald Trump at the start of their historic US-North Korea summit, at the Capella Hotel on Sentosa island in Singapore on June 12, 2018. Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty Images

For Trump, already weakened on the world stage by the ongoing war with Iran, it’s another own goal, analysts said.

“The cost savings from downsizing drills are marginal, while the diplomatic benefits for relations with North Korea are doubtful,” said Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul.

Just what Trump might want to achieve by meeting again with Kim is opaque. He failed in his first term to strong-arm the North Korean leader into giving up his nuclear ambitions, which have only grown. Meanwhile, Kim has moved closer to Russia and China.

Trump might see it as “unthreatening and respectful” to himself, but North Korea has become a much stronger military power in the near-decade since Trump first took office.

“Scaling (the drills) back can damage alliance coordination, slow the process of South Korea taking on greater responsibility for its own defense, and weaken deterrence against possible conflicts in Asia,” Easley said.

This story has been updated with additional developments.

World.title: It’s ‘Black August’ in Russia, but Putin is sweeping this summer’s crisis under the rug
World.content:
Over the past few decades, “Black August,” or “the August curse,” has become a sort of journalistic shorthand in Russia for dramatic crises that seem to happen in the last weeks of summer.

In some respects, Black August is Russia’s rough equivalent to the “silly season” in British journalism, the late-summer lull when frivolous headlines seem to dominate while parliament is out of session and royals are on holiday – or announce surprise returns home. But Russian folk wisdom is more pessimistic: a scan of recent Russian history appears to support the belief that dramatic, Black Swan events do tend to strike in August.

Thirty-five years ago, a group of Communist hardliners led a failed putsch against Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, unleashing the centrifugal forces that ultimately led to the collapse of the Soviet Union. In August 1998, a financial crisis hit Russia, causing a default on domestic debt and a collapse of the ruble. And one year later, a group of militants led an incursion into the southern Russian republic of Dagestan, kicking off the second Chechen War, a conflict that launched a political unknown, a former KGB officer named Vladimir Putin, into the top echelon of power.

Putin became Russian leader on New Year’s Eve of 1999, after a surprise handover by President Boris Yeltsin. But the new tough-guy leader was not immune from the August Curse either. One of his first major tests in office was the sinking of the Kursk, a nuclear submarine that went down with 118 sailors on board. And in August 2008, Russia went to war with neighboring Georgia, showing the belligerent new face of Putin’s foreign policy.

The past summer in Russia has also been shaping up as a bleak season for Putin’s Russia. Progress on the contested front lines in Ukraine by Russian troops has been scant; the skies over Russian cities have been blackened by Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries and Amazon-style distribution centers; and long lines at the fuel pumps and rumors of a fresh wave of mobilization have Russians grumbling.

Is this another Black August?

Exiled Russian commentator Ilya Varlamov posted his thoughts on that question this week, saying recurring historical disasters in August were “a coincidence, of course.”

A Wildberries emloyee looks at a plume of smoke rising during a fire near the town of Podolsk, outside Moscow on August 16. Ukraine has increasingly targeted warehouses the online retailer. Tatyana Makeyeva/AFP/Getty Images

But, Varlamov continued, “many Russians await August with apprehension. Especially now, when the country is truly in crisis. … The fuel crisis has returned, prices are rising and have no intention of stopping, the ruble is falling, elections are coming and God knows what else.”

Varlamov also noted the recently publicized remarks made by a top Russian economist, who warned that Moscow was facing a “social crisis” and “losing both the technological and economic competition globally” and would not win a war of attrition against a Ukraine backed by the West.

Even loyal, pro-Kremlin tabloid Moskovsky Komsomolets noted the traditional August anxieties in Russia, though it turned to astrology for guidance. “A lunar eclipse is set to occur this month; while not the most massive one, it will take place opposite Pluto – a planet associated with catastrophes,” the article read.

“This could trigger social shifts, political changes in relations with neighbors, and domestic unrest. Incidents of accidents, heightened anxiety, and breakdowns – including nervous disorders – may increase.”

The moon passes in front of the sun as it sets during a partial solar eclipse in Saint Petersburg on August 12. Olga Maltseva/AFP/Getty Images

But amid the uneasy speculation, Putin has projected his usual aura of confidence.

In remarks Wednesday on infrastructure and development projects, the Kremlin leader acknowledged the economic damage inflicted by Ukraine by strikes on the warehouses of e-commerce giant Wildberries, without naming the company – but downplayed their long-term impact.

“It goes without saying that these attacks will not have, do not cause and cannot bring about any critical consequences,” he said. “True, they do cause harm – this much is obvious, and we understand this, we see this, and we are aware of it.”

The Russian president said those logistics facilities would be built back with government support. But the war in Ukraine has been coming ever closer to home for many Russians, hitting them squarely in the pocketbooks.

Ukraine is also weathering domestic crisis in wartime. Earlier this week, recently ousted Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for wartime elections, presenting a fresh political challenge to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Whatever the merits of Fedorov’s arguments, the move potentially presents a fresh talking point to Putin, who has publicly and repeatedly cast doubt on Zelensky’s legitimacy as president.

Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks during a signing ceremony following his talks with Myanmar President at the Grand Kremlin Palace, in Moscow on August 18. Alexander Zemlianichenko/Pool/Getty Images

Therein lies the contrast.

Zelensky’s five-year term was originally expected to end in 2024, but elections in Ukraine have been postponed under martial law imposed following Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022. And the government reshuffles in Kyiv, as well as major anti-government protests, show that civil society and democratic processes are still alive and well in Ukraine.

The same can hardly be said for Russia. On Monday, a court in that country convicted opposition politician Lev Shlosberg to 11 years in prison for opposing the war in Ukraine Russia’s Supreme Court also barred Shlosberg’s party, Yabloko, from appearing on the ballot in upcoming parliamentary elections.

Russia’s domestic political opposition, then, has been effectively throttled since Putin launched his war on Ukraine. As the American author Ernest Hemingway would doubtless recognize, the stifling of civil society seemed to happen slowly, then all at once with the death of jailed opposition leader Alexey Navalny in February 2024. Navalny’s fatal journey to an Arctic prison colony also began on an August day in 2020, when he fell ill from nerve-agent poisoning on a return flight to Moscow from Siberia.

Coincidence or not, the month of August has been a punishing one for Russia.

World.title: Iranian women defy efforts by hardliners to enforce wearing of hijab
World.content:
A cultural faultline in Iran has re-emerged in recent months amid the turmoil of war and the revamping of the country’s hardline leadership: how and whether to enforce the wearing of the hijab by women.

At the height of the conflict with the United States this year, women without the headscarf were often seen at pro-government gatherings and in state media. The government and internal security forces had bigger issues to deal with.

In one video an unveiled woman carrying an Iranian flag said her husband was in the military, and that she was proud of him.

But in recent weeks, the clamor for restoring a hard line on what conservative clerics and politicians call “public nudity” has grown.

Many Iranian women are openly flouting the rule – and authorities seem wary of launching a crackdown, for now. The regime appears to have more pressing priorities – presenting the conflict with the United States as an existential struggle, managing the deep economic fall-out and reorganizing the security apparatus under the leadership of Mojtaba Khamenei.

Still, state media have been highlighting stories about cafes and other businesses being forced to close for failing to enforce rules on clothing. A CNN tally of articles in Iranian media at the end of last month found examples in half a dozen cities, including Tehran.

Four years ago, the protest movement “Woman Life Freedom” ignited after the death in police custody of Mahsa Amini, a young woman who had been detained on accusations she was improperly dressed. It was brutally suppressed.

Women hold up signs depicting the image of 22-year-old Mahsa Amini, who died while in the custody of Iranian authorities, during a demonstration denouncing her death by Iraqi and Iranian Kurds outside the UN offices in Arbil, the capital of Iraq’s autonomous Kurdistan region, on September 24, 2022. Safin Hamid/AFP/Getty Images

Amnesty International reported at the end of 2024 that the Iranian authorities were waging war on women and girls “through an increasingly violent crackdown on those defying draconian compulsory veiling laws.”

But the protests had lasting consequences. Despite the drumbeat of warnings and sporadic enforcement, there is widespread defiance of official regulations, especially among young Iranian women.

On July 19, at least seven cafes and restaurants in Tehran were closed down for not enforcing the mandatory hijab, according to human rights group HRANA. The group also compiled lists of social media accounts that have been blocked for defying public dress codes.

HRANA said authorities were using vague concepts such as “violation of norms,” “violation of modesty” and “failure to observe Islamic decency” in pursuing alleged offenders. But in one instance this month, it said a boutique was closed “due to unveiling,” without giving further details.

Young Iranian women walk along a sidewalk in downtown Tehran, Iran, on June 15. Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Getty Images

On Monday the Tehran Prosecutor’s office said it would take serious action against alleged “indecency” violations and offenses at certain cafes and restaurants in Tehran, as well as shops selling clothing deemed “unconventional” or inappropriate.

In the South Khorasan Province in eastern Iran, 10 cafes have been closed over alleged violations of “social norms and mandatory hijab rules,” the Mehr news agency reported, citing the province’s chief prosecutor.

The relentless state media campaign on the issue often cites prayer leaders who insist the hijab is part of Iranian cultural identity and that women should observe modesty.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari, who leads Friday prayers in Tehran, claimed there were organized efforts to promote “nudity” and that some people are paid to appear in public with “improper” dress.

There have been some high-profile cases. In June a popular Iranian singer, Parastoo Ahmadi, together with eight members of her band and production team, were sentenced in Qom to 74 lashes and banned from leaving the country for two years. Ahmadi had appeared with bare shoulders and uncovered hair at an event that she livestreamed on her YouTube channel in 2024.

The charges included “offending public decency through the production and publication of vulgar and immoral content on cyberspace platforms.”

Hardliners are stepping up pressure on the authorities. The editor of the journal Kayhan, Hossein Shariatmadari, wrote that enforcement is both a legal obligation and a religious duty for officials.

A television show – “Park Way” – produced for the Tehran Municipality has devoted several episodes to the issue of women’s dress, calling for action against those who flout approved dress codes. One said that “unconventional behaviors should not be exhibited by anyone in public places such as parks.”

Women have also been mobilized to demand the hijab be worn. At a small rally in Isfahan this week, one placard read: “Netanyahu: Unveiled women are our soldiers for free.”

Netanyahu is not on record as making that remark, but the slogan reflects a broader narrative promoted by Iranian hardliners, portraying women who do not wear the hijab as, at the very least, disloyal to their country.

A veiled pro-government supporter carrying an Iranian national flag arrives to take part in a ceremony commemorating the memory of Iran’s late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the Imam Khomeini Grand Mosque in downtown Tehran, Iran, on August 18. Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Getty Images

But there’s plenty of evidence that many Iranian women are not intimidated by official campaigns.

Social media videos have popped up showing young women on scooters wearing helmets, but no headscarves. The government is yet to fulfil a promise that women will be issued licenses to ride motorbikes.

The videos include convoys of young women on scooters riding through Tehran and other cities. One Instagram post features a group of women declaring: “We’re the motorcycle girls of Shiraz! Shiraz girls, let’s go!”

Another Instagram account posted video of about 20 female motorcyclists in the central city of Isfahan, describing it as “the biggest female motorcycle event in Isfahan.”

As with so many social and cultural issues in Iran, the wearing of the hijab seems to some a misplaced priority at a time of conflict and economic crisis.

That appears to include President Masoud Pezeshkian. Referring to an interview with a conservative cleric, he said: “The cleric mentioned hijab… Well, there are neighborhoods, there are mosques – go and work on it there! Can you really change people’s behavior through laws?”

Pezeshkian went on to say that his daughter sometimes disagreed with him.

“Does it mean I should force her?!” he asked.

“Changing behavior is a cultural matter; it’s about belief. You can’t create belief in people through force.”

Former MP Gholamali Jafarzadeh Imanabadi argued officials should focus on inflation and livelihoods instead of the hijab.

And an unofficial media outlet posted an article entitled: A Provocation to a War-Weary Public – What Is Behind the Return of Hijab Patrols and Business Closures?

Iranian authorities first began urging women to wear the hijab after the 1979 revolution. Before that, the monarchy had promoted a more secular and westernized image of women.

Article 638 of Iran’s Islamic Penal Code criminalizes women appearing in public without “Islamic hijab,” although it does not precisely define what that means. A much tougher law approved in 2024 would have introduced a broader system of escalating penalties and surveillance, but its implementation was halted following intervention by the Supreme National Security Council.

This has antagonized hardliners. One member of Iran’s parliament, Mohammad-Taqi Naqdali, said this week: “We see what the state of nudity and public vice is like in our midst…Israel and America cannot destroy us, but this decay that has plagued our religious culture and is spreading nudity in a disastrous and widespread manner in society will.”

But the regime is treading carefully – for now.

“They still don’t dare say anything to people on the street. Girls in Tehran are out and about wearing crop tops, shorts, and all kinds of clothes, and headscarves are practically no longer a thing,” one Tehran woman in her 60s told CNN by phone.

“I don’t think they can make these girls wear headscarves again. But then again, that’s also what we thought when the revolution happened. We never thought they would be able to force us to wear them, but in the end, they did.”

World.title: Iran in “full-scale” war, says president, as fresh US sanctions loom
World.content:
Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said the country is in a “full-scale war” and acknowledged the country’s economic difficulties as the US prepares to ramp up sanctions on it.

“We are apologetic that these problems exist, as we find ourselves in a full-scale economic, military, and security war,” Iranian state media IRNA reported Pezeshkian as saying on Sunday.

“As the government, we are seeking with all our being to steer inflation, public problems, people’s livelihoods, people’s jobs, people’s future, and people’s lives towards dignity and pride,” he added.

Iran, already drained by years of sanctions and grappling with the strains of war, is now facing another test as US President Donald Trump threatens to further squeeze its economy. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent earlier pledged economic measures that have “never been seen” against Tehran.

World.title: Kalumba alleges UPND plot to arrest him for treason as party, police deny knowledge
World.content:
Kalumba alleges UPND plot to arrest him for treason as party, police deny knowledge

Former home affairs minister Katele Kalumba says he has uncovered a scheme by United Party for National Development officials to have him arrested and charged with treason, an allegation both the ruling party and police say they know nothing about.

Kalumba told journalists that he had received information suggesting instructions had already been issued for his arrest, and that his name had been linked, alongside that of former intelligence chief Xavier Chungu, to claims of plotting a coup d’état. He dismissed the suggestion outright, saying it defied both logic and his own political history.

“It is extremely annoying that people want to accuse me and individuals like former intelligence chief Xavier Chungu of plotting a coup d’état,” Kalumba said. “My name has come up that we were trying to plot a coup, which to me is actually nonsense.”

He accused the current administration of running what he described as a witch-hunt aimed at silencing critical voices, and challenged law enforcement agencies to produce evidence for any claims that he had been involved in militia activity. He said investigators should be prepared to prove, rather than simply assert, that offensive weapons had been found or that anything untoward had taken place.

Kalumba pointed to his own record with the ruling party as evidence against the allegations, noting that he had previously supported UPND in Chienge and had contributed financially to the party. He said it was upsetting that his name and Chungu’s were now being associated with illegality after that history of support.

UPND media director Mark Simuuwe, when contacted for comment, said the party had no knowledge of any such plot. He said the investigation and apprehension of lawbreakers fell squarely within the mandate of law enforcement agencies rather than the party itself.

“As UPND, we are not aware of such an activity because, as you are aware, such undertakings are being conducted by law enforcement agencies and not the party,” Simuuwe said.

Zambia Police Service deputy public relations officer Chipo Kaitisha gave a similarly cautious response when asked about Kalumba’s claims, saying her office had no knowledge of any scheme to arrest or detain him, though she said she would look into the matter further.

“I am not aware of any plot to arrest Dr Kalumba. But I will find out,” Kaitisha said.

The allegation surfaces at a moment when concerns over the treatment of opposition and other political figures are already running high. Eleven people arrested in connection with a security operation at opposition leader Brian Mundubile’s Kabulonga residence face treason charges that carry no possibility of bail, while Mundubile and running mate Makebi Zulu remain at United Nations premises in Lusaka after being summoned for questioning rather than formally charged.

Against that backdrop, the Apostles Council of Churches in Zambia has urged government to extend a hand of reconciliation to achieve national unity and healing following the election. Separately, Apostle Zulu has warned that continued arrests and police summonses of opposition-linked figures risk deepening division rather than promoting the national healing political leaders say they want.

Kalumba’s allegation cannot currently be verified independently, and neither UPND nor police have confirmed any arrest plan or investigation targeting him. Whether the claim develops into a formal case, or fades as an unconfirmed rumour, will likely depend on whether either side produces evidence to support their respective positions in the days ahead.
